title: Backfill verbatim child-spawn preamble into ac-beadify + ac-plan-init conductor prompts
description:
Backfill the verbatim child-spawn preamble into ac-beadify + ac-plan-init child prompts.

discovered-from: ac-gcj.8 (refine r2, 2026-08-02)

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03)

- The rule is live: `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md`
  § "Child-spawn preamble" (heading at line 58) states the conductor includes the
  preamble block VERBATIM in every child delegation prompt, and that a pointer is NOT
  sufficient — evidence: 3 distinct children self-detached under pointer-only guidance.
  The verbatim block itself runs from ~line 72 to the end of that section.
- Both cited sites still carry pointer-only text at line 1:
  `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md:1` and
  `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md:1` —
  identical string, each tagged `<!-- net-growth-ok: ac-gcj.7 Pass C canon binding -->`.
- Mechanism is concrete: those two reference files ARE the child prompts —
  `skills/ac-beadify/SKILL.md:144` and `skills/ac-plan-init/SKILL.md` construct the spawn by
  using the reference file's content, substituting only `{ARTIFACTS_DIR}` / `{PLAN_PATH}`.
  So "backfill" = replace the pointer line at the top of each prompt with the verbatim block.
- **NO COMPLIANT EXEMPLAR EXISTS.** `grep -rn "ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT" skills/` returns exactly
  one hit: `delegation-contract.md` itself. No skill in the registry currently inlines the
  block, so the implementer copies from the canon file, not from a sibling skill.
- **This bead is a deliberate 2-of-9 pilot.** The same pointer-only line exists at NINE
  sites: `ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md`, `ac-beadify/references/validators.md`,
  `ac-hygiene/references/reviewers.md`, `ac-implement/references/engineer-prompt.md`,
  `ac-land/SKILL.md`, `ac-plan-clean/references/workflow.md`,
  `ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md`, `ac-plan-refine-external/references/workflow.md`,
  `ac-plan-refine-internal/references/workflow.md`. The other SEVEN are OUT OF SCOPE here
  and are NOT silently dropped: this bead pilots the mechanism on two skills; rolling it to
  the remaining seven is follow-on scope to be filed once the pilot's shape is proven
  (see AC below — filing that follow-up is part of this bead's done).
- `AGENT_NAME` caveat: `grep -n AGENT_NAME` over both SKILL.md files and both reference
  files returns nothing — ac-beadify validators and ac-plan-init explorers are plain Task
  spawns with no Agent Mail identity minted. The preamble's Agent Mail clause is already
  defensively worded ("CHECK whether you hold the tools — usually you do NOT"), so copying
  the block verbatim is a harmless no-op for these children. Copy it verbatim; do NOT trim.

## Work

Replace the pointer-only first line of `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md` and
`skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` with the verbatim preamble block from
`delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble, so every validator/explorer child receives
the environment contract in its own prompt rather than a pointer it must go read.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md` opens with the verbatim preamble block.
      Check: `grep -c "ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT (non-negotiable):" skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md`
      returns 1.
- [ ] `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` opens with the verbatim preamble block.
      Check: same grep against that path returns 1.
- [ ] The inlined text is byte-identical to the canon block (no paraphrase, no trimmed
      clause). Check: extract the block from
      `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble
      (strip the `> ` blockquote markers) and `diff` it against the inlined copy in each
      file — diff must be empty.
- [ ] Each inlined copy carries a `<!-- mirror: ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md
      § Child-spawn preamble -- edit there first -->` mark, per the SINGLE-HOME rule in
      `hooks/skill-edit-guard.py:61-66` (deliberate copies are mirror-marked).
      Check: `grep -c 'mirror:' <each file>` returns >= 1.
- [ ] `./lint.sh` exits 0 — specifically Check 14 (no-net-growth, `lint.sh:570-709`) stays
      green. Note: Check 14 is HARD and PER-FILE on `skills/**/SKILL.md` ONLY; both edited
      files live under `references/`, so Check 14 does not gate them. Verify rather than
      assume: `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. If a `net-growth-ok` stamp turns out
      to be needed, use `<!-- net-growth-ok: ac-08k child-spawn preamble backfill -->`.
- [ ] A follow-on bead is filed covering the remaining seven pointer-only sites (listed
      above), labelled `unrefined`, with `discovered-from: ac-08k`. Check:
      `br list --json --all --limit 0 | jq -r '.issues[] | select(.id != "ac-08k") | select((.description // "") | test("discovered-from: ac-08k")) | .id'`
      returns exactly one id. TWO guards are REQUIRED, neither decorative (both verified
      2026-08-03): (1) `// ""` — six live issues carry `description: null` and the
      unguarded form aborts with `jq: error: null (null) cannot be matched, as it is not a
      string`; (2) `select(.id != "ac-08k")` — this bead's own description contains the
      string `ac-08k`, so without that filter the check SELF-MATCHES and passes today,
      before any follow-on bead exists, and would keep passing forever if none were filed.

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md`
- `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md`
- Verification: `./lint.sh` (must exit 0) + the three greps above. There is no unit-test
  harness for skill prose; the greps and the byte-identity diff ARE the test.
- Seam note: the seam here is canon file <-> the two child prompts that must mirror it. The
  byte-identity diff is what goes RED if either side drifts alone — a presence-only grep on
  one side would not.

## Delivers

- `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md` + `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md`
  each carry the verbatim child-spawn preamble block, mirror-marked
- a follow-on bead covering the remaining seven pointer-only sites

## Consumes

- ac-gcj.8 -> the compliance VERDICT in `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md`
  that this bead acts on (ac-gcj.8 stated the non-compliance but did not act on it). CLOSED;
  a real `blocks` edge exists. NOTE: the § Child-spawn preamble section and its verbatim
  block are OLDER canon that predates ac-gcj.8 — they are not ac-gcj.8's deliverable. The
  block being copied is therefore already-present tree state (verified at
  `delegation-contract.md` line 58ff), not a promise from an upstream bead.

Both pilot child prompts now open with the verbatim child-spawn preamble, byte-identical to the canon block in ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md (extract + diff empty on both), each prefixed by the SINGLE-HOME mirror mark. Follow-on bead ac-syct filed for the remaining seven pointer-only sites (unrefined, discovered-from: ac-08k) — the guarded jq check returns exactly one id. lint.sh exits 0 (372 checks / 0 failures); Check 14 does not gate references/. Delivered: skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md, skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md, bead ac-syct. Commit 5963b7c.

title: bug: beads-closed-gate completeness scope is identity-lifetime, not batch — later ceremonies re-demand prior batches' progress files (--beads batch scope needed)
description:
Found live at RUN 20260719-185059-58770, wave-2 ceremony (second gate friction this run; first was ac-0wi). The completeness check's in-scope set is identity-lifetime — ALL beads assigned to the passed identities across the whole run — with no batch boundary. Every later ceremony in a run therefore re-demands per-bead entries for EARLIER batches' beads (already gate-validated and report-committed), forcing call-sites to accumulate every prior --progress file (5 files by wave 2 of this run). Also mislabels a TARGET_BEADS=1 wave as "multi-bead" because the N>1 conditional keys on in-scope-set size, not the current batch size.

Decision ac-x9a scoped the check to "the wave's progress.md" — the implementation is broader than the ratified spec. Fail-closed noise, workaround exists (pass all run files), so P2 not P1.

## Fix
Add an explicit batch scope: `--beads <id,id,...>` (the conductor KNOWS its batch set — explicit beats inference). When provided: completeness checks exactly those ids against the union of provided --progress files, and the N>1 conditional keys on that count. Open-bead check unchanged (still identity-wide — genuinely-open beads must block regardless of batch). Without --beads: current behavior (back-compat).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `--beads` accepted (comma-separated); completeness scope + N>1 conditional keyed to it.
- Live repro: wave-2-style call with --beads ac-mengto-distill-tt9.4 and ONLY the wave2 progress file → exit 0 despite prior-batch beads existing under the same identity.
- Without --beads: behavior identical to today (existing tests untouched and green).
- Tests L10 (batch-scoped pass) + L11 (batch-scoped fail names only in-batch missing id); full suite green.
- Both ac-loop SKILL.md gate call-sites updated to pass --beads with the batch's bead list.
close_reason: Fixed in a1a7e31 (--beads batch scope, tests 27/27); folded into wave-3 ceremony (bug-close fold)

title: bug: beads-closed-gate --progress single-file scope false-fails parallel waves — union coverage across repeated --progress flags needed
description:
Found live at RUN 20260719-185059-58770 wave ceremony, immediately after ac-514+a2ce4bd shipped. The completeness check scopes in-scope beads = ALL beads assigned to the passed identities (including beads closed in PRIOR batches this run, e.g. ac-bxg), but validates per-bead entries against ONE --progress file. A parallel wave whose children each write their own progress.md (the design invariant — children never share a progress file) therefore ALWAYS exit-1s: each child file is missing the sibling child's beads. Repro: gate1/gate2 outputs recorded in run transcript — gate1 missing ac-bxg, ac-f1i, ac-mengto-distill-tt9.3, ac-rjh (sibling + prior-batch beads) vs orphans1 progress.

## Fix (verified semantic)
Support REPEATED --progress flags; per-file: read that file's TARGET_BEADS + COMPLETED tally + Status-line checks as today; coverage check: the UNION of '### Bead <id>' entries across ALL provided files must cover the in-scope set. Keep identity-first (a2ce4bd). Add test L8: two child files whose union covers, each alone incomplete → exit 0; plus L9: union still missing one id → exit 1 naming only the truly-missing id.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated --progress accepted; single-file behavior unchanged (back-compat).
- Union coverage passes the live repro: --progress bugs/progress.md --progress orphans1/progress.md --progress orphans2/progress.md with identities TurquoiseHollow MistyDesert SilentElk → exit 0.
- beads-closed-gate.test.sh extended (L8, L9), full suite green.
- ac-loop SKILL.md gate call-site comment updated: parallel waves pass ALL child files in ONE call.

title: harness-sync --all --check runs 9m27s against a 180s hot-lane regen-timeout — check can never complete
description:
discovered-from: unknown (surfaced by /ac-human-session apply-verification, 2026-08-03)

`hot-lane-lint`'s Check 3 (projection regeneration test) runs
`harness-sync.sh --all --check` under a `timeout`/`gtimeout` cap that defaults to 180s. The
dry-run takes many minutes, so the cap fires every time and the check never produces a real
result — it always emits the `PROJ projections regen-timeout` WARN instead of the drift verdict
it exists to compute. The ac-hp0 lint hoist (which made lint fire once instead of per-target)
was only the first-order cost; the budget is structurally under-provisioned.

## Re-measured at refine (2026-08-03, HEAD a5ab150) — the filing's numbers were WRONG

Executed `bash ./harness-sync.sh --all --check` from the agent-compounds root, foreground,
wall-clocked:
    exit = 1 · wall = 567s (9m27s) · tail: "Done. changes=2 (dry-run)" +
    "DRIFT: projections out of sync — run harness-sync.sh to converge"

The filing recorded "12:30 wall, 21% CPU, exit 0, changes=0". Corrections:
- Wall is 567s, not 750s. Still 3.15x the 180s cap, so the core premise HOLDS — the check can
  never complete — but the number in the bead was stale and is now replaced.
- Exit is 1, not 0, and changes=2, not 0. The tree currently HAS real projection drift. Do not
  treat "converges cleanly" as a precondition for this bead.
- CPU% was not re-measured; the "21% CPU (I/O/subprocess-bound)" claim is dropped rather than
  carried forward unverified.
- The machine was under concurrent multi-agent load during the measurement, so 567s is a
  loaded-tree figure, not a floor.

## Mechanism (verified at refine, present-tree)

`infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint`, Check 3:
- `command -v timeout` and `command -v gtimeout` — BOTH present on this machine
  (`/opt/homebrew/bin/timeout`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/gtimeout`), so the cap really does bite; the
  unbounded fallback branch is not what runs here.
- The cap value is ALREADY PARAMETERISED: `"${REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS:-180}"`. Executed at refine:
  `grep -c 'REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS:-180' <hot-lane-lint>` returns 2 — the literal appears TWICE
  (the timeout invocation and the WARN message that reports the budget to the reader).
- Nothing anywhere in ~/Repos sets `REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS`, so 180 is what is in force.
- Check 3 is WARN-classified by explicit policy (a shared checkout carrying foreign WIP would
  otherwise flip the gate red on every in-flight edit). So a timeout does NOT fail the gate —
  the damage is a permanently uninformative WARN, not a red build.
- The consumer is the `dream` skill's Phase 3 mechanical stack-lint pass, not an interactive
  hot lane. A multi-minute budget inside a dream run is affordable; that is what makes option
  (a) cheap.

## RECOMMENDATION (refine's decidable answer — ONE option, this is a task not a decision)

Take option (a): raise the default to 900s. Rationale, now that the options are priced:
- (a) is a ONE-LINE default change to an already-parameterised value, in a WARN-classified
  check, whose only consumer is a batch ceremony. Measured need is 567s on a loaded tree; 900s
  gives ~1.6x headroom. Nothing new is built.
- (b) per-target incremental check with a rotating schedule needs new state (which target ran
  when), and trades whole-tree drift detection for a one-in-N sample — a worse signal for a
  check whose entire job is "are ALL projections in sync".
- (c) parallelising `sync_target` is a real change to a script whose stated invariants include
  "never clobber a real file" and "never touch foreign symlinks"; concurrency against a shared
  symlink tree is exactly where those invariants get violated. Not worth it to save minutes in
  a nightly.
Options (b) and (c) are recorded here as considered-and-declined. If the 900s budget later
proves insufficient, re-open with (c) — do not re-litigate now.

REFINE ROUND 2 CORRECTION — option (a) is NOT free, and the first draft of this
recommendation priced it wrong. The only scheduled consumer is the "Dream Cycle - Weekly" job
in `infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json`, whose whole-job `timeout` is **2400s**. At the current
180s cap the regen check is 7.5% of that budget; at 900s it is up to 37.5% (expected ~570s =
~24%). A 5x jump inside a fixed 6-phase job budget is a real cost the first draft never
checked. So option (a) must land as a PAIR:
  (a1) `REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS` default 180 -> 900 in hot-lane-lint, and
  (a2) "Dream Cycle - Weekly" job `timeout` 2400 -> 3600 in
       `infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json`, putting the regen check at 25.0% worst-case
       (900/3600) and 15.8% expected (567/3600) of the job — down from 37.5% / 23.6%
       against the current 2400s budget. (All four figures recomputed at refine round 3; an
       earlier draft mis-stated the post-fix worst case as ~16% by pasting the expected
       figure into both slots.)
3600 is precedented in the same file — the "Sofi - Pipeline Alignment" job already uses it
(verified at refine). Both files live in the SAME repo (the Repos root repo), so this is still
one commit. Landing (a1) without (a2) trades a never-completing check for a job that runs out
of budget before its later phases — strictly worse.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (refine round 1, structure lens): splitting this bead into a
`decision`-typed + `human-gate` bead. Round 2's structure lens independently adjudicated the
rejection SOUND — option (a) dominates (b) on coverage and (c) on risk-to-stated-invariants at
near-zero build cost, and the choice neither affects end-user experience nor profoundly changes
the development approach, so the design-decision gate does not fire. Recorded so the override
is visible rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The default budget is raised at BOTH call sites.
   `grep -c 'REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS:-900' <infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint>` returns 2 AND
   `grep -c 'REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS:-180' <same file>` returns 0.
   EXECUTED at refine on unfixed HEAD: 180-form returns 2, 900-form returns 0 — bites.
   SEAM: the two sites are the timeout invocation and the WARN message that reports the budget
   to a human. Changing only one leaves the message lying about the cap. The paired assertion
   above goes RED if EITHER site alone is changed — that is the seam-proof, and it is why this
   is one AC with two greps rather than two ACs.

1b. The consuming job's budget is raised in the SAME commit.
   `jq -r '.[] | select(.name=="Dream Cycle - Weekly") | .timeout' /Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json`
   returns 3600.
   EXECUTED at refine: returns 2400 — bites. Bite-proof confirmed by running the same jq shape
   against the "Sofi - Pipeline Alignment" job in the same file, which returns 3600.
   This AC and AC 1 are a pair: landing the raised cap without the raised job budget is
   strictly worse than doing nothing (see the round-2 correction above).

2. `hot-lane-lint` still parses and runs: `bash -n <infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint>`
   exits 0, and `hot-lane-lint --no-regen` completes (fast path, skips Check 3 entirely).
   EXECUTED at refine: `bash -n` exits 0, and `--no-regen` is a real flag. Note
   `grep -c '\-\-no-regen)' <file>` returns **2**, not 1 — the arg-parser case branch plus the
   "(skipped: --no-regen)" echo string. Refine's first draft asserted 1 and was wrong; if you
   want the parser branch alone, anchor it: `grep -c '^    --no-regen)' <file>`.

3. A full `hot-lane-lint` run no longer emits `regen-timeout`.
   UNRUNNABLE AT REVIEW SPEED — the run takes ~10 minutes. Labelled unrunnable deliberately.
   Verify it once at implement with a foreground run and paste the wall-clock + the Check 3
   section of the output into the close comment. Do NOT stamp this AC from the grep alone.
   Expect the check to then emit `regen-drift` rather than silence, because the tree currently
   has changes=2 (see the re-measurement above) — a `regen-drift` WARN is the CORRECT outcome
   of this bead, not a regression.

## ROUTING — this bead is filed on the wrong board (refine round 2, structure lens)

`beads-standards` § Where beads live: "a bead belongs in the repo whose code it changes; there
is no cross-repo dependency graph." Every file this bead touches
(`infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint`, `infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json`) belongs to the
**Repos root repo**, which has its own `.beads/` board (verified present at refine). This bead
sits on the agent-compounds board and changes nothing in agent-compounds.

Refine did NOT move it — creating a bead on another repo's board mid-run would leave an
orphaned ledger mutation in a repo this run does not own the commit for. Recorded as a routing
finding for the conductor / `ac-tidy`: re-file on the Repos-root board and close this one as
moved, with a cross-link. The bead is fully implementable as written in the meantime; the
implementer just works in the other repo (see the hazard below).

## HAZARD — this bead crosses a repo boundary

`infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint` belongs to the **Repos root repo**
(`git -C /Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/infrastructure rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns
`/Users/craigvanheerden/Repos`), NOT to agent-compounds. This bead is tracked on the
agent-compounds board but its only code change lands in a DIFFERENT repository. Per the fleet
rule, never commit across repo boundaries in one operation: commit the hot-lane-lint change in
the Repos root repo, on its own, and record the SHA in this bead's close comment. Nothing in
agent-compounds changes.

## Test Scope

No unit-test suite for `hot-lane-lint`; the script is its own guard.
- Job-budget anchor verified at refine:
  `jq -r '.[] | select(.name=="Dream Cycle - Weekly") | .timeout' /Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json` = 2400.
- Anchors verified present at refine (2026-08-03):
  `grep -c 'REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS:-180' /Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint` = 2 ·
  `grep -c 'Check 3: projection regeneration test' <same>` = 1 ·
  `grep -c '\-\-no-regen)' <same>` = 2 (parser branch + echo string).
- Syntax guard: `bash -n` on the edited file, exit 0.
- Fast functional guard: `hot-lane-lint --no-regen` completes.
- Slow functional guard: one full `hot-lane-lint` run (~10 min) at implement — declared
  UNRUNNABLE at review speed, must be executed once before close.
- agent-compounds is untouched, so `bash lint.sh` is not part of this bead's scope. (If the
  implementer touches agent-compounds anyway, that is scope creep — bounce it.)
- No browser/device/QA modality.

## Delivers

- config: infrastructure/tools/bin/hot-lane-lint — Check 3 regen budget default raised
  180s to 900s at both the timeout invocation and the WARN message (env override
  `REGEN_TIMEOUT_SECS` preserved)
- config: infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json — "Dream Cycle - Weekly" job timeout raised
  2400s to 3600s so the enlarged regen check stays a minority of the job budget
- decision: options (b) rotating per-target check and (c) parallelised sync_target recorded as
  considered-and-declined, with the pricing that declined them

## Consumes

- none

(ac-hp0 is closed and its lint hoist is already applied at HEAD; the filing's prose
"Consumes: ac-hp0 (applied)" is NOT a Consumes line — a Consumes line requires an open blocker
with a matching dep edge, and `br dep list ac-36wi` returns none. Recorded here as context.)

ROUTING FLAG (unchanged by this close, for ac-tidy / the conductor): this bead is tracked on the agent-compounds board but changes NOTHING in agent-compounds. Both files belong to the Repos ROOT repo, so the code landed there in its own pathspec-scoped commit e7db0bc4 (pushed; origin/master == local HEAD == e7db0bc4). agent-compounds working tree confirmed clean for lint.sh and skills/ — no cross-repo commit was made. Per beads-standards § Where beads live this bead should be re-filed on the Repos-root board and this one closed as moved with a cross-link; refine deliberately did not move it mid-run and neither did I.

Delivered:

- config: infrastructure/jobs/weekly.json — "Dream Cycle - Weekly" timeout 2400 -> 3600.
- decision: options (b) rotating per-target check and (c) parallelised sync_target stay considered-and-declined on the pricing already recorded in the bead; nothing was re-litigated.

Evidence:

AC 1b: jq '.[] | select(.name=="Dream Cycle - Weekly") | .timeout' = 3600 (was 2400); bite-proof shape re-run against "Sofi - Pipeline Alignment" = 3600; jq -e over the whole file confirms it still parses.
AC 2: bash -n on hot-lane-lint exits 0; hot-lane-lint --no-regen completes in 2.9s — 92 checks, 0 failures, 3 warnings, "Check 3 (skipped: --no-regen)". (Noting the refine correction: grep -c '^    --no-regen)' = 1 for the parser branch; the unanchored form returns 2.)
AC 3 (the unrunnable-at-review-speed one, executed once here in the foreground): full hot-lane-lint run, wall = 464s, exit = 0, "hot-lane-lint: 93 checks, 0 failures, 4 warnings". regen-timeout occurrences in the output: 0 (was the invariable outcome). Check 3 section verbatim:

    WARN: [regen-drift] neometa/software/agent-compounds/harness-sync.sh — regeneration test non-zero (exit 1): DRIFT: projections out of sync — run harness-sync.sh to converge — run harness-sync.sh to converge
That regen-drift WARN is the CORRECT post-fix outcome per the bead (the tree really does carry projection drift, changes=2 at refine) — the check now computes a verdict instead of timing out. 464s also lands under the old 567s measurement, so the 900s cap holds ~1.9x headroom on this run.

title: DECISION: registry-lint CI permanently red — Check 5 requires gitignored _plans/ (absent from every CI checkout)
description:
decision: How should lint.sh Check 5 treat _plans/, which AGENTS.md line 77 documents as deliberately untracked (.gitignored; public repo), so registry-lint.yml stops failing on every push?
options:
  a) Drop _plans from Check 5's hardcoded list (lint.sh:212) — simplest; loses local verification that the dir exists on the working machine
  b) Skip-if-gitignored: pass when '[ -e path ] || git check-ignore -q path' — preserves local presence check where the dir is tracked, CI-safe

title: doc: refresh 10_dcg.md false-positive section for dcg 0.6.7 (two modes fixed upstream; new redirect-truncation heuristic)
description:
Refresh the `## Known False-Positives — Sanctioned Workarounds` section in
`skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md` (added 2026-07-17, decision `ac-umq`) against dcg 0.6.7.

**REFINED 2026-08-03 — the 2026-07-19 filing's premise was only HALF right. Implement from
THIS text, not the original wording.** The original said "0.6.7 FIXES both documented modes";
a live probe re-run this run shows mode 1 survives in the shape agents actually hit.

## Evidence A — `dcg test` probe matrix (re-derivable; re-run it to confirm)

Verdicts from `dcg test "<cmd>"`, dcg 0.6.7, executed 2026-08-03T12:04:14Z. Every row is one
`dcg test` call and can be reproduced by anyone with dcg 0.6.7 on PATH:

| shape | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| prose quoting a destructive command, evaluated in isolation | ALLOWED |
| recursive delete of one's own `/tmp` session-scratch dir | ALLOWED |
| truncating redirect to a quoted variable path | BLOCKED |
| truncating redirect to an unquoted variable path | BLOCKED |
| heredoc into a truncating redirect at a variable path | BLOCKED |
| **append** redirect to a variable path | ALLOWED |
| `tee <var-path>` where the only redirect target is literal `/dev/null` | ALLOWED |
| `tee -a <var-path>` | ALLOWED |
| `tee <var-path>` fed by a heredoc | ALLOWED |
| truncating redirect to a LITERAL `/tmp` path | ALLOWED |
| recursive delete of a repo path (control) | BLOCKED |

## Evidence B — observed harness behavior (session observation, NOT derivable from Evidence A)

Labelled separately on purpose: this is a first-hand observation from RUN
20260803-113231-34132, not something the probe matrix above establishes. Three tool calls in
that run were rejected by the harness pre-execution guard even though the command they
*contained* is ALLOWED per Evidence A:

- a compound command line containing the literal `rm -rf /tmp/foo` **inside a quoted argument**
  (a `dcg test '…'` probe and a `br comments add "…"` body) → rejected, rule
  `core.filesystem:rm-rf-root-home` — note the cited rule is the ROOT/HOME rule, on a `/tmp` path.
- a compound command line containing a truncating-redirect example **inside a quoted argument**
  → rejected, rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path`.

Inference (state it as an inference in the doc, not as a proven internal mechanism): the
pre-execution guard evaluates the agent's whole command line, so a destructive or redirect
literal appearing merely as quoted text is matched as if it were an invocation. Whatever the
internal cause, the *observable* is stable and cost three turns this run.

## The three corrections this bead must land

1. **Mode 2 (session-scratch recursive delete) is cleanly FIXED — retire it.** Delete the entry
   and its workaround; note fixed-in-0.6.7.
2. **Mode 1 (prose merely quoting a destructive command) is NOT cleanly fixed — KEEP its
   workaround, and REFRAME its rationale.** Per Evidence A the isolated verdict is now ALLOWED;
   per Evidence B the literal still gets blocked when it rides along in a larger command line.
   So the existing workaround (write the body to a file and pass it by path —
   `br comments add <id> -f <file>`) stays; only the reason changes. The doc must say the
   defence is against the **pre-execution** scan of the whole command line, not against
   `dcg test`'s verdict on the isolated string. Corollary worth stating: probing dcg's own
   behavior requires assembling the literal from concatenated fragments, or running the probes
   from a script file, so the literal never appears on a command line.
3. **Document the live new mode `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path`.** It keys on
   **TRUNCATION**, not on path-dynamism — do NOT repeat the original filing's framing ("blocks
   shell redirects to dynamic/variable paths"), which is imprecise. Sanctioned workarounds, all
   verified ALLOWED in Evidence A: append (`>>`), `tee <path>` with a literal `/dev/null`
   redirect (the path becomes an argument, so there is no redirect operator to match), and
   fully-literal `/tmp` destinations. A literal redirect target is impossible to write in
   advance whenever the path carries a runtime discriminator, which is why `tee` is the
   general escape.

Keep the existing "never allowlist whole rules" warning (`dcg allow <rule-id>` is rule-granular,
not path-granular).

## KNOWN CONTRADICTION IN SIBLING CANON — do not inherit it

At HEAD, `skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md` says the rule "fires on a stdout
redirect — **truncating or appending**". Evidence A disproves the append half (append to a
variable path is ALLOWED). That file is owned by bead `ac-ji5`, which has NOT landed. **This
bead must write the truncation-only wording and must not copy the sibling's current phrasing.**
No dep edge is warranted — different files, no ordering cause; the two just have to agree once
both land. If `ac-ji5` lands first, match its corrected wording rather than re-deriving.

- doc: `skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md` — refreshed `## Known False-Positives — Sanctioned Workarounds`
- doc: `/Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/neometa/memory/auto/loop-retro-dcg-fail-closes-destructive-literals-in-command.md` — Recurrence 3 entry (see Landing steps)

## Consumes

## Landing steps beyond the doc edit (do not skip — SEPARATE REPO)

Evidence B is the **third** recorded occurrence of a class already tracked in the memory
substrate: `memory/auto/loop-retro-dcg-fail-closes-destructive-literals-in-command.md` carries
`recurrence: 2` (Recurrence 2 logged 2026-08-01). Folding Evidence B only into `10_dcg.md` would
scope it to one skill's lesson file and lose the fleet-wide signal.

Append a **Recurrence 3 (2026-08-03, RUN 20260803-113231-34132)** entry to that fact, bumping

`core.filesystem:rm-rf-root-home`** — the same quoted-argument-in-a-command-line shape also trips
`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path`. That broadening is the new information; the

## Notes for the implementer

The `guard-evasion` probe agent was given an isolated git worktree and told explicitly:
"NEVER touch the main checkout ... (read-only to you)". It nonetheless used **`git stash push`**
to park a probe. Stashes are a **repo-global** resource shared across all worktrees of the same
repository. A concurrent session popped that stash, materialising the planted code into the
main working tree at `scripts/curate-foods/lib/split-sql.ts`:

- `escalationToRelease?: string` added to `SplitSqlParams`
- an `escalationRelease` fragment emitting
  `UPDATE bca.curator_pending_escalations SET resolved_at = now() WHERE escalation_id = '${params.escalationToRelease}'`
- that fragment interpolated into the returned transaction

Two independent harms in ~14 lines: (a) it reinstates the **exact unaudited escalation-release
path** that commit `2ed92ddc` was written to delete, and (b) the interpolation is **not**
`requireValidUuid`-gated, unlike every other interpolation in that builder — a live SQL
injection into a privileged transaction.

It was undetectable by the repo's own defences: the structural guard test passes 3/3 with the
planted code present (that evasion is the subject of the sibling bead), and `pnpm type-check`
does not cover `scripts/**` (bd-jkqok).

A SECOND reviewer in the same run (`contracts`) independently ran `git checkout 79a94149 -- .`
against the shared tree, overwriting it with stale content, then repaired it with
`git show HEAD:<path>` + `git stash pop`. A THIRD (`security`) reported seeing a fully staged
revert of all six batch commits in the index mid-run.

## Why the existing doctrine did not prevent it

`ac-review`'s isolation discipline (SKILL.md § test-quality METHOD, and
`references/review-dimensions.md`) says: "All destructive probes run in a disposable worktree —
`git worktree add`, probe there, `git worktree remove --force`. To you, the shared tree is
read-only."

That is necessary but **not sufficient**. It does not name the repo-global escape hatches, and
an agent that believes it is inside an isolated worktree reasonably assumes every git operation
is also isolated. It is not:
- **`git stash` / `git stash pop`** — the stash stack is shared repo-wide.
- **`git checkout <ref> -- <path>`** — overwrites the working tree (dcg blocks this
  interactively, but not from every harness/agent).
- **`git add` / index writes** — the index is per-worktree, but a staged revert was still
  observed escaping.

Note this checkout already carries 17 stashes accumulated from prior sessions, so a stray
`git stash pop` picking up the wrong entry is a live, recurring hazard, not a one-off.

## Proposed fix (agent-compounds, `skills/ac-review/`)

1. **Name the banned operations explicitly** in the isolation-discipline block, not just the
   principle: *"`git stash`, `git stash pop`, and `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` are BANNED even
   inside a worktree — the stash stack is repo-global and checkout overwrites the shared tree.
   To park state, copy files to `/tmp`. To restore, `git show <ref>:<path> | tee <path>`."*
2. Add the same block to `_shared/delegation-contract.md` so every skill that spawns probing
   subagents inherits it, not just ac-review.
3. **Add a conductor post-panel tree check** to ac-review Phase 3: after the panel returns and
   BEFORE synthesis, run `git status --short` and diff any unexpected working-tree change
   against the reviewed range. A planted probe that escapes must be caught by the ceremony, not
   by luck. This run caught it only because two agents volunteered confessions in their reports.
4. Consider a dcg rule blocking `git stash` outright in agent sessions (this repo's own
   environment contract already bans it by prose — prose is not enforcement).

## Acceptance

- The banned-operations list appears in `ac-review/SKILL.md` and
  `_shared/delegation-contract.md`, grep-verifiable by the string `git stash`.
- ac-review Phase 3 contains a mandatory `git status --short` tree check with a documented
  action on non-empty unexpected output.
- A dry-run of ac-review on a trivial range shows the tree check executing.

AC3 (dry-run) satisfied by the guard's 12/12 executed proofs + green post-guard review runs

comments.author: craigvanheerden
comments.text:
SECOND INCIDENT, SAME SESSION, DIFFERENT AGENT, WORSE OUTCOME. Raising this from
"a reviewer leaked code" to "the shared checkout is actively unsafe under concurrency".

Incident 1 (this bead as filed): an ac-review guard-evasion reviewer ran `git stash push`
believing its worktree isolated it. The stash stack is repo-GLOBAL, a concurrent session
popped it, and a live unaudited `UPDATE ... SET resolved_at = now()` carrying an
UN-VALIDATED interpolation — a SQL injection — landed in the shared tree and survived ~40
minutes. Invisible to the guard test and to type-check. Caught only because two agents
confessed and the conductor ran `git status`.

Incident 2 (new, ~2h later, ac-implement batch 8): a DIFFERENT concurrent session ran
`git stash -u` and SWALLOWED an implementer's uncommitted verified work, including an
untracked file. It left a 17-file / 1346-deletion changeset existing ONLY in the working
tree — index blob equal to HEAD — i.e. ONE `git checkout` away from being unrecoverable.
The implementer recovered it, but reported "near-total loss of a verified bead".

So the same primitive caused, in one session: (a) hostile code injected into the shared
tree, and (b) near-destruction of another agent's completed work. Both directions.

WHY THE CURRENT INSTRUCTION IS NOT ENOUGH
The conductor DID ban `git stash` explicitly in the delegation prompts. It happened anyway,
twice, because the ban reached the conductors and not the NESTED agents they spawned. An
instruction that must survive two levels of delegation to be effective is not a control.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS, in order of strength:
  1. Make it impossible — a repo-local pre-command guard (dcg already intercepts Bash) that
     refuses `git stash` outright in this checkout. dcg is the natural home; it already
     blocks other destructive shapes.
  2. Fail loudly — the spawning ceremony verifies the tree after the panel returns
     (`git status --short` plus a diff of any security-relevant path against HEAD) rather
     than trusting agent self-reports. Incident 1 was found this way, by accident.
  3. Enumerate the banned escape hatches in the child-spawn preamble — `git stash`,
     `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`, `git restore` — because "work in a worktree" does NOT
     name them, and an agent that believes it is isolated will still reach for them.

The implementer's own lesson from incident 2 is worth adopting verbatim: "commit the INSTANT
ACs verify" is the sole protection under concurrency, not a style preference. It batched a
lint run before committing and nearly lost the bead for it.

Recommend: implement (1) as the real fix, (2) as the backstop, (3) as the cheap immediate
mitigation. Do not close this on (3) alone — that is the control that already failed twice.

title: Fix ac-land defaults conflict: 'leave local Supabase running' vs the loop-close CI dispatch's stack guard on self-hosted runners

Where -- if anywhere -- does the local-Supabase-stack <-> CI-guard collision still occur after bd-pwt44, and which repo owns the fix?

title: Add structured verification-verdict grammar to beads-standards + QA/review/close skills (machine-readable, greppable)
description:
Record QA/review/CI verification verdicts as structured, machine-readable, greppable data on beads (not prose comments) at each ceremony. Rationale: close-status alone is a weak label — a BCA bead closed green while its symptom survived; only the verdict chain shows it. - Grammar includes `discovered-from:<bead-id>` origin linkage for finding beads, with `unknown` a legal value (escape-depth metric counts only linked findings).
- Grammar states VERIFIERS write verdicts + linkage; implementers NEVER do (Goodhart guard) — made explicit in the spec.
- The canonical catch-stage vocabulary is ratified as a CLOSED set: `qa-finding`, `review-finding`, `hygiene-finding`, `ci-finding`, `prod-finding` (sentry normalized/aliased into `prod-finding`). NOTE: `ci-finding` + `prod-finding` are NEW (absent from the db today); `qa-finding`/`hygiene-finding` exist in the label table but are currently unused in this db; `review-finding` is in use.
- A LABEL-FREEZE paragraph is added to beads-standards: eval-load-bearing labels (`refined`, `human-gate`, the verdict grammar tokens, the catch-stage closed set) are versioned/stable — renamed only with a migration note.
- The verdict-write step is added to the writer skills: ac-qa-browser + ac-qa-device (QA_VALIDATION), ac-review (VERDICT), ac-batch-close (CI outcome).

## Test Scope
- doc: grep beads-standards SKILL.md for the VERDICT grammar block, `discovered-from:`, the closed catch-stage set, and the LABEL-FREEZE paragraph.
- doc: grep ac-qa-browser / ac-qa-device / ac-review / ac-batch-close for the verdict-write step.
- data: verdict comments are greppable via a stable prefix (e.g. `grep 'VERDICT:' .beads/issues.jsonl`).

## Delivers
- doc: skills/beads-standards/SKILL.md — verdict-grammar canon + catch-stage closed set + LABEL-FREEZE paragraph
- doc: skills/ac-qa-browser/SKILL.md, ac-qa-device/SKILL.md, ac-review/SKILL.md, ac-batch-close/SKILL.md — verdict-write step
- convention: structured-comment VERDICT grammar (consumed by ac-21z, ac-xqy, ac-qaw)

- none

## Approach (advisory)
Grammar sketch: `VERDICT: <outcome-verb>: <detail>` + `discovered-from: <bead-id|unknown>` on finding beads, mirroring `close_reason`'s `shipped:/fixed:/wontfix:` verbs so the same clustering tooling reads both. title: ac-batch-close Act 1 can report Tier 1 CI green with zero runs — make it assert, not assume
description:
Make `ac-batch-close` Act 1 **assert** its Tier 1 CI gate rather than assume it — so a batch
whose diff triggers no workflow can never be reported as "Tier 1 CI: green".

discovered-from: ac-tidy-tier2-gate-unsound-7ba
observed: 2026-08-03 · RUN 20260803-113231-34132

## REFINE DECISION (2026-08-03) — the fork is resolved; implement option (c)

Filed as an `investigation` with three options and "pick one". Refine resolved it and
**retyped this to `bug`**. Rationale, recorded so it is not re-litigated:

- **Type: `bug`.** `beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` § Types defines `bug` as a
  "CONFIRMED defect (root cause or solid repro in hand)" and adds: "**No confirm-ceremony
  beads.** If the finding stage already diagnosed it — **diagnosed = source-traced, not
  inferred** — file the `bug` directly. `investigation` is only for genuine unknowns, AND for
  any finding whose cause is a hunch." Both halves are satisfied: the root cause was read
  directly out of `registry-lint.yml`'s `paths:` filter and `ac-batch-close` Act 1's
  skip-silently branch, and the repro is solid (see Steps to Reproduce). Nothing here is a
  hunch, so the quarantined-guess rule does not apply and `investigation` is the wrong carrier.
- **Not `decision`.** That type is reserved for "a fork only the human can resolve (taste,
  product, money, risk)". This is none of those: it is a CI-mechanism engineering tradeoff with
  a stated objective criterion (blast radius), and the filing itself already argues (c) is
  widest. So **no `human-gate`** — a decision bead here would be the confirm ceremony the canon
  forbids.
- **Option (c) chosen.** It fixes the class in EVERY repo that lacks a `quality-gate.yml`, not
  just agent-compounds; (a) and (b) are repo-local and only mask this instance. (c) is
  strictly additive (it tightens a report, changes no user-facing behavior, commits to no new
  infra), which is why refine could resolve it rather than escalate.
- **(a) and (b) are NOT foreclosed** — they remain available as later complements to whoever
  owns agent-compounds' CI. They are simply not this bead's scope, and (c) does not depend on
  either. If a future run wants (a) or (b), file it separately; do not reopen this fork.

## Approach (advisory)

Rejected alternatives, kept for context only — do NOT implement:
(a) add a `quality-gate.yml` to agent-compounds with `workflow_dispatch` + `reason` +
`batch_anchor` inputs (most faithful to Act 1, most new infra, repo-local);
(b) drop `registry-lint.yml`'s `paths:` filter so every push to main is gated (simplest,
~15s per ledger-only commit, repo-local).

## Evidence (EXECUTED — the defect this bead closes)

`ac-batch-close` Act 1 specifies
`gh workflow run quality-gate.yml -f reason=batch-close -f batch_anchor="$ANCHOR"`.
agent-compounds has **no `quality-gate.yml`** — `.github/workflows/` holds `lint.yml` and
`registry-lint.yml` only. Act 1's documented escape hatch (skip silently on file absence,
note the gap) fired correctly for batch `ac-tidy-tier2-gate-unsound-7ba-20260803`, whose gate
was in fact satisfied by the push-triggered `registry-lint.yml` run for the batch head
(run 30807914994, `success`) plus the full local equivalent. **Nothing was ungated in that
batch** — this bead is about the next one.

The hazard: `registry-lint.yml` is path-filtered —

    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
        paths: ["skills/**", "hooks/**", "lint.sh", ".github/workflows/**"]

so a batch touching none of those paths (a docs/`templates/`/`.claude/`-only batch, or the
batch-close mark commit itself — verified: **no run was created for `5469877`**) produces
**zero CI runs**. A conductor taking the "skip silently" branch and then reporting "Tier 1 CI:
green" asserts a gate that never executed. Silent, and it reads clean — same species as
bd-kudrb.

## Delivers

- `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` § Act 1 — the silent-skip branch replaced by an assertion:
  the conductor may report "Tier 1 CI: green" ONLY on (i) a completed successful run whose
  head SHA is the batch anchor, or (ii) an explicitly recorded local-equivalent gate naming
  what was run. Neither present -> report "Tier 1 CI: NOT GATED (<reason>)" — never "green".
- `skills/ac-pipeline/references/verification-gate.md` — the same assert-don't-assume rule
  stated once as canon, with ac-batch-close binding to it (this is a cross-skill contract, so
  it belongs in the shared canon, not only in Act 1).

**What "a recorded local-equivalent gate" must mean (spec, so the implementer does not have to
ask).** It is a written line in the batch-close report naming, at minimum: (1) the exact
command(s) run — e.g. `./lint.sh` plus any touched proof scripts — (2) their exit codes, and
(3) the SHA they were run against. A local-equivalent gate that does not name all three is not
recorded and does not satisfy branch (ii). The precedent to copy is the
`ac-tidy-tier2-gate-unsound-7ba-20260803` batch, which recorded "`lint.sh` 314/0 + the three
touched proof scripts" — make that shape mandatory rather than incidental.

## Consumes

- none

No upstream blocker: both files exist at HEAD 878a6f1 and the change is local text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` § Act 1 no longer permits a silent skip.
   Check: `grep -n 'quality-gate.yml' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` — every hit sits inside
   a branch that, on file-absence, routes to the assertion (i)/(ii) above rather than to a
   bare "note the gap and continue". Read the surrounding branch, not just the grep hit.
2. The report vocabulary is enforceable, i.e. an explicit NOT-GATED outcome exists:
   `grep -c 'NOT GATED' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` >= 1. **RED now: 0** (executed
   2026-08-03 at HEAD 878a6f1).
3. `skills/ac-pipeline/references/verification-gate.md` carries the assert-don't-assume rule:
   `grep -c 'NOT GATED' skills/ac-pipeline/references/verification-gate.md` >= 1.
   **RED now: 0** (executed). *Do NOT use `grep -c 'verification-gate'
   skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` as the check — it already returns **2** at HEAD and is
   therefore vacuous; the binding exists, the rule does not.*
4. **Executable end-to-end check (this is the bite-proof — it must go RED before the fix).**
   Identify a commit on `main` touching ONLY paths outside
   `skills/**`/`hooks/**`/`lint.sh`/`.github/workflows/**` — `5469877` (a ledger-only
   batch-close mark commit) is such a commit, verified this round. Then:

       GH_DEBUG= gh run list --workflow registry-lint.yml --json headSha,conclusion --limit 100 \
         2>/dev/null | jq -r '[.[] | select(.headSha | startswith("5469877"))] | length'

   returns **0** — EXECUTED 2026-08-03, 0 of 100 runs match. (`GH_DEBUG=` and `2>/dev/null`
   are load-bearing: this shell exports a debug-tracing `gh` that otherwise prefixes non-JSON
   lines and makes `jq` exit 5 — a false "check errored", not a false green.) Walk Act 1
   against that SHA as the batch anchor and confirm the written procedure yields "NOT GATED",
   not "green". Before the fix the same walk yields "green" — that is the RED.
5. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the exit code ONLY, never the check
   count** (314 -> 372 within one hour on 2026-08-03).
6. Check 14 (per-file no-net-growth on `skills/**/SKILL.md`) gates
   `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md`. Expect to need an honest `<!-- net-growth-ok: ... -->`
   stamp or to fold the assertion into an existing bullet. Confirm with `git diff --numstat`.
   `verification-gate.md` is under `references/` and is NOT gated by Check 14.

## Steps to Reproduce

All four steps EXECUTED 2026-08-03 at HEAD 878a6f1.

1. `ls .github/workflows/` -> `lint.yml`, `registry-lint.yml`. **There is no
   `quality-gate.yml`** — the workflow `ac-batch-close` Act 1 dispatches by name.
2. Read `.github/workflows/registry-lint.yml`'s trigger: `on.push.paths` is
   `["skills/**", "hooks/**", "lint.sh", ".github/workflows/**"]`. A push touching none of
   those creates no run.
3. Take `5469877` — a real batch-close mark commit on `main`. Its diff touches only
   `.beads/`, `.beads/.br_history/` and `.claude/reviews/batch/` (executed:
   `git show --name-only --format='' 5469877 | sed 's|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u`) — **none** of
   which is in `registry-lint.yml`'s `paths:` list. Then:

       GH_DEBUG= gh run list --workflow registry-lint.yml --json headSha,conclusion --limit 100 \
         2>/dev/null | jq -r '[.[] | select(.headSha | startswith("5469877"))] | length'

   -> **0**. Zero CI runs exist for that commit.
4. Walk `ac-batch-close` Act 1 with `5469877` as the batch anchor. `quality-gate.yml` is absent,
   so the documented escape hatch fires: skip silently, note the gap, continue — and the
   conductor's report then says "Tier 1 CI: green" while **no gate executed at all**. That is
   the defect: silent, and it reads clean. Same species as bd-kudrb.

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` § Act 1 (the `quality-gate.yml` dispatch + the
  file-existence escape hatch) — grep-verified present at HEAD 878a6f1.
- `skills/ac-pipeline/references/verification-gate.md` — present at HEAD.
- `.github/workflows/registry-lint.yml` (the `paths:` filter, read this round),
  `.github/workflows/lint.yml` — READ-ONLY; option (b) is rejected, so neither is edited.
- No unit harness exists for markdown canon. `grep` + the AC-4 `gh run list` walk +
  `./lint.sh` ARE the verification surface. AC 4 requires network access to GitHub; if `gh` is
  unavailable, that AC is **unrunnable-here** and must be reported as such, not assumed green
  — which is precisely the failure mode this bead exists to close.

title: bug: verification-gate CLASS_RUNTIME silently under-fires — grep -qvE broken for multi-line ANY-match on macOS (ugrep/BSD)
description:
## Defect
`skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70` classifies "any runtime code touched" with:
```
printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -qvE '\.(md|mdx)$|\.test\.|\.spec\.|__tests__/|^\.github/|^docs/' && CLASS_RUNTIME=1
```
Combining `-q` (quiet, short-circuit) with `-v` (invert) does NOT yield ANY-non-matching-line semantics under the grep in use — `grep` here resolves to a **ugrep 7.5.0** shim (BSD-grep-like). `-qv` exits 0 only when EVERY line fails the pattern; on a mixed changeset it exits 1, so CLASS_RUNTIME stays 0 and the runtime verification gate SILENTLY skips — violating the "never silently skip / ambiguity counts as a match" invariant (same file, line 38).

## Empirical repro (verified live, RUN 20260719-185059-58770, 2026-07-19T16:53:03Z; artifact `/tmp/bead-work-refine-bxg-20260719-185059-58770/repro-ac-bxg.txt`)
```
P='\.(md|mdx)$|\.test\.|\.spec\.|__tests__/|^\.github/|^docs/'
printf 'a.ts\n'       | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 0  correct (runtime present)
printf 'x.md\n'       | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  correct (no runtime)
printf 'x.md\na.ts\n' | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  WRONG — a.ts is runtime, want 0
printf 'a.ts\nx.md\n' | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  WRONG — order-independent
```
Nearly every real changeset mixes runtime source with at least one .md/.test/.github/docs file → gate skips.

## Fix (target: `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70`, single line, single file)
Decouple `-q` from `-v`. Two forms, both verified correct under the failing shell (artifact above):
- **A (capture-and-test emptiness):**
  ```
  RT=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -vE '<pattern>')
  [ -n "$RT" ] && CLASS_RUNTIME=1
  ```
- **B (decouple pipe):** `printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -vE '<pattern>' | grep -q . && CLASS_RUNTIME=1`

Audit result: line 70 is the ONLY `-qv` (quiet+invert) combo in the file — the positive `-qE` matches on 54/55/58/59/61/64/67/178/179 are correct ANY-match semantics and need no change. Keep the existing fail-safe intent: ambiguous class errs toward runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md` contains NO `grep -qv`/`-qvE` (quiet+invert) combo. Check: `grep -nE 'grep -[A-Za-z]*q[A-Za-z]*v|grep -[A-Za-z]*v[A-Za-z]*q' skills/_shared/verification-gate.md` returns nothing.
2. A mixed changeset sets CLASS_RUNTIME=1. Check: run the file's Step-1 block with `FILES=$'x.md\na.ts'` → `CLASS_RUNTIME=1`. (Also `a.ts\nx.md` → 1, order-independent.)
3. A docs/test-only changeset keeps CLASS_RUNTIME=0. Check: `FILES=$'x.md\ndocs/z.md'` → `CLASS_RUNTIME=0`; `FILES='a.ts'` → 1.
4. Behavior holds under the machine grep. Check: run AC2/AC3 with `grep --version` = ugrep 7.5.0 shim (this env), exit codes as above.

## Delivers
- `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70` — CLASS_RUNTIME classifier that fires on ANY runtime file in a mixed fileset (decoupled `grep -v` existence test), restoring the never-silently-skip invariant for every app that runs the verification gate on macOS/ugrep.

## Consumes
- none (standalone shared-doc fix; no blocker bead)

## Provenance

Shared skill — fix affects every app running the verification gate.

title: Probe: does Grok's plugin adapter honor additionalContext (recall-hook push channel)
description:
## Open question
Grok Build discards passive-event hook stdout from USER hook files (empirically verified 2026-07-12, v0.2.93) — including Claude's `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` JSON form. This closed the push-recall channel on Grok, which the shipped plan compensated for with the static memory digest (render_context_grok) + qmd MCP pull. OPEN: does Grok's *plugin* adapter (Claude-format plugin packaging) honor `additionalContext` even though user hook files do not? A commercial memory plugin (Vectorize Hindsight) bets it does. If true, push-recall could be restored on Grok at the canon level, closing the one remaining injection gap.

## Approach (advisory)
Package the existing recall hook as a Claude-format plugin and load it into a Grok session; emit a known marker via additionalContext; check whether the model can see it (same execution-proof method used in the original 2026-07-12 experiments — filesystem marker confirms the hook ran, model-visibility is the actual test). ~1h. Recall hook source: Repos/.claude/hooks/memory-retrieval.py. Grok context surface it would supplement: ~/.grok/AGENTS.md (generated by render_context_grok in agent-compounds/harness-sync.sh).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented yes/no answer, with execution proof, on whether Grok's plugin adapter surfaces additionalContext to the model (check: recorded test transcript + filesystem-marker proof the hook executed).
- If YES: a follow-up implementer bead is spawned (discovered-from this one) to wire plugin-channel push-recall into the hook canon; if NO: the finding is recorded and this bead closes documented-and-closed.

## Test Scope
Investigation/spike — no app runtime surface. Manual Grok-session probe against Repos/.claude/hooks/memory-retrieval.py; no automated tests. Files consulted (read-only): Repos/.claude/hooks/memory-retrieval.py, neometa/software/agent-compounds/harness-sync.sh (render_context_grok).

## Delivers
- decision: recorded answer (yes/no + evidence) on Grok plugin-adapter additionalContext support, plus any spawned follow-up implementer bead.

## Consumes
- none
close_reason: Investigation complete. FINDING: NO — Grok 0.2.93 plugin adapter does not honor additionalContext; it never executes plugin-packaged hooks (discovery advertises has_hooks=true but dispatcher loads only settings-file hooks; execution-proof: FS marker never written + --debug-file trace). Per-type close evidence: findings comment above with recorded transcript results + filesystem-marker proof; no follow-up fix bead spawned (NO branch of AC). Push-recall stays closed on Grok; static-digest + qmd-MCP compensation remains correct.

comments.text:
FINDING (execution-proof, Grok Build 0.2.93, grok-4.5): NO — the plugin adapter does NOT honor additionalContext, because it never EXECUTES plugin-packaged hooks at all. The gap sits one layer below additionalContext: the plugin hook never fires.

METHOD: Built a valid Claude-format plugin (d29-probe: .claude-plugin/plugin.json + hooks/hooks.json registering SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit 'command' hooks). Each hook (a) appends an FS execution marker and (b) emits hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext carrying a unique passphrase (BANANA_HELICOPTER_7XQ). `grok plugin validate` passed; `grok plugin install --trust` succeeded; `grok inspect` listed the plugin enabled with hooks. Probed headless: `grok -p '<ask for passphrase>' --output-format json`.

RESULTS:
- Run 1 (live config, [compat.claude] hooks=false): model=NO_MARKER_FOUND; FS marker NOT written. Under the shipped config, Claude-format hooks (incl. plugin) are globally gated OFF — inspect shows 'claude -> hooks OFF (config)'.
- Run 2+3 (flipped [compat.claude] hooks=true in a backed-up config; restored after, md5-verified identical): model STILL NO_MARKER_FOUND; FS marker STILL NOT written. --debug-file trace is decisive:
  * Plugin discovery DID see it: 'plugin discovered name=d29-probe ... has_hooks=true' (xai_grok_agent::plugins::discovery).
  * But the hook DISPATCHER loaded only settings-file hooks: 'xai_grok_hooks::discovery: hooks: discovery complete total_hooks=12' — every one prefixed global/settings:*. Plugin-hook contribution = 0. Every dispatched hook was global/settings:session_start/user_prompt_submit/stop — my plugin's sessionstart.sh/userprompt.sh are never referenced.

MECHANISM: In 0.2.93 the plugin discovery subsystem and the hook dispatcher (xai_grok_hooks) are NOT bridged — plugins advertise has_hooks=true but their hooks.json is never wired into the execution path. README line 2226 ('hooks discovered and used by Grok at runtime') overstates: discovered yes, executed no.

IMPLICATION: The Vectorize Hindsight bet (plugin-packaged hooks reopen the push-recall channel on Grok) does NOT hold on Grok Build 0.2.93. The one remaining injection gap cannot be closed via the plugin adapter. Shipped compensation stands correct: static digest (render_context_grok in harness-sync.sh) + qmd MCP pull. No follow-up implementer bead spawned (per AC: NO -> documented-and-closed). Re-probe when the companion xAI-changelog watch item fires (Grok hook/plugin subsystem changes).

SAFETY: machine-local only; config backed up + restored (md5 identical, hooks=false); probe plugin uninstalled; installed-plugins/ empty; /tmp probe residue removed. Zero residue.

The conductor hit the same rule independently at run start, and once more when this bead's own original description quoted the offending construct verbatim — 3 trips, same class, same fix.

**PREMISE CORRECTED at refine round 1 (2026-08-03, dcg 0.6.7, every shape empirically probed with `dcg test`):**

- The original description blamed a truncating write into the `$STATE` variable path. **That is WRONG.** `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md:207` APPENDS to `$STATE`, and `dcg test` rules that shape **ALLOWED** (exit 0). No fix is needed there.

- The bead's original proposed fix (print-the-computed-dir-then-paste-a-literal) is **SUPERSEDED**: the pipe-into-`tee` shape is the sanctioned replacement (`skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md` § Sanctioned shapes) because `tee` takes its destination as an argument, so there is no redirect operator to match. - `:229` already carries an inline warning comment pointing at `shell-guardrails.md` (added by an earlier partial fix) but the SHAPE was never converted — so it still blocks verbatim, and the comment can mislead a fixer into believing the line is handled. `:230` and `:231` carry no comment at all.

Title also corrected: the snippet is `### Gather Batch Context`, not the run-ledger.

## Delivers

- doc: `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md:229-231` — the three `Gather Batch Context` writes converted to the dcg-sanctioned `tee` shape, and the stale inline warning comment on :229 dropped (the shape now demonstrates the guidance instead of apologising for it)

## Consumes

## Approach (advisory)

Replace each of the three writes with the pipe-into-`tee` form, destination as an argument, discarding stdout to the fully-literal `/dev/null`. `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` § dcg-safe writes contains a worked in-repo example of exactly this conversion.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every command below was EXECUTED against HEAD on 2026-08-03; the RED-now results are measured, not assumed.

1. No truncating stdout redirect into a variable-built path remains in the file.
   Check: `grep -cE '[^>]> *"?\$' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns `0`.
   RED now: returns `3` — lines 229, 230, 231 (executed 2026-08-03). This grep is itself dcg-safe: it was executed successfully on 2026-08-03 and was not blocked.
2. **Positive confirmation — the three writes still EXIST, converted rather than deleted.** AC 1 alone can be satisfied vacuously by deleting :229-231, which would silently break the `Gather Batch Context` feed into the Act 3 batch-close report.
   Check (one line; the section-scoping and the comment filter are both load-bearing):
   `sed -n '/^### Gather Batch Context/,/^## /p' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md | grep -v '<!--' | grep -cE '\| *tee (-a )?"?\$\{?ARTIFACTS_DIR\}?"?/(beads\.json|commits\.txt|diff-stats\.txt)'` returns `3`.
   RED now: returns `0` (executed 2026-08-03).
   **Calibration — this exact check was arrived at by discarding two weaker drafts, both caught by bite-proofs:**
   - *Too tight* (rejected round 3): `tee "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/` alone returns 0 for `tee -a "…"`, `tee $ARTIFACTS_DIR/…`, `tee "${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/…"` and `tee "$ARTIFACTS_DIR"/…` — all dcg-ALLOWED, and `tee -a` is explicitly sanctioned at `skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md:38`. It would FAIL a correct fix.
   - *Too loose* (rejected round 4): an unanchored file-wide text match passes when :229-231 are DELETED and replaced by an HTML comment that still names `tee` and the three filenames — a realistic mid-edit accident that reproduces the very vacuous-pass this AC exists to close. Hence the leading pipe anchor, the `### Gather Batch Context` section scope, and the `<!--` filter.
   **Bite-proof executed 2026-08-03** against four constructed file states: HEAD -> `0`; a faithful fix using three DIFFERENT valid shapes (`tee -a "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/…"`, `tee ${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/…`, `tee "$ARTIFACTS_DIR"/…`) -> `3`; the comment-out deletion -> `0`; `tee` to literal `/tmp` destinations instead of `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` -> `0`. There is no pre-existing `tee` write to `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` in this file, so over-match risk is nil.
3. Each replacement line is confirmed ALLOWED by the guard, not merely assumed. For each converted line: copy its text into a literal `/tmp` file with the Write tool, then run `dcg test "$(cat /tmp/<file>)"` capturing output to a literal `/tmp` path; assert exit 0 / `Result: ALLOWED`. **Never inline the candidate text in the bash command** — dcg's parse is positional, so a command that merely QUOTES the construct is blocked (this is what cost the third of the three original trips, and it also blocked two probe attempts during this refine round).

5. `./lint.sh` stays green. Measured at HEAD 2026-08-03: `lint: 314 checks, 0 failures`.
6. No QA modality — doc-canon only, no user-facing surface.

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` (anchors :207 append-ALLOWED, :220-223 ARTIFACTS_DIR/STATE derivation, :229-231 the three blocked writes — all verified present at HEAD 2026-08-03)
- `dcg test` (dcg 0.6.7, `which dcg` → `/Users/craigvanheerden/.local/bin/dcg`) — the executable guard oracle for AC 2; run per-line, never on a compound command
- `skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md` — the sanctioned-shapes table the fix must conform to; read-only for this bead

- No test files: markdown canon plus the `dcg test` oracle is the whole verification surface.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From the agent-compounds repo root, run `sed -n '/^### Gather Batch Context/,/^## /p' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` — three writes whose destination path is built from `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` (:229 beads.json, :230 commits.txt, :231 diff-stats.txt).

Result: exit 1, `Result: BLOCKED`, rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path`. Repeat for the other two — all three block.
3. **Do NOT paste the line directly into a bash command to test it.** dcg's parse is positional, so a command that merely QUOTES the construct is itself blocked. That mistake accounts for one of the three originally-measured trips and two more during refine.
4. Control, showing the fix direction: put `br list --json | tee "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/beads.json" >/dev/null` in a literal `/tmp` file and `dcg test` it — exit 0, `Result: ALLOWED`. Same for `tee -a`, bare and braced variable forms.
5. Control, showing the ORIGINAL premise was wrong: `dcg test` the `$STATE` append at :207 — exit 0, `Result: ALLOWED`. Measured against dcg 0.6.7 on 2026-08-03.

title: Bare tr silently no-ops under the tr->tmux zsh alias — use command tr in agent-pasted skill snippets (8 invocations / 7 lines, 4 files)
description:
discovered-from: ac-ji5 (surfaced during ac-bead-refine RUN 20260803-113231-34132, child FuchsiaWolfRefineD — the hazard broke this run's OWN Phase-0 CHILD_ID formula before it broke anything else)

Filed by ac-bead-refine as Exhaust-Rule capture (outside that run's `TARGET_BEAD_IDS`), then REFINED later the same day by RUN `20260803-113231-34132` child FuchsiaWolfRefineE — 3 reviewers x 4 rounds. See the `refine-corrections:` comment for what changed.

`tr` is an **alias for `tmux new-session -A -s repos -c ~/Repos`** in this user's interactive zsh profile. Any skill snippet an agent pastes into its Bash tool that uses bare `tr` therefore does not run `tr` at all: it prints `open terminal failed: not a terminal`, exits non-zero, and — because the failure is inside a `$( )` — **silently yields an empty string** rather than stopping. Measured live this run: `ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md:65`'s `CHILD_ID="$(printf '%s' "${AGENT_NAME:-anon}" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9')-$$"` produced `CHILD_ID="-13351"`, collapsing the per-child artifacts directory to an anonymous `/tmp/bead-refine--<pid>-<run-id>`. Four such orphaned directories from sibling children are on disk right now — i.e. the bd-baudw per-child-key safety was silently degraded for every child of this run. Re-reproduced 2026-08-03 by the refine child that wrote this correction: a `printf '%s\n' $LIST | grep ... | tr '\n' ' '` pipeline printed `open terminal failed: not a terminal` and produced no output.

**In-repo precedent for the fix already exists and should be cited, not re-litigated:** `skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md:193` carries the inline comment ``NOT `| tr -d ' '` — `tr` is a tmux alias in the fleet's interactive profile``, and `skills/context-engineering/workflows/context-mining-daily.md:83` already uses `command tr`. This bead simply finishes the sweep.

## The safe/broken split (EXECUTED, not assumed — it is what scopes this bead)

A zsh alias expands only in an **interactive** shell. Verified this run: bare `tr` pasted directly into the Bash tool fails (`open terminal failed`, exit 1); the identical bare `tr` inside a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script run via `bash script.sh` or `./script.sh` prints correctly and exits 0; `command tr` pasted directly works.

- **BROKEN (in scope):** bare `tr` inside a fenced snippet a skill hands an agent to paste.
- **SAFE (explicitly out of scope):** bare `tr` inside a committed shebang'd `.sh` script, including `lint.sh` — never touch these; the churn buys nothing.
- **Out of scope, dead prose (2 lines, BOTH must survive AC 1):**
  - `skills/ac-pipeline/references/run-id.md:20` — quotes `tr` inside a description of a retired convention, not an executable instruction.
  - `skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md:193` — a comment that quotes ``| tr -d ' '`` as the thing NOT to do. Rewriting it to `command tr` would destroy the warning.

## Delivers

- `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` — bare `tr` -> `command tr` at the CHILD_ID formula (`:65`), the `TARGET_BEAD_IDS` comma-split (`:168`, **two** invocations on one line), the SCOPE echo (`:238`), and the snapshot-integrity WARN (`:677`) — 5 invocations on 4 lines
- `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` — the identical CHILD_ID formula (`:216`); its own comment cites `ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` as its source, so the defect propagated between skills
- `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` — the Act-3 FATAL's `ls -1 … | tr '\n' ' '` (`:542`)
- `skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md` — the Mechanics block's `| tr -d '()'` (**`:179`** — the filing said `:178`; corrected by re-grep at HEAD 878a6f1)

**Totals, so the title and the ACs agree: 8 invocations across 7 lines in 4 files.** (The filing's title said "7 invocations" — it was counting lines. `workflow.md:168` carries two.)

title: ac-bead-refine parity gate: echo "$row" corrupts br JSON under zsh (34 open beads -> 4 survive)
description:
The Title/Label Parity Gate in `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md`
(grep-target: the `### Title/Label Parity Gate` heading and the fenced bash block
immediately under it — at 8fc9e36 that is lines 629-649, but ANCHOR ON THE GREP, not the
line number) streams `br list --json` rows through a `while read` loop and re-parses each
row with `echo "$row" | jq -r`.

**Corrected premise (refine 2026-08-03, executed against 8fc9e36 under zsh — the original
filing blamed both halves; only one is a corrupter):**

1. `echo "$row"` — **THIS IS THE DEFECT.** Under zsh, `echo` interprets backslash escapes,
   so the `\n` inside br's JSON string values is expanded and the row is no longer valid
   JSON. Measured on this board: 34 open beads in, **4 survive** the re-parse — 30 dropped
   with `jq: Invalid string: control characters`. Silent under bash, corrupting under zsh
   (the fleet's default shell). Replacing `echo` with `printf '%s'` restores 34/34.
2. `jq -c '…' | while IFS= read -r row` — **NOT itself corrupting.** Executed: `jq -c`
   emits one line per row with `\n` correctly escaped inside the JSON string, and row/record
   correspondence is preserved (34 in → 34 out when the body uses `printf '%s'`). It is a
   redundant per-row re-parse and a latent hazard (it is the shape line 169 of this same file
   warns about for `jq -c '.[0]'`), so the fix removes it — but do NOT claim it as the cause.

Fix shape: replace the whole loop with ONE single-pass `jq -r` that emits the ids directly,
e.g. `jq -r '.issues[] | select(.status=="open") | select(<gate predicate>) | .id'`, with no
per-row re-parse and no `echo`. Verified to emit 34/34. If a per-row loop must survive for
some other reason, `printf '%s'` replaces `echo` (also verified 34/34).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `cd` to this repo (its board has multi-line-description beads).
2. Build a snapshot: `br list --json --all --limit 0 > /tmp/snap.json`
   (NOTE: `br list --json --id X` does NOT filter — jq over the full board instead.)
3. Under zsh, run:
   `jq -c '.issues[]|select(.status=="open")' /tmp/snap.json | while IFS= read -r row; do echo "$row" | jq -r '.id'; done | grep -c .`
4. Compare with `jq -r '.issues[]|select(.status=="open")|.id' /tmp/snap.json | grep -c .`
   Observed 2026-08-03: **4 vs 34**.

## Acceptance Criteria
All three EXECUTED at draft on 8fc9e36; baselines are the pre-fix numbers.

- **AC1 (bite-proof, baseline 2 → must be 0):**
  `grep -c 'echo "\$row"' skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md`
  returns `2` at 8fc9e36 and MUST return `0` after the fix.
- **AC2 (bite-proof, baseline 2 → must be exactly 1):**
  `grep -c 'jq -c' skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md`
  returns `2` at 8fc9e36 — line 169 (legitimate PROSE: "multi-line descriptions break
  `jq -c '.[0]'`") and line 639 (the offending command). After the fix it MUST return
  **exactly 1**, and `grep -n 'jq -c' <file>` must show that the single survivor is the
  prose mention, NOT a command. (Do not write a line-range-scoped grep — it is not
  directly runnable; this count assertion is the runnable equivalent.)
- **AC3 (bite-proof via an INJECTED fixture — NOT a live-board equality check).**
  Refine drafted a live-board equality AC and EXECUTED it: the gate predicate matches
  **0** beads on this board, so `0 == 0` is vacuous and cannot detect the bug. Use an
  injected snapshot instead:

      # one synthetic decision bead with a MULTI-LINE description and no human-gate
      br list --json --all --limit 0 > /tmp/snap.json
      jq '.issues += [{"id":"zz-synth.1","status":"open","issue_type":"decision",
          "title":"DECISION: synthetic parity probe","labels":["tooling"],
          "description":"line one\nline two\nline three"}]' /tmp/snap.json > /tmp/inject.json
      # the replacement snippet, run against /tmp/inject.json, MUST emit exactly 1 id: zz-synth.1

  Executed at 8fc9e36: the **current** `echo "$row"` shape finds **0** on this fixture
  (RED — it drops the very bead the gate exists to catch); a single-pass `jq -r` finds
  **1** (GREEN). Paste both runs in the close reason.
- **AC3b (no-drop, separate check — do not merge with AC3).** On the plain `.id`
  projection over the unmodified snapshot, the replacement must emit the SAME count as
  `jq -r '.issues[]|select(.status=="open")|.id' | grep -c .` (34 at 8fc9e36; use the
  then-current number, the point is equality, not the literal 34). This is a different
  query from AC3's filtered one — they cannot be satisfied by a single command.
- **AC4:** `bash lint.sh` exits 0. Measured at draft: exit 0, 372 checks, 0 failures, ~16s.

## Test Scope
- `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` § Title/Label Parity Gate — manual execution

- `bash lint.sh` — VERIFIED at draft: exit 0, "lint: 372 checks, 0 failures", ~16s.
