title: ac-loop claim-at-selection omits TARGET_BEADS header — beads-closed-gate skips its completeness check
description:
`skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh` (grep-targets: the
`# Phase 1e — header \`TARGET_BEADS={N}\`` comment and the
`check_progress_completeness()` function — at 8fc9e36 lines 57 and 130-200) parses a
`TARGET_BEADS={N}` header out of each `progress.md` to run its completeness-union check.

`skills/ac-loop/references/delegation-prompts.md` DOES instruct spawned children to write
`TARGET_BEADS=N` (grep-target: `TARGET_BEADS=N.` in that file — line 38 at 8fc9e36).

**BUT BOTH of ac-loop's own CLAIM-AT-SELECTION steps omit it** (corrected scope, refine
2026-08-03 — the original filing named only the Phase-2 step, and cited a stale line):
- **Phase 1** (orphan/bug-lane drain) — grep-target
  `**Claim the batch (loop's job, before any implementation — CLAIM-AT-SELECTION)**`,
  line **350** at 8fc9e36. Mandates minting the claim id, writing `.claim-id`, and
  mirroring it "as the first line of `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/progress.md`'s header". No `TARGET_BEADS`.
- **Phase 2** (wave batch) — grep-target
  `**Claim the batch (loop's job — CLAIM-AT-SELECTION)**`, line **477** at 8fc9e36
  (the filing said 469 — stale, `### Execute the wave` is at 475). Mandates writing the
  claim id "to `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/.claim-id` + the `progress.md` header". No `TARGET_BEADS`.

Result: a conductor-authored batch `progress.md` reaches the gate without the header and
the completeness check WARNs and returns 0.

**Corrected premise — severity is HIGHER than filed (executed at draft, 8fc9e36).** The
filing said the run "was covered only because `--beads` happened to supply the bead set
explicitly." **That is false.** `check_progress_completeness()` short-circuits on
`[ "$valid_files" -eq 0 ] && return 0` BEFORE the union-coverage check, so a missing header
voids the check *regardless of `--beads`*. Proven:

    # fixture: progress.md with NO TARGET_BEADS header, genuinely INCOMPLETE
    # (declares fake-1 only), --beads names BOTH fake-1 and fake-2
    $ bash skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh --allow-empty \
        --progress /tmp/no-header-short.md --beads fake-1,fake-2 NoSuchAgentZZZ
    beads-closed-gate: WARNING — no 'TARGET_BEADS=' header ...; skipping it in the completeness union.
    []
    EXIT=0            # <-- should have been 1

    # same content WITH `TARGET_BEADS=2` added:
    beads-closed-gate: PROGRESS-INCOMPLETE — ... no '### Bead <id>' result entry ...: fake-2
    EXIT=1            # <-- the check has teeth once the header exists

So that batch was **not** covered at all. This is the same defect class as
ac-batch-close-ci-gate-vacuous-adbq (a gate silently downgrading to a no-op), fixed
earlier in the same run.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Write `/tmp/no-header-short.md` with a claim-id header, `### Bead fake-1` + `- Status:`,
   `COMPLETED: 1 / 2`, and NO `TARGET_BEADS=` line.
2. `bash skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh --allow-empty --progress /tmp/no-header-short.md --beads fake-1,fake-2 NoSuchAgentZZZ; echo EXIT=$?`
3. Observe WARNING + `EXIT=0`. Add `TARGET_BEADS=2` as line 3 and re-run → `EXIT=1`.

## Acceptance Criteria
Executed at draft on 8fc9e36 unless marked.

- **AC1 (prose side, bite-proof).** Both claim-at-selection steps must name
  `TARGET_BEADS=<count>` as a header field the claim step writes, alongside the claim id.
  Baseline at 8fc9e36: `grep -n 'TARGET_BEADS' skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md` returns **5** hits,
  at lines **374, 480, 722, 724, 784** — ALL of them per-child-parallelism mentions, NONE
  inside either claim step. (The filing's "three mentions at 366/714/776" was stale — do not
  use it.) A total-count assertion is NOT sufficient: refine drafted an
  `awk '/CLAIM-AT-SELECTION/{f=1} f&&/TARGET_BEADS/{n++}'` form and EXECUTED it — it
  reports n=5 and PASSES at 8fc9e36, i.e. it cannot fail. Use this per-block check instead,
  which was executed RED at HEAD and GREEN on a patched copy:

      f=skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md; fail=0
      while IFS= read -r start; do
        end=$(awk -v s="$start" 'NR>s && /^2\. \*\*Invoke/{print NR; exit}' "$f")
        [ -z "$end" ] && end=$((start+40))
        n=$(sed -n "${start},$((end-1))p" "$f" | grep -c 'TARGET_BEADS')
        echo "claim-step at $start: hits=$n"; [ "$n" -ge 1 ] || fail=1
      done < <(grep -n 'CLAIM-AT-SELECTION)\*\*\|CLAIM-AT-SELECTION\*\*' "$f" | cut -d: -f1)
      exit $fail

  Executed at 8fc9e36: `claim-step at line 350 (block 350..371): hits=0` /
  `claim-step at line 477 (block 477..477): hits=0` → **exit 1 (RED, correct)**. Executed on
  a copy with the header mandate injected into both blocks → hits=1/1, **exit 0 (GREEN)**.
  This check must go from exit 1 to exit 0 across the fix.

- **AC2 (SEAM PROOF — must go RED if EITHER side is reverted).** One end-to-end run, not two
  half-checks. Build a `progress.md` EXACTLY as the amended Phase-2 claim step now instructs
  (claim id + `TARGET_BEADS=N`), for a deliberately INCOMPLETE batch (N=2, one `### Bead`
  entry), and run:

      bash skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh --allow-empty \

title: ac-review Phase 1 scope detection has no .beads/ exclusion — 7.5x reviewer noise per registry run
description:
`skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` Phase 1 Scope Detection resolves `DIFF_RANGE` (grep-target:
the `DIFF_RANGE=` assignments and the rung list — at 8fc9e36 lines 153-212) and then feeds
it straight to `git diff $DIFF_RANGE` with no pathspec exclusion. In a beads-carrying repo
the range is dominated by `.beads/` JSONL churn, which no reviewer can act on.

**Corrected measurements (refine 2026-08-03 — the filing's numbers do NOT reproduce; these
were re-executed against 8fc9e36 and are the ones to use):**

    $ git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --name-only | wc -l
    129                       # filing said 160
    $ git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --name-only | grep -c '^\.beads/'
    105                       # filing said 111
    $ git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --stat | tail -1
    129 files changed, 6989 insertions(+), 4932 deletions(-)          # filing said 7910 ins
    $ git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --stat -- ':(exclude).beads/' | tail -1
    24 files changed, 934 insertions(+), 56 deletions(-)              # filing said 963 ins

Both SHAs exist and are ancestors of HEAD (`git cat-file -t` → commit for both), so the
range is stable; the filing's numbers were simply wrong. The effect is unchanged and large:
**105/129 files (81%) are `.beads/` churn; excluding them cuts 6989 insertions to 934 (7.5x)**.

**Corrected site count:** `grep -c 'git diff \$DIFF_RANGE' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` = **6**
at 8fc9e36 (lines 160, 161, 211, 212, 295, 301) — the filing said "4+". Six is the number to
plan against.

Every registry-repo ac-review run pays this today. The exclusion belongs at the point
`DIFF_RANGE` is consumed, so all downstream consumers (Phase 2 reviewer prompts, the report's
Scope line, Phase 4 auto-fix scoping) inherit it from one place.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --name-only | wc -l` → 129
2. `git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --name-only | grep -c '^\.beads/'` → 105
3. `git diff 44717df..0ffc1a4 --stat -- ':(exclude).beads/' | tail -1` → 24 files, 934 ins
4. The unfiltered form is what `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` prescribes (grep-target
   `git diff $DIFF_RANGE --stat` / `--name-only`, lines 160-161 at 8fc9e36).

## Acceptance Criteria
Baselines EXECUTED at draft on 8fc9e36.

- **AC1 (bite-proof, baseline 0 → must be ≥1):**
  `grep -c 'exclude).beads' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns **0** at 8fc9e36 and MUST
  return ≥1 after the fix, with `grep -n` showing the hit inside Phase 1 Scope Detection
  (i.e. at a line number above the `## Phase 2: Parallel Review` heading — line 288 at 8fc9e36;
  note the heading is `##`, not `###`).
- **AC2 (single point of application, bite-proof, SHELL-SHAPE-AGNOSTIC).** Baseline: 6
  `git diff $DIFF_RANGE` sites. The check must accept EITHER the scalar or the array
  pathspec idiom — refine drafted a scalar-only grep and proved it wrongly fails a correct
  array-form implementation (`"${DIFF_PATHSPEC[@]}"`, which is the word-splitting-safe
  shape). Use this:

      f=skills/ac-review/SKILL.md
      all=$(grep -c 'git diff \$DIFF_RANGE' "$f")
      covered=$(grep -cE 'git diff \$DIFF_RANGE ("\$\{DIFF_PATHSPEC\[@\]\}"|\$DIFF_PATHSPEC|--.*:\(exclude\)\.beads)' "$f")
      defs=$(grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*DIFF_PATHSPEC=' "$f")
      echo "sites=$all covered=$covered defs=$defs"
      [ "$all" -eq "$covered" ] && [ "$defs" -eq 1 ]

  i.e. **every** `git diff $DIFF_RANGE` site carries the exclusion, and it is carried by a
  single `DIFF_PATHSPEC` definition (defined once next to the `DIFF_RANGE` resolution)
  rather than the pathspec being copy-pasted 6 times. EXECUTED at 8fc9e36:
  `sites=6 covered=0 defs=0` → **exit 1 (RED)**. Executed on a scalar-form patched copy:
  `6/6/1` → **exit 0**. On an array-form patched copy: `6/6/1` → **exit 0**. Both correct
  implementations pass; HEAD fails.
- **AC3 (decision RESOLVED by refine — implement it, do not re-litigate).** `DIFF_PATHSPEC`
  excludes **`.beads/` ONLY** in this change. `.claude/reviews/` and other generated-artifact
  paths are **deliberately NOT excluded**: a prior run's review artifacts are rare in a range,
  are legitimately reviewable when a skill changed how they are written, and a silent
  over-exclusion hides real findings — which is the strictly worse failure mode than a little
  extra noise. Record exactly this rationale in the skill text next to the `DIFF_PATHSPEC`
  definition, naming `.claude/reviews/` as considered-and-rejected so the next reader does not
  re-open it. (If a future run measures `.claude/reviews/` noise as material, that is a new
  bead with its own measurement.)
- **AC4 (measurement, executed):** run the amended snippet against `44717df..0ffc1a4` and
  paste the before/after insertion counts in the close reason. Expected: 6989 → 934.
- **AC5:** `bash lint.sh` exits 0. Measured at draft: exit 0, 372 checks, ~16s.

## Test Scope

- `bash lint.sh` — VERIFIED at draft: exit 0, "lint: 372 checks, 0 failures".

## Delivers

title: consensus.py keys on exact file:line — same defect at adjacent lines never reaches consensus
description:
`skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py` computes its match key in `norm_key()`
(grep-target: `def norm_key(f):` — lines 58-63 at 8fc9e36) as
`"<normalized file path>:<line>|<lowercased category>"`. The secondary same-location
any-category check (grep-target: the `by_loc` index and the
`# Same-location secondary index:` comment — lines 152-173 at 8fc9e36) is keyed on
`f["_key"].rsplit("|", 1)[0]` — i.e. also an EXACT line match.

Consequence: two reviewers who find the SAME defect but anchor it to adjacent lines produce
two distinct keys and two distinct locations, so neither reaches the 2-reviewer consensus
threshold. Both stay DEFERRED instead of becoming one consensus AUTO_FIX, and the defect
ships unless a human happens to read both entries.

**Reproduction VERIFIED at draft (refine 2026-08-03, 8fc9e36).** The filing's repro steps
omitted `severity`, which makes them unsatisfiable as written — see AC-CRITICAL note below.

## Steps to Reproduce
Exact, executed at draft. `consensus.py` reads `panel-round-<N>.json` + one
`round-<N>-<role>.json` per spawned role from `--artifacts-dir`.

    mkdir -p /tmp/cx
    printf '%s' '{"spawned": ["correctness", "contracts"]}' > /tmp/cx/panel-round-1.json
    printf '%s' '{"findings":[{"title":"unchecked null deref in handler","severity":"medium","file":"src/handler.ts","line":17,"category":"correctness","fix":"guard the null","auto_fixable":true}]}' > /tmp/cx/round-1-correctness.json
    printf '%s' '{"findings":[{"title":"handler may deref null on the same path","severity":"medium","file":"src/handler.ts","line":19,"category":"contracts","fix":"guard the null","auto_fixable":true}]}' > /tmp/cx/round-1-contracts.json
    python3 skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py --artifacts-dir /tmp/cx --round 1

Observed at 8fc9e36:

    Findings: 2 total → 2 after dedup
    AUTO_FIX (0):
    DEFERRED (2) — ...
      - [medium] src/handler.ts:17 — unchecked null deref in handler  (correctness)
      - [medium] src/handler.ts:19 — handler may deref null on the same path  (contracts)

**`severity: medium` is MANDATORY in the fixture.** Executed with `severity: high` the same
inputs yield `AUTO_FIX (2)` with reason `severity:high` — the location bug is fully masked
because severity alone triggers auto-fix. An implementer who picks `high` as a natural demo
severity will conclude there is no bug.

**Control (exact-line, executed):** the same two findings both at `line: 17` DO reach
consensus at 8fc9e36 — `AUTO_FIX (2)` with reason `same-location-consensus:contracts,correctness`.
So the secondary index works; only its exactness is the defect.

**PROVEN CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX (this is the load-bearing new finding — read before choosing).**
Refine built the anti-false-merge control the filing asked for: two GENUINELY DIFFERENT
defects, medium severity, adjacent lines 17/19, different categories
(`off-by-one in loop bound` @17 / `response type omits the error branch` @19). Executed at
8fc9e36 → `AUTO_FIX (0) / DEFERRED (2)`.

That control is **byte-identical to the RED fixture in every field `norm_key` reads**
(file, line, category) — they differ only in `title`/`fix` text. Therefore **any
location-only fix (candidate (a) line-proximity window, or candidate (b) enclosing-symbol
keying) provably cannot satisfy both ACs at once**: whatever merges the RED pair also merges
the control pair. Do not spend a session discovering this. Note also that HEAD already
accepts exactly this trade at exact-line granularity (the CONTROL above merges two
distinct-titled findings at :17), so "never false-merge" is not the current bar either.

Candidate fix shapes, re-scoped against that proof (pick ONE, justify against the false-merge
mode in the close reason):
- **(a) line-proximity window** (`|line_a - line_b| <= K`, K small and named) — cheapest;
  MUST be paired with an explicit written acceptance that same-location-different-defect pairs
  merge, citing the HEAD precedent above. Cannot pass a "control stays separate" AC at the
  same distance.
- **(b) enclosing symbol/heading keying** — same limitation as (a), plus it needs source
  access the script does not currently have.
- **(c) near-miss REPORT the conductor must adjudicate** (adjacent-line pairs surface as a
  third bucket, never silently auto-merged) — the ONLY candidate that satisfies both the RED
  fixture and a strict "genuinely different defects stay separate" control, because a
  near-miss is neither an AUTO_FIX nor a silent DEFERRED.

title: ac-batch-close Act 3 carry: rename snippet is dcg-blocked verbatim + ${CARRIED:+...} pathspec word-splits wrong under zsh
description:
`skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md:613-615` prescribes:

    CARRIED=".claude/reviews/batch/$(basename "$PENDING_REPORT")"
    git mv "$PENDING_REPORT" "$CARRIED" 2>/dev/null \
      || { mv "$PENDING_REPORT" "$CARRIED" && git add "$CARRIED"; }

Both the `git mv` and the `mv` fallback take fully variable-built paths, which dcg blocks
as a dynamic-path move (VERIFIED at HEAD 8fc9e36:
`dcg test 'git mv "$PENDING_REPORT" "$CARRIED"'` -> BLOCKED, rule
`core.filesystem:mv-dynamic-path`). The snippet is therefore unrunnable as written — every
batch-close that reaches the carry step must stop, re-resolve the two paths by hand, and
re-issue the move with literals. The skill ships an instruction its own guard rejects.

**Second, independent defect found during refine (2026-08-03, execute-at-draft):** the
pathspec at SKILL.md:625 —

    ${CARRIED:+"$CARRIED" ".claude/reviews/pending/"}

— is ALREADY BROKEN under zsh, the fleet's default shell. An unquoted `${VAR:+a b}`
alternate value is word-split in bash but NOT in zsh, so when `CARRIED` is set the two
paths collapse into ONE pathspec word and `git commit -- ...` matches no file. Executed at
HEAD 8fc9e36:

    bash: argc=4  [--] [batch.md] [.claude/reviews/batch/X.md] [.claude/reviews/pending/]
    zsh : argc=3  [--] [batch.md] [.claude/reviews/batch/X.md .claude/reviews/pending/]

This fires on exactly the path this bead touches (a report IS carried), so it is fixed here
rather than filed separately. Word-safe replacement, verified identical under both shells:

    ${CARRIED:+"$CARRIED"} ${CARRIED:+".claude/reviews/pending/"}
    bash argc=4 / zsh argc=4 (set) ; bash argc=2 / zsh argc=2 (empty)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a batch-close with a pending findings report, set `PENDING_REPORT` and `CARRIED` per
   SKILL.md:597 / 613.
2. Issue `git mv "$PENDING_REPORT" "$CARRIED"` exactly as written.
3. dcg blocks the call (`core.filesystem:mv-dynamic-path`).

title: DECISION: mandate execute-at-draft verification for ACs and preamble paste-sites (ac-bead-refine workflow.md + ac-pipeline delegation-contract.md)
description:
decision: should the pipeline mandate that every authored verification artifact (an
acceptance-criterion command, a paste-site instruction) be EXECUTED against its literal
target at draft time — with the run pasted as proof — rather than validated by
construction?

options:
  a) Mandate it in both homes (recommended) — add an execute-at-draft gate to
     `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` § AC authoring, and an
     assert-the-anchor-in-the-target-body gate to
     `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble.
     Cost: two skill edits + a small per-AC time tax at draft. Benefit: removes the
     single largest cost cluster of this run.
  b) Mandate it in ac-bead-refine only — cheaper, but leaves the preamble-rollout half
     (the one that shipped 6/12 sites broken across two waves) uncovered.
  c) Do nothing — rely on the existing memory fact
     `verify-doctrine-claims-against-live-tools`. Rejected by the evidence: that fact was
     already in the substrate this entire run and did not prevent any of the instances
     below.

context:
One root cause produced the largest aggregate cost of RUN 20260803-113231-34132, in two
surfaces that look unrelated but are the same mistake — **the artifact was verified by
CONSTRUCTION, never by FUNCTION**.

Surface 1 — acceptance criteria drafted by reading:
- child FuchsiaWolfRefineD, Phase 2: "every AC drafted from reading rather than execution
  had a defect. Execute at draft time, not at review time." ~15 min across 9 ACs.
- child FuchsiaWolfRefineF, R2-R4: "every AC baseline drafted by reading had to be
  corrected by running it — 2 vacuous ACs, 2 wrong baselines." 2 extra rounds.
- child FuchsiaWolfImplB: an AC reading "git diff lint.sh | grep CONDUCTOR_CEILING returns
  nothing" is unsatisfiable, because diff CONTEXT lines carry the token (~2 min); a second
  AC grep missed the "## Method verdict" heading it targeted because greps are
  case-sensitive (~2 min).
- children FuchsiaWolfImplC / FuchsiaWolfImplD: three separate instances of corrected prose
  reusing the exact token its own AC greps for, plus line-budget near-misses — 3+ extra
  edit cycles.

Surface 2 — paste-site instructions verified by byte-diff, not by grepping the target body:
- the Phase-2 retrospective confirms wave 2's fix (`ac-08k`) added an anchor-referencing
  paste instruction that was never checked against the actual prompt body, and wave 4's
  12-site rollout (`ac-syct`) shipped the same class at 6 of 12 new sites.
- one instance (`skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md`) is confirmed still broken at
  HEAD 0ffc1a4 — grep shows the anchor phrase appears only in the instruction, never in the
  body. Tracked as open bead `ac-kfjc` (the instances); this decision is about the DOCTRINE
  that would have prevented them.

Recurrence is already evidenced in the substrate: memory fact
`verify-doctrine-claims-against-live-tools` ("run the command before writing its behavior
into skill text; on review, execute unexecuted claims"). Its existence is why option (c)
fails — the lesson is recorded but not GATED, so it is honoured only when an agent happens
to remember it.

Adjacent open item: `ac-bl0` (dream proposal, "bead-refine-quality-gate-anchors-acs")
touches AC anchoring in the same skill. Its memo file is absent from the tree, so overlap
could not be verified — worth reading the two together before applying either.

## Proposed change

**Target 1 — `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md`, § AC authoring (Phase 2):**
an AC whose criterion is a shell command may not be written down until that command has
been RUN against the current tree and its output recorded as the baseline. The recorded
baseline, not the author's expectation, is what the later round verifies against. Two
named sub-rules earned this run: (i) draft replacement prose against the AC's LITERAL
grep, not its intent — a correction that reintroduces the greped token silently fails its
own AC; (ii) an AC that greps must state case-sensitivity and anchor on a literal, since
`grep -n 'method verdict'` does not match `## Method verdict`.

**Target 2 — `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md`, § Child-spawn
preamble:** closing a preamble-site bead requires grepping the literal anchor phrase in
each TARGET PROMPT BODY, not a byte-diff or fence-count over the instruction block. State
the failure mode inline: an instruction that references an anchor absent from the body it
governs is inert, and byte-level checks cannot see that.

**Deletion/supersession check:** neither edit supersedes existing content — both are
additive gates on steps that currently have no gate. If applying them makes the standing
"verify before write" prose in either file redundant, that prose should be REMOVED in the
same change rather than left to accrete (promotion-ladder: removal ranks equally with
addition).

recommendation: **(a)** — the objective bar is cleared twice over: recurrence is evidenced
by an existing substrate fact AND by two waves shipping the same defect class, and the
material per-run cost is ~25+ minutes plus 2 extra refine rounds plus a still-broken site
at HEAD. This is the single highest-cost item of the run, filed as this land's one T2
under the per-land cap; every other candidate was demoted to a T3 observation.

## Delivers
- decision: recorded human choice on whether execute-at-draft becomes a mandated gate in
  ac-bead-refine and ac-pipeline's delegation contract, and the consequent skill edits
close_reason: Decided (a): execute-at-draft mandated in both homes; edits landed

title: Upstream ask (dcg): path-scoped allowlist exemptions + invocation-vs-prose matching
description:
From decision ac-umq (ratified by Craig 2026-07-17). dcg false-positived 3-4x in RUN 20260716-111224-31570 across two modes: (a) descriptive prose merely QUOTING a destructive command inside comment/heredoc bodies, (b) recursive deletes of session-owned /tmp scratch dirs. Verified 2026-07-17 on dcg 0.6.5: the local allowlist is RULE-granular only (dcg allow <rule-id>) — no path scoping, so exempting scratch dirs locally would disable a whole rule everywhere. Sanctioned workarounds are documented in skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md.

REFINE VERIFICATION (2026-07-19, TurquoiseValley): premise VALID. Installed dcg still 0.6.5 (`dcg --version`, checked 2026-07-19) — the "check for a newer release first" step is unlikely to have already fixed this, but re-confirm at implement time.

## Deliverable
Check the latest dcg release first (dcg update; re-confirm 0.6.5 is still current at implement time). If still missing, file upstream feature request(s): (1) match only actual command invocations, not quoted text inside string/heredoc/comment bodies — the higher-frequency, zero-risk fix; (2) path-scoped allowlist entries (rule-id + path pattern) so session-owned scratch dirs can be exempted tightly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `dcg update` run and the resulting version recorded in a comment. IF the invocation-vs-prose matching and path-scoped allowlist are STILL absent in the current release: one or two upstream feature requests filed (the two asks above), URLs recorded in a comment. IF a newer dcg already ships either fix: record that instead and note whether the local workaround in jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md can be retired. Closing requires either filed-reference URLs or a recorded "already fixed in <version>".

FINDING: same-session token-free auth is (a) INTENDED-BUT-CONDITIONAL, NOT (b) 'never a guarantee' and NOT a clean upstream bug.
- register_agent (app.py:6021) and macro_start_session (app.py:9780) BOTH call _bind_session_agent, and _authenticate_agent (app.py:5154) returns token-free when _session_is_bound_to_agent is true. So the carry is a real designed mechanism.
- BUT the binding is keyed on a stable ctx.session_id (_session_binding_key, app.py:5050-5074). It fails in two ways our architecture hits: (1) each phase child is a SEPARATE MCP session that never inherits the conductor's binding; (2) transports that don't surface a stable session_id fall to a per-call orphan UUID (ctx refuses attribute caching), so the binding is written under one key and looked up under another -> invisible -> name-only call rejected. This exactly reproduces run 20260719-102946 (three independent children each rediscovering rejection).

CONCLUSION: our docs were OVER-CLAIMING the carry as dependable. It works only within one stable-session-id lifetime. Fix = always thread registration_token on every privileged call (blanket rule). No upstream bug filed: the mechanism is intentional and correct under a stable session id; issue #148 already fixed the HTTP variant. If a future repro proves failure WITHIN one confirmed-stable ctx.session_id, THAT would warrant an upstream file with this repro. Self-deregister (Layer 1, same session that registered) legitimately keeps the token-optional carve-out.

title: B1 pilot: trigger precision/recall pass over the 6 pipeline-conductor skill descriptions
description:
Roadmap item 5: the promotion ladder names a trigger precision/recall list as the CHEAPEST
skill eval and it has never been run. Per skill: ~5 "should-activate" natural phrasings +
~5 "should-NOT-activate" near-misses, judged against that skill's frontmatter `description:`;
descriptions that fail get fixed. This tests ROUTING — the one quality axis nothing else in
the registry covers.

discovered-from: unknown (roadmap item 5, banked by commit be40028 "roadmap items 5+6 banked
before session close" — no single originating bead)

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03)

- **Never run, no artifact exists.** No trigger-test corpus file exists anywhere in the repo.
- Doctrine that mandates it: `skills/skill-builder/references/promotion-ladder.md:158-166`
  ("trigger **precision/recall list** — a 'should-activate' set of natural prompts + a
  'should-NOT-activate' exclusion set, run against the description ... Do this for every
  skill", listed as cheapest-first item 1).
- The per-skill pattern already exists but with no corpus:
  `skills/skill-builder/workflows/create-skill.md:162-171` (2-3 trigger variations +
  exclusion cases) and `skills/skill-builder/references/testing-patterns.md:128,150-151,
  170-173,205` (worked examples of a pass/fail log, including a real false-negative fix).
- What EXISTS and is NOT this: `lint.sh` Check 13 (`lint.sh:557-568`) validates description
  BUDGET (<1024 chars) and the invocation graph. It does not test routing at all.
- Corpus size: **58** skills at HEAD (`ls skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l` = 58). NOTE:
  `ls -d skills/*/` returns 59 because `skills/_tools/` is a directory with NO SKILL.md and
  is not a skill — always enumerate from `skills/*/SKILL.md`, never from `skills/*/`, or
  every completeness check reports a phantom `MISSING _tools`. At ~5 positives + ~5
  negatives each that is ~580 judgments.

## Work

Build the corpus and run the pass.

**Artifact home (single file, so it is greppable and diffable):**
`skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — one `## <skill-name>` section per
skill, each with a `should-activate` list and a `should-NOT-activate` list, plus a verdict
column recorded per phrasing on each run.

**THIS BEAD IS BATCH B1 ONLY — the 6 pipeline conductors** (rescoped at refine 2026-08-03;
~580 judgments is not one bead). B1 = ac-loop, ac-implement, ac-review, ac-batch-close,
ac-merge, ac-land — the tier with the highest routing stakes, and the batch that validates
the method before it is run at scale. That is ~60 judgments, one sitting.

**The remaining ~52 skills are NOT dropped** — they are the follow-on bead this bead files
as part of its own done (see the last AC), which is BLOCKED on this one so B1's go/no-go
verdict actually gates it. Delivers partition: B1 owns the corpus file's creation, its
6 conductor sections, those 6 descriptions' fixes, and the method verdict; the follow-on
owns every other skill's section and description fixes.

The conductor tier is defined in `lint.sh:739-746` (`CONDUCTOR_SKILLS`) — read it at
implement time rather than trusting the list above.

**Judging:** for each phrasing, decide from the frontmatter `description:` ALONE (that is
all the router sees) whether the skill would be selected. A should-activate phrasing that
would not select = recall failure. A should-NOT phrasing that would select = precision
failure. Both are findings; the fix is a description edit, re-judged after.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` exists with one `## <skill>`
      section for each of the 6 conductor skills named in `lint.sh:739-746` — no more, no
      fewer. Check:
      `for s in ac-loop ac-implement ac-review ac-batch-close ac-merge ac-land; do grep -q "^## $s$" skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md || echo "MISSING $s"; done`
      prints nothing. (When the follow-on bead extends this to the rest, enumerate from
      `skills/*/SKILL.md` — a `skills/*/` loop always reports a phantom `MISSING _tools`,
      verified 2026-08-03.)
- [ ] Every section carries >= 5 should-activate and >= 5 should-NOT-activate phrasings.
      Check: a count script over the file asserts both minima per section.
- [ ] Every phrasing carries a recorded verdict from this run (pass/fail), not a blank.
      Check: grep the file for un-verdicted rows; must return none.
- [ ] Precision/recall failures are listed with the description edit that fixed each, and
      the re-judged verdict. Check: the file's summary section names each fixed skill.
- [ ] The file carries an explicit **method verdict** section: did judging from the
      `description:` alone produce usable, non-noisy signal on these 6? A plain GO or NO-GO,
      with the reasoning. This is the gate on the follow-on bead — an ambiguous verdict is
      not done. Check: `grep -n 'method verdict' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`.
- [ ] A follow-on bead exists covering the remaining skills (everything in
      `skills/*/SKILL.md` minus the 6 conductors), labelled `unrefined`, carrying
      `discovered-from: ac-gcj.10`, and BLOCKED on this bead. Check:
      `br list --json --all --limit 0 | jq -r '.issues[] | select(.id != "ac-gcj.10") | select((.description // "") | test("discovered-from: ac-gcj[.]10")) | .id'`
      returns exactly one id. BOTH guards are required (verified 2026-08-03): `// ""`
      because several live issues have a null description and the unguarded form aborts;
      and `select(.id != "ac-gcj.10")` because that `discovered-from:` phrase appears
      inside THIS bead's own AC text, so without it the check self-matches and passes
      before any follow-on bead exists.
- [ ] Every description edited is still under the 1024-char budget and lint stays green.
      Check: `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0` (Check 13 enforces the budget).
- [ ] `git diff --stat skills/*/SKILL.md` shows edits ONLY to `description:` lines — no
      body content changed by this bead. Check: `git diff skills/ -- '*/SKILL.md'` and read.

## Test Scope

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` (new)
- `skills/{ac-loop,ac-implement,ac-review,ac-batch-close,ac-merge,ac-land}/SKILL.md` —
  frontmatter `description:` lines only. No other skill's SKILL.md is touched by this bead.
- Verification: the corpus-completeness and per-section-minimum scripts above, plus
  `./lint.sh` exit 0 (Check 13 = description budget + invocation graph; Check 14 =
  no-net-growth per SKILL.md, which a one-line description edit must not trip — if it does,
  the edit is too large).
- There is no automated router to test against: judgments are model-made from the
  description alone. **This check is NOT machine-runnable** — it is explicitly a judged
  eval, and the corpus file with recorded verdicts is the evidence. Do not write an AC that
  looks executable when it is a judgment call.
- The method verdict is this bead's real output alongside the corpus: it is what decides
  whether the follow-on bead is worth running at all.

## Delivers

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — created, with should-activate /
  should-NOT-activate phrasing lists + recorded verdicts for the **6 pipeline conductors**
- `description:` fixes on whichever of those 6 failed precision or recall
- an explicit GO/NO-GO method verdict in that file
- a follow-on bead owning the remaining ~52 skills, blocked on this one

## Consumes

- none

## Approach (advisory)

If B1 shows the corpus is more valuable as per-skill files than one big file, splitting is
fine — but then update the completeness check above to match, and keep ONE grep-able index.
Suggested batching for the follow-on: remaining ac-* skills, then domain skills
(brand-system, supabase, capacitor, beads-standards, context-engineering, skill-builder,
dream, ...), then everything else. A NO-GO verdict here is a legitimate, valuable outcome —
the point is routing evidence, not corpus volume.

title: Ratchet Check 15 CONDUCTOR_CEILING once ac-znk.3 Stage-2 diets ac-review
description:
Split out of ac-gcj.6 at refine (2026-08-03) to close a dropped-scope gap: ac-gcj.6 was rescoped to the standard-tier ratchet only, and the conductor-tier ratchet it de-scoped was claimed ONLY in an ac-znk.3 COMMENT, never in ac-znk.3's `## Delivers` or ACs. A comment is not an owner. This bead is the owner.

discovered-from: ac-gcj.6

## Premise state at HEAD (re-verified 2026-08-03 at HEAD 21d6db6 — ALL line anchors below were EXECUTED, and the filing's anchors had drifted; do not trust an anchor you have not re-grepped)

> **ANCHOR WARNING — `lint.sh` line numbers move HOURLY. Grep, never `sed -n '<N>p'`.** During this refine pass alone the numbers below shifted **twice within one hour** (CONDUCTOR_CEILING `:736` at filing -> `:738` -> `:743`), because ac-gcj.6's standard-tier work is in flight in the same shared checkout. Every anchor here is dated; treat it as a pointer to a *grep target*, not a coordinate.

- `grep -n '^CONDUCTOR_CEILING=' lint.sh` -> value **1110** (at `:743` as of 2026-08-03 13:15; `:738` an hour earlier; the filing said `:736`).
- `grep -n '^STANDARD_CEILING=' lint.sh` -> **730** in the working tree as of 2026-08-03 13:15 (was 770 at the filing) — ac-gcj.6's scope, in flight, NOT this bead's.
- The conductor-tier derivation comment is the block containing "the W3.2 pilot dieted+wired ac-loop to … 963 lines … x 1.15 ~= 1107 -> 1110" (`:726-730` on 2026-08-03; the filing said `:723-727`, which is the preceding header sentence).
- The banner echo repeating the stale basis: `grep -n 'conductor-tier ceiling:' lint.sh` (`:756` on 2026-08-03 13:15; `:751` an hour earlier; the filing said `:749`).
- Check 15 begins at the comment `# Check 15 — post-pilot line ceilings` (`:713`); the conductor leg is the `for cskill in "${CONDUCTOR_SKILLS[@]}"` loop. (The filing said `:711-790`.)
- **Correction to the filing's doctrine citation.** The filing cited `lint.sh:733-735` as forbidding a raise. The text "do not raise it to accommodate a bloated skill — diet the skill instead" (`grep -n 'diet the skill instead' lint.sh`) actually sits inside the **STANDARD-tier** derivation paragraph, not the conductor one. The principle is plainly meant to bind both tiers and this bead adopts it as binding — but the citation named the wrong tier and is corrected here rather than repeated.
- **Conductor-tier sizes re-measured at HEAD 2026-08-03** (`wc -l skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`): ac-loop **916** · ac-implement **682** · ac-review **1061** · ac-batch-close **717** · ac-merge **727** · ac-land **658**. Max = **ac-review 1061**. (The filing said ac-implement 681 / ac-review 1058 — both drifted upward. Anchors and sizes in this section will drift again; re-measure at implement time, do not copy these forward.)
- **The ratchet remains arithmetically IMPOSSIBLE today.** 1061 x 1.10 = 1167.1 and 1061 x 1.15 = 1220 — both ABOVE the current 1110, so applying the formula would RAISE the ceiling, which the doctrine forbids. The blocker is ac-review's size.

## The trigger threshold (this is the number to watch)

For a x1.10 ratchet rounded UP to the nearest 10 to land strictly BELOW 1110, the result must be <= 1100, so `max_conductor_lines` must be **<= 1000**. ac-review is 1061 today: **at least 61 lines must come out of the largest conductor skill** before this bead is implementable. That single number, not a narrative, is the readiness test.

## Work

After ac-znk.3 Stage-2 lands, re-measure the conductor tier and lower `CONDUCTOR_CEILING` in `lint.sh` to `ceil_to_10(max_conductor_lines x 1.10)`, updating the derivation comment and the banner echo (locate both by grep, per the anchor warning) to the new measured basis. Use x1.10 to match the sibling ratchet in ac-gcj.6; if the repo settles on keeping its single x1.15 convention, use that instead and say which. **The invariant is that the value goes DOWN, never up.**

## Delivers

- `lint.sh` `CONDUCTOR_CEILING` ratcheted DOWN to a post-Stage-2 measured basis, with its derivation comment and echo line refreshed to the new measured max, skill name and multiplier

## Consumes

- none

**Why `- none` despite a `blocks` edge — sequencing only, no artifact claim.** `bead-conventions.md` § Bead I/O contract requires each Consumes entry to be either `<blocker-id> -> <artifact>` or the single literal `- none`; the literal is used here deliberately so the contract stays mechanically parseable. This bead has a `blocks` edge to ac-znk.3 because it must not be attempted before that diet wave runs. It deliberately names NO consumed artifact from ac-znk.3: ac-znk.3's `## Delivers` promises only "ac-loop core shrunk by measurement, not argument" and it has no `## Acceptance Criteria`, so a "dieted ac-review" is **not** part of ac-znk.3's binding surface — it appears only in ac-znk.3's comments. Refine round 1 (RUN 20260803-113231-34132) verified this and flagged the original Consumes line, which claimed that unpromised artifact, as a binding claim resting on future state. It has been dropped rather than fabricated. `bead-conventions.md` § Bead I/O contract explicitly permits a dep edge with no Consumes line where the dependency is pure sequencing. **This bead therefore self-gates on AC 0 below rather than trusting its blocker's scope.**

## Acceptance Criteria

Commands below were EXECUTED against HEAD on 2026-08-03; RED-now values are measured.

0. **PREMISE GATE — run this FIRST and stop if it fails.** Re-measure: `for s in ac-loop ac-implement ac-review ac-batch-close ac-merge ac-land; do wc -l < skills/$s/SKILL.md; done | sort -n | tail -1`. If that max is **> 1000**, the downward ratchet is arithmetically impossible: post a comment on this bead recording the measured max and the date, leave the bead OPEN and UNIMPLEMENTED, and stop. Do NOT raise the ceiling and do NOT weaken the multiplier to manufacture a pass. (RED now: max = **1061** — this gate FAILS at HEAD, which is the correct and expected state today.)
1. `grep '^CONDUCTOR_CEILING=' lint.sh` yields a value strictly LESS than 1110 AND >= the max re-measured in AC 0. (RED now: 1110.)
2. No stale "ac-loop 963 +15%" figure survives anywhere in the file — the derivation comment AND the banner echo both carry the new measured basis: `grep -c '963' lint.sh` returns 0. (RED now: **3** — executed; two hits in the derivation comment, one in the banner echo. The count covers the whole file precisely because the stale figure appears in more than one place, and an earlier draft of this AC guessed 2 and was wrong.)
3. Every conductor skill still passes, checked over the CONDUCTOR leg only: `./lint.sh | sed -n '/^conductor-tier ceiling:/,/^standard-tier ceiling:/p' | grep -c '^  PASS'` returns **6**. (Executed at HEAD: returns 6.) **Do not use a bare `grep -c 'PASS  ac-'`** — it returns 29 because the standard tier also contains `ac-*` skills; that over-matching form was drafted, executed, and rejected during refine.
4. **Negative proof (the check must be able to go RED).** Temporarily set `CONDUCTOR_CEILING` to `<re-measured max> - 1`; `./lint.sh` must FAIL naming the offending skill (the `fail "Check 15: conductor '$cskill' …"` branch); then revert. A ratchet that cannot fail is not a ratchet.
5. `STANDARD_CEILING`'s VALUE is unchanged by this bead (that is ac-gcj.6's scope). **Check by value, not by `git diff`:** record `grep '^STANDARD_CEILING=' lint.sh` before starting and assert it is identical after. A `git diff lint.sh | grep -c STANDARD_CEILING` check is UNSOUND here — executed during refine on a nominally clean tree it returned **4**, because this is a shared checkout and a sibling's in-flight ac-gcj.6 work (STANDARD_CEILING 770 -> 730) was already sitting uncommitted in `lint.sh`. A diff-shaped AC cannot distinguish your edit from a co-worker's.
6. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the EXIT CODE only — never the check count.** The count drifts constantly in this shared checkout (`314` at 13:00 on 2026-08-03, `372` an hour later after siblings landed a new check).

- `lint.sh` — Check 15 block, conductor-tier leg ONLY. Locate by grep, not line number: `^CONDUCTOR_CEILING=`, `conductor-tier ceiling:`, `# Check 15 — post-pilot line ceilings`, `for cskill in`. - Verification harness: **`./lint.sh` itself is the test.** Check 15 has NO unit harness — `scripts/lint-net-growth.test.sh` (repo root, verified present at HEAD) covers Check 14 only. The AC-4 negative proof is what substitutes for a harness here.

  must be dieted before any conductor ratchet is possible. **ac-znk.3 already owns this**

  de-scope prevents.
- **Half B' — standard-tier ceiling ratchet: EXECUTABLE at HEAD.** This is the remaining
  scope of this bead. Largest standard-tier SKILL.md = ac-hygiene 660 lines;
  660 x 1.10 = 726 -> 730 (clean round-up), well under the current `STANDARD_CEILING=770`

  `lint.sh:726` and `lint.sh:732` both derive today's ceilings with **x1.15** headroom, and
  the echo lines at `lint.sh:749,764` say "+15%". This bead's originating instruction

  than a restatement. Implement at **x1.10** and say so in the derivation comment. For
  reference, x1.15 would give 660 x 1.15 = 759 -> 760, which also ratchets; if the
  implementer prefers to keep the repo's single 15% convention, 760 is an acceptable

Ratchet `STANDARD_CEILING` in `lint.sh` from 770 to 730 and update its derivation comment
(`lint.sh:730-737`) to the measured basis. Re-measure at implement time — do not trust the
number above if standard-tier files changed since; the rule is `max(standard-tier SKILL.md
line counts) x 1.10`, rounded up to the next 10, and it must be LOWER than the current
value or the bead does nothing (report and close rather than raising).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `STANDARD_CEILING` in `lint.sh` is lowered to `ceil_to_10(max_standard_lines * 1.10)`,

- Verification command: `./lint.sh` (full run, must exit 0) — the standard-tier leg prints

Fingerprint lint check deliberately LEFT OUT (Craig ruling 3). If at implement time the

report the measurement and close the bead rather than raising the ceiling.

title: Spawn-context economics: contracts paste, payloads point — convert fan-out panels to write-once-point-many
description:
Craig-identified 2026-08-01: conductors GENERATE payload context into N child prompts (conductor output tokens x panel width) where one artifacts file + a literal-path read line would do. Evidence FOR: refine beads-snapshot.json + QA journey/manifest pattern (already point-based); BCA friction loop-retro-delegation-brief-claims-are-hints (children reading primary sources beat pasted briefs — paste is a drift vector, not just cost). Boundary: the orchestrator trap stands — CONTRACT lines (preamble, env invariants binding from action #1) stay verbatim-pasted; only TASK PAYLOAD points.

Premises verified against HEAD 2026-08-02 (refine r1-r4): of the four originally-named panels, only TWO carry a real paste-cost pattern. ac-hygiene's lens payload is `{SCOPE_CONTEXT}` (already point-sized; the whole `### Gather Codebase Context` section at SKILL.md:116-133 is orphaned — its `CODEBASE_CONTEXT` output feeds nothing). ac-plan-init has no explorer brief — only a `[feature]` slug (7x, already point-sized). Scope corrected accordingly.

## Work

1. **Doctrine** — `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` (99 lines at HEAD; no payload section exists; last section `## Child-spawn preamble` runs line 61-EOF, so "insert after" = append at EOF) gains `## Payloads point, contracts paste`, opening with the boundary sentence: this section governs the TASK PAYLOAD only — the env-contract preamble above stays verbatim per its own evidence. Three rules: (a) literal paths, never vars; (b) the payload read is numbered step 1 of the child prompt; (c) verdicts must cite the payload read (completeness-validator tripwire). Plus the payload-transport rule: the invariant is NEVER paste bulk payload content inline. Transport is chosen by whether a deterministic primary source exists — where the payload is live repo/board state a command can regenerate deterministically, point children at that command with literal, resolution-anchored args (`br show <id>`, `git diff <sha-anchored range>`); where the payload is conductor-authored content with no primary source (e.g. `proposed-structure.md`), a written artifact file read by literal path is the correct transport, not a violation. Also state in the same section the compliance verdict on the existing pointer-only preamble references (`validators.md:1`, `explorers.md:1`): verified non-compliant at refine r2 (delegation-contract.md:63-70 explicitly rules pointer-only insufficient; neither ac-beadify nor ac-plan-init SKILL.md injects the verbatim block into constructed child prompts) — the section states "needs backfilling"; the backfill itself is OUT OF SCOPE here (tracked in follow-up bead ac-08k — do not edit validators.md:1/explorers.md:1 in this pass).

   **Converted-prompt shape (identical across all 4 converted prompts — 3 validators + reviewer template). Exactly TWO edits per prompt, nothing else restructures or renumbers:**
   - **(i) Payload read list** — replace the pasted payload block(s) with a numbered list containing ONLY payload acquisitions, one line per payload: `1. Read <literal path>` (artifact transport) or `1. Run: git diff <literal resolved range>` (command transport). A multi-payload prompt (the Completeness validator has two: plan + proposed structure) gets ONE list — `1. Read <plan path>` / `2. Read <proposed-structure path>` — replacing all its pasted blocks and their per-payload sub-headings (`### Original Plan` / `### Proposed Bead Structure`). The prompt's existing task sections (`## Check`, `## Your Method`, etc.) ARE the task — they stay unchanged, un-numbered, and nothing after the read list is renumbered.
   - **(ii) Verdict citation (doctrine rule c)** — each prompt's `## Output` verdict format gains exactly one payload-citation field: validators.md's three formats gain a `**Payload read:** <literal path(s)/command from the read list>` line; reviewer-prompt-template.md's JSON schema gains a top-level `"payload_read"` string key (additive — the conductor's findings merge ignores unknown keys). This is the completeness tripwire: a verdict that cannot name its payload is a child that never read it.

2. **Convert ac-beadify validators** — TWO files, both required:
   - `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md`: `{PROPOSED_STRUCTURE from artifacts}` pasted 3x (lines 30/69/107) though `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/proposed-structure.md` already exists on disk (ac-beadify SKILL.md:134) — replace with the step-1 literal-path read per the shape spec above. `{PLAN_CONTENT}` appears 2x (line 6 substitution-instruction header + line 27 body, Completeness validator only) — CONVERT both (decided refine r2: plan path is discovered once at ac-beadify SKILL.md:47 and stable through validator spawn; point the Completeness validator at the literal plan-file path in the same read list). Update the lines 6-8 substitution-instruction header to describe the new point-based mechanism (it currently frames both as template variables). Per shape-spec edit (ii): add the `**Payload read:**` line to all three validator Output formats (validators.md:39-50, 77-89, 119-130).
   - `skills/ac-beadify/SKILL.md:144`: the conductor spawn instruction "substituting `{PLAN_CONTENT}`, `{PROPOSED_STRUCTURE}`, and `{ARTIFACTS_DIR}`" goes stale once the placeholders are gone — rewrite it to instruct substituting only `{ARTIFACTS_DIR}` (and the literal plan path) into the step-1 read lines.
3. **Convert ac-review panel** — TWO files, both required:
   - `skills/ac-review/references/reviewer-prompt-template.md`: `{DIFF}` (lines 7/20) is instantiated into up to 7 spawned reviewers (6-dimension panel + skills/-gated doctrine-delta lens). Decided refine r2: primary-source-command-only (no diff artifact file) — the conductor already resolves and records `DIFF_RANGE` at Phase 1 (ac-review SKILL.md:252); per the shape spec, step 1 becomes `1. Run: git diff <literal resolved DIFF_RANGE>` with the resolved range substituted (a point-sized string). Per shape-spec edit (ii): add the top-level `"payload_read"` string key to the Output JSON schema (reviewer-prompt-template.md:38-53).
   - `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md:447`: the prompt-build instruction "Substitute `{DIFF}` (the Phase-2 diff)... into each" goes stale — rewrite to instruct substituting the resolved `DIFF_RANGE` string (plus the surviving `{ARTIFACTS_DIR}`/`{ROUND}`/`{N_OTHERS}` placeholders, which stay).
4. **Dead-section cleanup**: remove the entire orphaned `### Gather Codebase Context` section at `skills/ac-hygiene/SKILL.md:116-133` (heading + prose + bash block + the `CODEBASE_CONTEXT` save line — the output feeds nothing; all 7 lenses consume `{SCOPE_CONTEXT}`, set independently at SKILL.md:57).

- [ ] `grep -c "^## Payloads point, contracts paste" skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` returns 1; the section contains the three rules, the payload-transport rule (inline-paste ban + command-vs-artifact criterion), and the verbatim-boundary sentence.

- [ ] `grep -c "{PLAN_CONTENT}\|{PROPOSED_STRUCTURE}" skills/ac-beadify/SKILL.md` returns 0 (conductor spawn instruction at :144 rewritten).
- [ ] `grep -c "{DIFF}" skills/ac-review/references/reviewer-prompt-template.md` returns 0; the template's step 1 directs `git diff <resolved DIFF_RANGE>` (no diff artifact file introduced).
- [ ] `grep -c "{DIFF}" skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns 0 (prompt-build instruction at :447 rewritten).
- [ ] `grep -c "Gather Codebase Context\|CODEBASE_CONTEXT" skills/ac-hygiene/SKILL.md` returns 0 (whole section removed, not just the save line).
- [ ] `./lint.sh` exits 0 (structural/ref check only — does not verify paste-vs-point semantics).
- [ ] `grep -c "Payload read:" skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md` returns 3 (one per validator Output format) and `grep -c "payload_read" skills/ac-review/references/reviewer-prompt-template.md` returns 1 (JSON schema key) — the verdict-citation tripwire from doctrine rule (c), shape-spec edit (ii).

(`explorers.md` deliberately NOT in scope — see Work item 1's out-of-scope note.)

description:
PLAN: _plans/2026-08-01-bead-creation-canon.md — read it first; it carries the measured evidence, the settled design decision, and every verified file:line.

WHY THIS IS P1, not P2: four sources file beads WITHOUT the 'unrefined' label, so ac-implement treats them as refined and implements straight off a raw note. One of them (ac-triage/references/feedback-adapter.md:105) is AUTOMATED and HIGH-VOLUME — every user feedback row. Another (same file:124) files -t decision with NO human-gate label, which per beads-standards L38-43 is the sole gate — so those decisions are silently workable and auto-closable AROUND Craig.

ROOT CAUSE (this is the ac-gcj shape): every bead-creating source reinvented the creation rules, so good ideas do not propagate. ac-review has anchor-dedupe + severity floor + rollup ceiling but no cause/symptom split. qa-shared has the best CONFIRMED-vs-SUSPECTED split in the fleet but ZERO dedupe and ZERO volume control. The canon they should both inherit from (skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md) is WEAKER than either: keyword dedupe only, no floor, no rollup, no perishability. ac-review has outgrown the canon it cites. Five sources cite no canon at all.

NOTE: skills/_shared/bead-conventions.md DOES NOT EXIST. Real path is skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md. This is the dual-canon confusion ac-gcj wave 1 already names.

SETTLED DESIGN DECISION (do not re-litigate; rationale in the plan): for an INFERRED cause, do not mandate validation-before-filing (a QA agent cannot source-trace, so the mandate produces PERFORMED validation — the same defect class as a test that cannot fail), and do not ban the hunch (throws away signal). Instead QUARANTINE it: symptom enters as fact, cause enters a marked-unverified slot the implementer re-derives. Type is the carrier — source-traced cause -> -t bug, inferred cause -> -t investigation.

WORK, ranked by blast radius x cheapness (full detail + verified anchors in the plan):
- P0 x4: add missing 'unrefined' (feedback-adapter:105, ac-batch-close:357, ac-beadify:301/304) and missing 'human-gate' (feedback-adapter:124). One-token fixes.
- P1 x3: fix contradictions — ac-hygiene 154/179/223 file -t bug for non-defects (inflates the Rule-0 preemptive bug lane, contradicts hygiene's OWN L435); ac-land:265 contradicts ac-land:106-109 inside one file; bead-conventions L29-30 licenses filing an inferred cause as bug.
- P2 x3: promote ac-review's anchor-dedupe + floor/ceiling and qa-shared's CONFIRMED/SUSPECTED templates INTO the canon, then have sources cite instead of copy. Port dedupe + volume control to qa-shared (keyed on journey+checkpoint, since QA has no file:line).
- P3 x1: perishability — 0 of 13 sources have any rule. One sentence in the canon body template covers ac-batch-close, ac-triage and ac-hygiene at once. This is what bd-6m0xm asks for.

EVIDENCE BASE: 100/100 P2-P3 review-findings adjudicated against current code (94 KEEP / 5 STALE / 1 DUP; priorities right 70/71) => the finding lane is REAL DEBT, not noise, so do NOT tighten the intake filter — it would suppress true findings. Plus a 2024-closed-bead analysis whose headline is that it CANNOT measure filing quality, because refine corrects false premises in place and they close as 'Implemented and tested'.

DO NOT REDO — shipped in agent-compounds 7da0e5e: ac-loop file-cluster batching; ac-review ANCHOR DEDUPE + ROLLUP CEILING; ac-bead-refine mandatory 'refine-corrections: N' + AC-commands-must-execute, both blocking pre-stamp gates.

- grep -rn 'br create' skills/ --include='*.md' | grep -v 'unrefined'  => only human-gate/decision-lane sites remain

title: ac-triage/ac-tidy scheduled worktree pattern contradicts ac-pipeline's 'no worktrees' invariant
description:
discovered-from: ac-triage-worktree-isolation-l3i

## Problem

`skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` § 0 Preflight **mandates** creating an
isolated git worktree for every scheduled run ("Do NOT run triage in the live checkout.
**Explicitly create a dedicated worktree**").

`skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` states the opposite as a load-bearing pipeline invariant
(grep anchors, not line numbers — this file moves):

- `grep -n "no worktrees" skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` — "The pipeline shares one checkout
  (no worktrees), so concurrent work is kept safe by **identity-scoped file reservations**,
  not branch isolation."
- `grep -n "deliberately rejected" skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` — "Worktrees are
  deliberately rejected (filesystem multiplication, cross-worktree edits corrupt ...)"

Neither side carves out an exception or cross-references the other. `ac-tidy`'s nightly
workflow carries the same worktree pattern, so the contradiction predates this batch —
ac-triage merely made it a second instance, and made it visible.

## Why it matters

A reader of `ac-pipeline` (the owner-hosted coordination canon) reads the ban as absolute
and will treat both scheduled workflows as in violation. A reader of the workflows will
create worktrees inside a pipeline that declares them rejected. One of the two statements
is wrong and the registry does not say which.

## Decided resolution (refine, 2026-08-03) — this is a spec, not an open question

Refine adjudicated this and it is **not** a human taste call: the two situations differ on
an objective, already-load-bearing axis, so the ban is **scoped too broadly** and
`ac-pipeline` is the side that is wrong.

- `ac-pipeline`'s invariant governs **concurrent pipeline ceremonies sharing one app
  checkout**, coordinated by identity-scoped file reservations. Multi-writer.
- A scheduled heartbeat (`ac-tidy` nightly, `ac-triage` daily) is a **single-writer job in
  an app repo whose checkout state it does not control**. There are no siblings to reserve
  against, and the branch guard the worktree replaced is what caused an outage (see the
  bead this was discovered from).

**Implement:** narrow `ac-pipeline`'s invariant to pipeline ceremonies and name the
scheduled-heartbeat carve-out, with a pointer each way. Do NOT delete either workflow's
worktree instruction — they are the correct behaviour for their case.

## Constraint the implementer MUST satisfy (hazard — refine-added)

`skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` is under `lint.sh` **Check 14 (no-net-growth, HARD,
PER-FILE, diff-aware)**. A net-positive edit to that file PASSes only if **that file's own
diff** carries an ADDED line with the exact token `<!-- net-growth-ok: <reason> -->`
(verified: `grep -n "Check 14" lint.sh`; the file already carries 5 such stamps). So
either keep the edit net-neutral-or-shrinking (preferred — reword the existing sentences
rather than appending), or add the stamp. A shrink in another file does NOT offset it.

Sequencing: **ac-vx8p trims narrative from this same file and must land first** (dep edge
added by refine). Landing the trim first leaves headroom and makes a stamp unnecessary.

## Delivers

- `doc: skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` — the worktree invariant restated with explicit scope
  ("concurrent pipeline ceremonies sharing one checkout") + a named scheduled-heartbeat
  carve-out pointing at the two workflows.
- `doc: skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` § 0 and
  `doc: skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md` § 0 — each carries a pointer back to the
  carve-out so a reader of either side reaches the other.

## Consumes

- `doc: skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` (post-trim state) <- ac-vx8p — the provenance trim
  frees net-growth headroom in the same file this bead edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both `no worktrees` / `deliberately rejected` hits in `skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` sit
   inside text that NAMES the scope (concurrent pipeline ceremonies sharing one checkout)
   rather than stating an unqualified ban.
2. That same text names the scheduled-heartbeat carve-out, and both
   `skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` § 0 and
   `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md` § 0 carry a pointer back to it — a reader landing
   on either side reaches the other.
3. Neither workflow's worktree instruction is deleted or weakened.
4. `./lint.sh` exits 0 with 0 failures, and Check 14 PASSes for
   `skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` (net-neutral-or-shrinking, or its own `net-growth-ok:`
   stamp added in the same diff).

Commands for each are in `## Test Scope`.

## Test Scope

No executable harness — markdown canon; grep is the verification surface. All baselines
below RE-MEASURED at refine time (2026-08-03), not carried from filing.

- `grep -n "no worktrees\|deliberately rejected" skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` — currently
  2 hits, both unqualified. AFTER: both hits must sit inside text that names the scope
  (pipeline ceremonies) rather than an unqualified ban. RED now: neither hit contains a
  scope qualifier.
- `grep -rn "worktree" skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md`
  — currently 18 and 24 hits respectively (both workflows carry the pattern). AFTER: each
  file must additionally contain a pointer to the ac-pipeline carve-out. RED now: neither
  file mentions ac-pipeline's invariant.
- `./lint.sh` — must exit 0 with **0 failures**. Re-measured at refine time: `lint: 372
  checks, 0 failures`, exit 0. **Do not assert the check COUNT** — it drifts hourly as the
  registry grows (this bead previously claimed 314); assert `0 failures` + exit 0 only.
- Check 14 specifically must PASS for `skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` — read its line in
  lint.sh output; a net-positive edit without the file's own `net-growth-ok:` stamp HARD
  FAILs.
- No QA modality (doc-canon only).
close_reason: Implemented and tested. ac-pipeline's worktree invariant narrowed to concurrent pipeline ceremonies sharing one checkout; scheduled-heartbeat carve-out named with pointers both ways; neither workflow's worktree instruction weakened. lint.sh: 390 checks, 0 failures, exit 0; Check 14 net 0 for ac-pipeline/SKILL.md. Delivered: skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md, skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md, skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md. Commit 11a10e2

title: pipeline-proposal exclusion is bead-semantics canon written into ac-tidy's workflow core (3 sites)
description:
discovered-from: ac-tidy-tier2-gate-unsound-7ba

## Problem

Two independent review lenses (architecture, doctrine-delta) flagged the same placement
defect at `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md`.

The rule "beads carrying the `pipeline-proposal` label are EXCLUDED from `N_matching` /
`N_closed`" is **bead-semantics domain canon**, not ac-tidy workflow ordering. It answers
"what does this label mean and what may count it as proof" — true in any workflow that
counts beads as evidence. The `pipeline-proposal` label is already consumed by `ac-align`,
`ac-human-session`, and `ac-dashboard`.

It was restated in ac-tidy's SKILL.md core at three sites instead of being registered once
in `skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md`'s label table and cited.

This is the repo's own workflow/domain litmus
(`skills/skill-builder/references/structure-standard.md` § "The workflow/domain litmus"):

> **Would this sentence be true in ANY workflow?** -> it is DOMAIN CANON: it lives in the
> domain's OWNING skill's references/ ... never in a workflow skill's text.

## Which sites are in scope (refine-corrected — the filing's count was wrong)

`grep -c "pipeline-proposal" skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` returns **5**, not 3. Two of those
hits are label-EMISSION mentions and are **OUT of scope** — they name what ac-tidy emits,
which is genuine workflow content:

- the Tier-3 bullet ("emit a proposal file + a `human-gate,pipeline-proposal` bead")
- the NIGHTLY Tier-3 section ("emit one `human-gate,pipeline-proposal` bead per cluster")

The three IN-SCOPE restatements are the ones asserting the exclusion rule. Select them
with the exclusion wording, not the label name:

`grep -c "EXCLUDED from both\|EXCLUDES every" skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` -> **3** (verified
at refine time): the NIGHTLY Guardrails "Positive proof" bullet, Phase 2b, and Phase 2c.

## Fix shape

1. Register `pipeline-proposal` in `bead-conventions.md`'s label table with its semantics,
   including "never counts as implementation proof — it names a plan, it does not
   implement one."
2. Reduce ac-tidy's three restatements to a one-liner naming the *when/who* plus a `§`
   pointer to the canon (the litmus's WORKFLOW BINDING form).

Not auto-fixed at filing: it edits `beads-standards` canon owned by another domain and it
is a three-site collapse — a placement decision, not a typo.

## Delivers

- `doc: skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` — a `pipeline-proposal` row
  in the label table carrying the "never counts as implementation proof" semantics.
- `doc: skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` — the three exclusion restatements collapsed to one
  workflow-binding line + `§` pointer at the canon.

## Consumes

- none (no blocker; `bead-conventions.md` and `ac-tidy/SKILL.md` both exist at HEAD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md`'s label table gains a
   `pipeline-proposal` row whose Meaning cell carries the phrase "never counts as
   implementation proof".
2. The three exclusion restatements in `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` collapse to ONE workflow
   binding line naming the when/who plus a `§` pointer to that canon row.
3. The two label-EMISSION mentions in `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` (Tier-3 bullet, NIGHTLY
   Tier-3) are UNCHANGED — they are workflow content, not restatements.
4. The gate's behaviour is unchanged: Phase 2b and Phase 2c each still reach the exclusion
   rule, directly or via the pointer.
5. `./lint.sh` exits 0 with 0 failures.

Commands for each are in `## Test Scope`.

## Test Scope

No executable harness — markdown canon; grep is the verification surface. All baselines
RE-MEASURED at refine time (2026-08-03).

- `grep -c "pipeline-proposal" skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` —
  must return >=1 (the label-table registration). **RED baseline re-verified at refine
  time: returns 0.**
- **Semantic AC (guards the false-green above).** Presence of the label STRING is not
  proof the row carries the meaning this bead exists to record — an empty row passes the
  grep above while missing the goal entirely. So also require:
  `grep -c "never counts as implementation proof" skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md`
  -> must be **>=1**. RED baseline EXECUTED at refine time: **0**. The new row goes in the
  existing label table, whose header is `| Label | Meaning |` (verified present).
- `grep -c "EXCLUDED from both\|EXCLUDES every" skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` — must drop from
  **3 to 1** (the surviving workflow binding). **Baseline re-verified at refine time: 3.**
  Use THIS command, not `grep -c "pipeline-proposal"` — that one returns 5 and counts the
  two out-of-scope emission mentions, so it can never reach 1 without deleting real
  workflow content.
- `grep -c "pipeline-proposal" skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md` — must remain **>=3** afterwards
  (2 emission mentions + >=1 in the surviving binding/pointer). This is the guard against
  over-collapsing.
- The gate's BEHAVIOUR must not change: the exclusion must still bind at every site that
  defines "matching". Re-read Phase 2b and Phase 2c after the collapse and confirm each
  still reaches the rule (directly or via the pointer).
- `./lint.sh` — must exit 0 with **0 failures**. Re-measured at refine time: `lint: 372
  checks, 0 failures`, exit 0. Do not assert the check COUNT (the filing's 314 was already
  stale within a day) — assert `0 failures` + exit 0.
- No QA modality (doc-canon only).

title: bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh executes unvalidated text extracted from SKILL.md
description:
discovered-from: ac-wno

## Problem

`skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` (added by ac-wno as the seam
proof for ac-implement's per-child bead-work key) greps the live `CHILD_ID=` and
`ARTIFACTS_DIR=` assignment lines out of `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` and splices that
raw markdown text directly into a `bash -c "..."` / `zsh -c "..."` payload, then executes
it (Cases 1-3), with no validation of what was extracted.

This is eval-of-markdown-content: if either SKILL.md line is ever edited to contain
something other than the expected `tr -cd` expression, the test executes it as arbitrary
shell, unconditionally, whenever the test runs.

## The tension (both reviewers are partly right — resolve, do not just patch)

The security lens rates this Medium. The test-quality lens independently praised the same
property: the script reads the **real on-disk file** rather than a retyped copy, which is
exactly why its sabotage probes convict (reverting the SKILL.md derivation turns the test
RED). Naively replacing the extraction with a hardcoded copy would destroy the seam proof
and reintroduce drift — do not do that.

The resolution is to keep reading the real file but **validate before executing**: assert
the extracted lines match the expected shape and hard-fail with a clear message if they do
not. That preserves the drift-detection property AND removes the arbitrary-execution path
— a mismatch becomes a loud test failure instead of silent execution.

Threat model is honest: the actor must already be able to edit registry skill text. Hence
P3 — this is hardening of a test harness, not a live exploit.

## Approach (advisory)

Anchor the shape assertion on the two extracted lines' stable prefixes. Both were
re-verified present in `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` at refine time (2026-08-03) — grep
them, do not trust a line number:

- `grep -n 'CHILD_ID="\$(printf' skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md`
- `grep -n 'ARTIFACTS_DIR="/tmp/bead-work-' skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md`

**Be precise about "expected shape" — the sanctioned lines DO contain metacharacters.**
Both lines were read at refine time and the `CHILD_ID=` line legitimately contains a
**pipe** (`| command tr -cd ...`) inside its command substitution, so a blanket
"no metacharacters" rule would reject the correct text and the guard would never pass.
The two live lines, verbatim at refine time:

    CHILD_ID="$(printf '%s' "${AGENT_NAME:-anon}" | command tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9')-$$"
    ARTIFACTS_DIR="/tmp/bead-work-${CLAIM_ID}-${CHILD_ID}${RUN_ID:+-$RUN_ID}"

Preferred implementation: **whole-line allow-list by regex** — assert each extracted line
matches a pattern describing the whole expected assignment, rather than blocklisting
characters. A whole-line match makes the pipe question moot and cannot be defeated by a
metacharacter the blocklist forgot. If a blocklist is used instead, `|` MUST be explicitly
permitted inside the sanctioned `$( ... )` and the blocklist must still reject `;`, `&&`,
`||`, backticks, redirects, and any second command substitution.

## Delivers

- `file: skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` — a shape-validation
  guard that runs on the text extracted from `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` BEFORE any
  `bash -c` / `zsh -c` execution, hard-failing with a named message on mismatch.
- `test: bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` new negative case proving the guard fires
  (substituted text is reported, never executed).

## Consumes

- none (the script and `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` both exist at HEAD; no blocker).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` validates the shape of the
   text it extracts from `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` BEFORE any `bash -c` / `zsh -c`
   execution, and hard-fails with a named message on mismatch.
2. The validation accepts the two CURRENT sanctioned lines verbatim — including the pipe
   inside the `CHILD_ID=` command substitution.
3. A new negative case proves the guard: substituted text is REPORTED, never executed.
4. The seam proof survives — the existing sabotage probes (Cases 0, 1, 3, 4) still turn the
   test RED when their targets are reverted. The script still reads the real on-disk file;
   it is NOT replaced with a hardcoded copy.
5. `bash skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` exits 0 on an
   unmodified tree; `./lint.sh` exits 0 with 0 failures.

Commands for each are in `## Test Scope`.

## Test Scope

`skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` is itself the harness; it is
directly runnable and must stay green. Baselines RE-MEASURED at refine time (2026-08-03).

- `bash skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh` — **exit 0**.
  Re-verified at refine time by EXECUTING it: exit 0, final line "All bead-work sibling-
  collision + seam assertions passed." (all 5 cases, incl. Case 4 doctrine half).
- **New negative case (the fix's own regression proof, and this bead's bite-proof):** in a
  disposable `git worktree add`, rewrite the `CHILD_ID=` line in
  `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` to an unexpected-but-harmless shape and re-run — the
  script must exit non-zero with the new shape-validation message, and the substituted
  text must NOT be executed. A guard that cannot be shown RED is not a guard.
- **Seam must survive:** re-run the existing sabotage probes — reverting the ac-implement
  derivation must still turn the test RED (Cases 0, 1, 3), and reverting `run-id.md`'s
  wording must still turn Case 4 RED. If either goes green, the fix destroyed the proof.
  This is the anti-regression on the "just hardcode a copy" failure mode.
- `./lint.sh` — exit 0, **0 failures** (re-measured at refine time: 372 checks, 0
  failures; assert 0-failures + exit 0, never the drifting check count).
- No QA modality (script-level, no user-facing surface).
close_reason: Implemented and tested. Case 0a whole-line allow-list validates both extracted assignments (accepting the sanctioned pipe) before any bash -c/zsh -c; Case 0b proves unsanctioned text is reported and never executed (sentinel absent). Script still reads the real on-disk file — no hardcoded copy. Probes: unexpected CHILD_ID shape -> exit 1 with the named guard message, Cases 1-3 not run; reverted ARTIFACTS_DIR derivation -> Case 0 + 0a RED; reverted run-id.md wording -> Case 4 RED. Unmodified tree: exit 0, lint 0 failures. Delivered: skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh. Commit 228101d
