title: ac-loop + shell-guardrails: hardcoded .claude/ script path at ac-loop/SKILL.md:383, and shell-guardrails.md wrongly claims append trips the dcg truncate rule
description:
discovered-from: ac-vqf (the sibling defect; ac-vqf's close note records AC6 "skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md:383 deliberately UNTOUCHED — tracked separately as ac-ji5") and ac-d4r. Surfaced during ac-bead-refine RUN 20260803-113231-34132, child FuchsiaWolfRefineB, while verifying those two beads' premises.

Two verified defects, deliberately held OUT of scope of ac-vqf and ac-d4r so those beads stayed single-file.

**SPLIT VERDICT (refine round 1, RUN 20260803-113231-34132, 3/3 reviewers independently concurring): DO NOT SPLIT.** A sibling run's round-2 reviewers proposed splitting this into one bead per defect. Judged against the documented thresholds (`ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` § Agent 3: split candidates touch >5 files or span multiple concerns; merge candidates are <30 min with no dependents): both halves are one-to-few-line documentation edits, in one repo, with no dependency between them, no dependents, and a single shared verification gate (`./lint.sh`). A split buys no sequencing and no parallelism — the same agent does both in one sitting — while costing two full bead bodies with duplicated Test Scope. Do not re-open this.

**(1) `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md:383` hardcodes a `.claude/` script path** — same defect class as ac-vqf. It builds the gate-script path as `$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh`; in agent-compounds (the canonical registry) the script lives at `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh`, so the invocation fails from this repo. Verified at HEAD 2026-08-03: line 383 is the ONLY invocation site of that script anywhere under `skills/` (grep-verified); `.claude/skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh` does not exist here, `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh` does (mode 755). Fix mirrors ac-vqf's pinned decision: probe-both-roots, registry layout preferred, harness layout as fallback.

**`PROJECT_ROOT` MUST be re-derived at the invocation site (refine round 1 correction — this is ac-vqf's round-3 lesson, and it is not optional).** `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md` sets `PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` at `:143` ONLY, bare and unexported, in a different fenced bash block from `:383` — and the very line above `:383` says "re-assert in THIS call — exports don't persist across bash calls". ac-vqf reproduced exactly this: with `PROJECT_ROOT` unset the both-roots probe resolved to `/.claude/...` and exited 2, i.e. the same failure class moved one variable later. Use the mint-if-absent shape.

**(2) `skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md:17` overstates the dcg rule on TWO counts.** It states that `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path` fires on a stdout redirect "truncating or appending, and on a heredoc-fed one". Both halves are empirically FALSE against **dcg 0.6.7**. Full probe matrix, EXECUTED 2026-08-03 (all targets variable-built):

| probed command | result |
| --- | --- |
| `echo hello > "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/probe.txt"` | **BLOCKED** (`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path`) |
| `echo hello >> "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/probe.txt"` | **ALLOWED** |
| `{ echo a; echo b; } >> "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/dump.txt"` | **ALLOWED** |
| `cat > "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/x.md" <<'EOF' … EOF` | **BLOCKED** |
| `cat >> "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/x.md" <<'EOF' … EOF` | **ALLOWED** |

The rule keys on **TRUNCATION ONLY**. Appending is never blocked, and a heredoc is NOT an independent trigger — a heredoc-fed *append* passes. dcg's own explain text actively lists "Use append (>>) when preserving existing content is acceptable" as a SAFER ALTERNATIVE, so the doc steers authors away from a shape the guard itself recommends, and it is canon other skills cite.

**(3) The same false claim is PROPAGATED at `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md:224-227`** (found by this refine pass, 2026-08-03; not in the original filing). It reads "append via `tee -a`, **NOT a brace-group append-redirect**. `dcg` blocks a redirect whose target path is variable-built". The brace-group append probe above disproves both the prohibition and its justification. The `tee -a` shape stays a perfectly good recommendation — what must go is the false claim that the alternative is BLOCKED. (The historical 3-of-4-children block that note cites was almost certainly the *truncating* init write on the line below it, not the append.)

**SCOPE FENCE for defect (3) — do NOT mass-edit.** The phrase "the guard blocks a redirect whose target path is variable-built" also appears at `ac-plan-clean/references/workflow.md:64`, `ac-plan-refine-internal/references/workflow.md:64`, `ac-plan-refine-external/references/workflow.md:97`, `ac-hygiene/SKILL.md:98` and `ac-merge/SKILL.md:289`. Each of those describes a **truncating** write and is therefore CORRECT in context. Only `ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` applies the claim to an APPEND, which is what makes it false there. Leave the other five alone.

## Delivers

- doc: `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md:383` — gate-script path resolved by a both-roots probe off a re-derived `PROJECT_ROOT`, no single hardcoded `.claude/` path
- doc: `skills/ac-pipeline/references/shell-guardrails.md:17` — the "truncating or appending" claim corrected to truncating-only, recording the measured dcg 0.6.7 append result
- doc: `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md:224-227` — the propagated "dcg blocks a redirect whose target path is variable-built" justification corrected to the truncating form only (the `tee -a` recommendation stays)

## Consumes

title: ac-review trunk-direct scope: stale review-mark (weeks old) with no Range: lines in prior reports needs an explicit fallback rule
description:
discovered-from: ac-znk.2

Observed RUN 20260802-084558-9799 (ac-znk.2): the review-mark (last commit touching `.claude/reviews/batch/`) had been stale since 2026-07-19 and the prior reports lacked `Range:` lines, so since-mark scope would have swept two weeks of already-reviewed commits. The child fell back to the conductor-supplied batch definition by judgment. `ac-review/SKILL.md`'s only documented fallback is the `v*`-tag bootstrap, and it fires **only when no mark exists at all**. Document an explicit stale-mark fallback ladder in ac-review's Scope Detection section.

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03; the filing carried no anchors)

- Scope Detection is `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` § "Scope Detection (dual-mode, CRITICAL)" (`:131` on 2026-08-03 — grep the heading, do not pin the number; this file is under concurrent edit).
- `REVIEW_MARK=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- .claude/reviews/batch/)`, then `if [ -n "$REVIEW_MARK" ]; then DIFF_RANGE="$REVIEW_MARK..HEAD"; else` v*-tag bootstrap. **There is no staleness test anywhere.** A stale-but-present mark takes the `$REVIEW_MARK..HEAD` branch unconditionally. Premise CONFIRMED exactly as filed.
- The pieces the ladder needs already exist and must be REUSED, not re-invented:
  - `skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md` § Scan D already computes `MARK_AGE_DAYS` and publishes a shared **staleness classification** (`ALARM` when `MARK_AGE_DAYS > 7`), explicitly annotated "the same 7-day line `ac-review` § Standing weekly review already draws". Scan D also computes the union of recorded `Range:` claims across `.claude/reviews`. `ac-review/SKILL.md` already cites board-scan.md (3 hits) and already names Scan D as the true coverage source ("this probe measures ACCEPTANCE, never coverage").
  - Every report carries a mandatory, machine-parsed `**Range:** <base>..<head>` line (§ Report Destination), so rung 2 below has a guaranteed data source.
  - `ac-loop` already prints Scan D's staleness verdict every run and files a P1 review-blackout bead on `ALARM` (board-scan.md § consumers). So the ladder must consume that signal, NOT mint a second trigger.
- **Ownership fence (must not be violated by the fix).** § "Standing weekly review of `main`" states the >7-days-no-batch standing review belongs to the weekly `ac-hygiene PANEL=full` run, and that ac-review owns only the *mechanism*. This bead adds a SCOPE fallback used when ac-review is invoked; it must NOT make ac-review self-trigger or self-schedule a standing review. Exactly one owner.

## The ladder (pinned at refine — rung order is a decision, not a suggestion)

When `REVIEW_MARK` is present but STALE (`MARK_AGE_DAYS > 7`, reusing board-scan.md's shared threshold — do not fork the definition):

1. **Conductor-supplied batch range**, if one was handed down with the invocation. Highest precedence: an explicit human/conductor scope beats any inference.
2. Else **narrow using Scan D's already-covered set, expressed as a RANGE.** Run board-scan.md § Scan D, take the commit set it writes to `$D/uncovered` (`comm -23 inrange covered`), and set `DIFF_RANGE="<oldest commit in $D/uncovered>^..HEAD"`. Rationale: coverage, not acceptance, determines what still needs reviewing, and reports written to the non-mark-advancing destinations (`.claude/reviews/` root, `pending/`) are full-weight coverage per bd-zl1y5 — exactly what a stale mark cannot see. **This range may re-include already-covered commits in the middle; that is accepted.** Over-inclusion is safe; silent under-inclusion is not.

   > **It MUST be a range, not a set (refine round 3).** An earlier draft told the reviewer to "review the commit SET, not a range". That is unimplementable: every downstream consumer of `DIFF_RANGE` in `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` (10 call sites — `git diff $DIFF_RANGE`, `git log $DIFF_RANGE`, and reviewer-prompt interpolation) treats it as a literal `base..head` string. The `^..HEAD` form above is therefore the PRIMARY instruction, not an escape hatch. Guard the degenerate cases: if `$D/uncovered` is EMPTY there is nothing to review (say so and exit, do not fall through to a wider rung); if its oldest commit is a root commit, `^` has no parent — use the commit itself.

   > **Refine round-2 correction — the earlier draft of this rung was WRONG and the error is recorded so it is not re-introduced.** It said "the head of the newest recorded `Range:` claim that is a descendant of `REVIEW_MARK`". Scan D computes no such value: reading its script, it emits `MARK`, `MARK_AGE_DAYS`, `BASE`, `ACCEPT_GAP`, the files `$D/ranges` / `$D/covered` / `$D/inrange` / `$D/uncovered`, and the counts `UNCOVERED` / `CODEISH` — there is no ranked "newest descendant head" anywhere. Specifying a field the producer does not emit is precisely the false-dependency shape refine exists to catch.
   >
   > **The rebase / force-push hole is already closed upstream — cite it, do not re-implement it.** Scan D builds `covered` with `git rev-list "$r" 2>/dev/null`, so a `Range:` naming a rewritten or unknown SHA is silently DROPPED, and board-scan.md states the design intent in-line: "Both choices UNDER-credit coverage: this probe fails loud, never silently green." A dropped claim therefore *widens* scope, which is the safe direction. Adding a second ancestry test in ac-review would duplicate a guarantee the producer already makes.

3. Else **keep `$REVIEW_MARK..HEAD` unchanged and surface the staleness loudly** (print Scan D's `ALARM`). The `v*` tag is NOT a rung.

**Rung 3 — the reasoning was reversed at round 2 and RESTORED at round 3. Read this before "improving" it again.** The filing proposed a `v*`-tag rung. Round 2 objected that a tag can be NEWER than a stale mark (true: `git describe --tags --match 'v*' --abbrev=0` returns the nearest tag reachable from HEAD, tracking RELEASE cadence, not review cadence) and the draft was changed to "take the newer of the two". **That was wrong and is retracted.** `DIFF_RANGE` is `BASE..HEAD`, so a NEWER base yields a NARROWER range: `tag..HEAD` is a strict subset of `mark..HEAD`. A release tag postdating the mark proves a release happened — it proves NOTHING about whether the commits between the mark and the tag were reviewed. Adopting it would silently DROP genuinely-unreviewed commits, which is the exact failure this bead exists to prevent, and the `ALARM` print does not compensate (it flags staleness, not the excluded gap).

The invariant: **narrow only on evidence of coverage.** Rung 2 has that evidence (Scan D's recorded `Range:` claims); rung 3 by definition does not, so it must not narrow at all. With no coverage evidence, WIDE is the correct conservative answer — the defect was never "scope is too wide", it was "scope is wide with no signal that it is wide". Hence: keep the mark, print the `ALARM`. (The existing `v*`-tag bootstrap stays exactly where it is, serving its own separate case: no mark exists at all.)

## Honest limit of this ladder — read before implementing (refine round 4)

**Rung 2 provides ZERO narrowing in the literal reported scenario, and the doc must say so.** ac-znk.2's incident had prior reports with **no `Range:` lines at all**. Traced through Scan D: with no `Range:` claims, `$D/ranges` is empty, so `$D/covered` is empty, so `$D/uncovered = comm -23 inrange covered` is the ENTIRE stale set — and `<oldest uncovered>^..HEAD` reduces to exactly `REVIEW_MARK..HEAD`, i.e. rung 3's behavior. The empty-uncovered guard never fires either, because the set is full, not empty.

So: **rung 2 mitigates the case where reviews DID record `Range:` lines to non-mark-advancing destinations. Rung 1 — the conductor-supplied range — is what actually resolved the reported incident**, and the ladder correctly ranks it first. This is not a defect: the fall-through behavior stays safe (wide scope + a loud `ALARM`), which is the conservative direction. But the shipped text must state the limit plainly rather than implying the ladder solves a case it does not, and it should note that the durable fix for the reported class is upstream — every report carrying its mandatory `**Range:**` line, which `ac-review` § Report Destination already requires (bd-zl1y5).

## Delivers

- doc: `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` § Scope Detection — an explicit stale-mark fallback ladder (rungs 1-3 above) keyed on board-scan.md's shared `MARK_AGE_DAYS > 7` threshold, carrying (a) a statement that the >7-day standing review remains `ac-hygiene`'s to schedule and that this ladder only affects scope resolution for an invocation already under way, and (b) the honest-limit note above — that rung 2 collapses to rung 3 when no `Range:` claims exist at all, so rung 1 is the mitigation for that case

## Consumes

- none

Every input the ladder reads — `MARK_AGE_DAYS`, the staleness classification, Scan D's `Range:`-claim union, and the mandatory `**Range:**` line — exists in the tree at HEAD (grep-verified above). `board-scan.md` is READ, not modified, so there is no upstream blocker and no `blocks` edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

Commands below were EXECUTED against HEAD on 2026-08-03; RED-now values are measured.

1. The ladder reuses board-scan's threshold rather than inventing one: `grep -c 'MARK_AGE_DAYS' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns at least 1 (RED now: **0** — executed). A hardcoded literal `7` with no reference to board-scan.md's shared classification FAILS this AC — the point is one definition of "stale", not two.
2. All three rungs are documented in precedence order, and the ordering is CHECKABLE, not just asserted. Executable check: `grep -n 'conductor-supplied\|uncovered\|ALARM' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md | head -3` must return the three rung markers in that order (conductor rung first, Scan-D rung second, ALARM rung third) within the Scope Detection section. **And the retracted rung must not reappear:** `grep -ci 'newer of' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns 0, and the new text must not name `git describe` as a stale-mark fallback (the existing no-mark bootstrap use of `git describe` is unchanged and does not count — check that `grep -c 'git describe' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` has not INCREASED from its pre-edit value — record that value at the start of work rather than trusting this bead, since the file is under concurrent edit; it measured **2** on 2026-08-03).
2a. **Rung 2 names only fields Scan D actually emits.** Every identifier the new text attributes to Scan D must appear in `skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md` — check each one: `grep -c 'uncovered' skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md` returns at least 1 (currently **4** — executed). Conversely, the text must NOT claim a ranked "newest descendant head", which Scan D does not compute: `grep -ci 'newest.*descendant' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns 0. This AC exists because that exact non-existent field was drafted and caught at refine round 2.
3. **The ownership fence holds.** The new text states that the >7-day standing review remains `ac-hygiene PANEL=full`'s duty and that this ladder does not self-trigger one. Check: the existing "Standing weekly review" section survives unedited (`grep -c 'ac-hygiene' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` does not decrease from its pre-edit value; record that value before starting). This AC exists because the obvious wrong implementation is to add a staleness trigger that quietly duplicates ac-hygiene's job.
4. **Scope honesty — this bead is DOC-ONLY and must say so.** The existing `REVIEW_MARK` / `DIFF_RANGE` bash block is NOT changed by this bead; only prose describing how a conductor or Scan-D input resolves scope is added. Consequently there is no runtime seam to drive, and no fixture is required. The seam risk that DOES exist — the ladder naming fields Scan D does not actually publish — is covered by AC 1's grep against the literal `MARK_AGE_DAYS` name board-scan.md defines, plus a manual read-back confirming every field the new text names appears in board-scan.md's § Scan D output schema. **If the implementer instead chooses to change the bash block, this AC is void and AC 3 of ac-nsb's shape applies: a fixture proving the stale path selects differently from the fresh path is then mandatory.**
5. **lint Check 14 (no-net-growth, per-file) — and a diet interaction worth knowing.** `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` is a conductor SKILL.md under the ratchet and is currently **1061 lines**, the LARGEST in the conductor tier. It is simultaneously the blocker for ac-gcj.11's Check-15 ceiling ratchet, which needs the conductor max at **<= 1000**. So: **prefer landing this edit net <= 0 lines on that file (offset the addition with a cut, or put the ladder detail in `references/`) over adding a `net-growth-ok:` stamp.** A stamp is permitted by lint but pushes ac-gcj.11 further out of reach. Verify: `git diff --numstat -- skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` shows net <= 0, or the diff carries a fresh added `<!-- net-growth-ok: <reason> -->` line.
6. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the EXIT CODE only — never the check count.** The count drifts constantly in this shared checkout (`314` at 13:00 on 2026-08-03, `372` an hour later after siblings landed a new check).

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` — § "Scope Detection (dual-mode, CRITICAL)" (the `REVIEW_MARK=` block and its `if/else`), and § "Standing weekly review of `main`" (the ownership fence, must survive). Locate by heading/grep, not line number.
- `skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md` — § Scan D: `MARK_AGE_DAYS`, the staleness classification table, the `Range:`-claim union, and the output schema. READ-ONLY reference; this bead must not edit it.
- No test harness exists or is required for a doc-only change (see AC 4). `grep` + `./lint.sh` + the AC-3 read-back ARE the verification surface. If the implementer changes runtime bash instead, AC 4 mandates a fixture.
- `./lint.sh` — Check 14 leg for AC 5, whole run for AC 6.

Delivered: skills/ac-review/SKILL.md § Scope Detection — stale-mark fallback ladder (rungs 1-3) keyed on board-scan.md § Scan D's shared MARK_AGE_DAYS > 7 threshold, with the ownership fence (standing review stays ac-hygiene PANEL=full's) and the honest-limit note (rung 2 reduces to rung 3 when no Range: claims exist; rung 1 is the mitigation). Doc-only, per AC 4 — the REVIEW_MARK/DIFF_RANGE bash block is unchanged, so no fixture required. title: Preamble paste-instruction anchor absent from prompt body (2 sites remain: explorers.md + engineer-fix-prompt.md)
description:
discovered-from: ac-syct

The child-spawn preamble paste-instruction names an insertion anchor that does NOT exist
in the child prompt body at some sites. An agent following the instruction literally
cannot find the insertion point, which risks reproducing the very inert-preamble failure
ac-08k/ac-syct were filed to fix.

## Remaining broken sites — RE-MEASURED at refine time (2026-08-03), ac-syct now CLOSED

The filing predates ac-syct's 12-site roll. Refine re-ran the check across the whole live
corpus (`grep -rl "ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT (non-negotiable)" skills/` -> 15 files) and the
result differs from the filing in both directions. **This list supersedes the filing's.**

1. `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` — **STILL BROKEN** (as filed). Its
   instruction names the anchor `First: read AGENTS.md`; the phrase occurs only in that
   instruction and never after it, while the file carries three `Task(...)` prompt bodies.
2. `skills/ac-review/references/engineer-fix-prompt.md` — **BROKEN, NOT IN THE FILING.**
   This is a 7th site of the same class, delivered by ac-syct's roll TODAY and shipped
   with the defect. Its instruction names `First: read AGENTS.md`; the body says
   `Read AGENTS.md for project context.` instead. An implementer working the filing's
   two-item list would ship an incomplete fix.

**Removed from scope by re-measurement:** `skills/ac-plan-refine-external/references/workflow.md`
is **NOT** broken — its instruction names a third phrasing (the fenced block *beginning*
`You are making a single targeted edit to a plan document.`) and that phrase does occur in
the body. Two earlier drafts of the audit below false-positived on it; see the Test Scope
note. `skills/ac-plan-refine-internal/references/workflow.md` is likewise fine (anchor
present in all nine bodies) — its only defect is wording ("`Task(...)` prompts" when the
prompt is a separate fenced block above the call). Wording-only, lowest priority, optional.

`skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` is the canon source, governs no
local body, and is legitimately exempt.

## The AC gap that let this ship (item 3 — the durable half)

ac-syct's close evidence recorded "byte-identical 21-line canon block (AC2 diff empty on
all 12); N matches fence count per file" — it verified block identity and Task-block COUNT
but never that the named anchor exists in the target body. Same root cause as wave 2
(ac-08k): the site was verified by CONSTRUCTION, not by FUNCTION. Three waves, same class.

The durable fix is a runnable check, not a promise. Refine has WRITTEN AND EXECUTED it
(below); the deliverable is to commit it.

Note: the DOCTRINE fix that would prevent the class generally is a separate human-gate
decision, ac-ewgr.7 under epic ac-ewgr — not this bead.

## Delivers

- `doc: skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` — anchor reconciled (either add the
  named phrase to each of the three prompt bodies, or reword the instruction to name each
  body's real opening line, matching how the six already-fixed sites were handled).
- `doc: skills/ac-review/references/engineer-fix-prompt.md` — same, for its one body.
- `file: skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/preamble-anchor-audit.test.sh` — the executable
  anchor audit below, exit 0 only when every carrier's named anchor occurs in the body it
  governs.

## Consumes

- none (ac-syct is CLOSED; all target files exist at HEAD).

## Approach (advisory) — the audit script, verified

Refine wrote and RAN this; it currently exits 1 naming exactly the two sites above, and
exits 0 once they are fixed. Position-based by design (see Test Scope).

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 2
    rc=0
    for f in $(grep -rl "ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT (non-negotiable)" skills/ | sort); do
      case "$f" in *delegation-contract.md) continue;; esac
      cline=$(grep -n 'ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT (non-negotiable)' "$f" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
      hdr=$(sed -n "1,${cline}p" "$f" | tr '\n' ' ')
      anchor=$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | grep -o 'above its *`[^`]*`' | head -1 | sed 's/above its *`//; s/`$//')
      [ -n "$anchor" ] || anchor=$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | grep -o 'above the *`[^`]*`' | head -1 | sed 's/above the *`//; s/`$//')
      [ -n "$anchor" ] || anchor=$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | grep -o 'beginning *`[^`]*`' | head -1 | sed 's/beginning *`//; s/`$//')
      if [ -z "$anchor" ]; then echo "NO-ANCHOR-NAMED  $f"; rc=1; continue; fi
      probe=${anchor%…}
      last=$(grep -nF "$probe" "$f" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1)
      if [ -z "$last" ] || [ "$last" -le "$cline" ]; then
        echo "BROKEN  $f  anchor=[$probe]"; rc=1
      else echo "ok      $f  anchor=[$probe] (body hit at line $last)"; fi
    done
    exit $rc

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` and
   `skills/ac-review/references/engineer-fix-prompt.md` each have their paste-instruction
   anchor reconciled with the prompt body it governs — either the named phrase is added to
   each body, or the instruction is reworded to name each body's real opening line.
2. `skills/ac-plan-refine-external/references/workflow.md` is NOT modified — it is already
   correct; two earlier check drafts false-positived on it.
3. The audit script ships at `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/preamble-anchor-audit.test.sh`,
   is position-based (not occurrence-count-based), and recognises all three instruction
   phrasings including the ellipsis-truncated form.
4. Running that script exits 0 with zero BROKEN lines and accounts for all 14 governed
   carriers.
5. `./lint.sh` exits 0 with 0 failures.

Commands and the RED baseline are in `## Test Scope`.

## Test Scope

Grep-verifiable, no runtime. Baselines RE-MEASURED at refine time by EXECUTION.

- **Primary AC — run the audit above.** RED baseline pasted from the refine-time run:
  exit 1, with exactly two BROKEN lines —
  `skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` and
  `skills/ac-review/references/engineer-fix-prompt.md` — and twelve `ok` lines. GREEN
  target: **exit 0, zero BROKEN lines.** This is the bead's sole evidence, and it is
  bite-proof: it is currently RED and names the two sites.
- **The check MUST be position-based, not count-based.** Refine's first two drafts used
  "anchor occurs more than once" and BOTH false-positived on
  `skills/ac-plan-refine-external/references/workflow.md`, whose instruction line-wraps the
  anchor so the joined phrase matches only the body. A count-based check would send an
  implementer to "fix" a file that is already correct. Assert the anchor occurs at a line
  AFTER the first `ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT` line.
- **All three instruction phrasings must be recognised** — `above its X line`,
  `above the X opening line` (anchor may end in an ellipsis, which must be stripped before
  grepping), and `the fenced block beginning X`. A check handling only the first reports
  six false NO-ANCHOR-NAMED results; refine hit exactly that.
- `grep -c "First: read AGENTS.md" skills/ac-plan-init/references/explorers.md` — currently
  1 (the instruction, before the contract block at line 9); its three `Task(` bodies carry
  none. Must rise, or the instruction must be reworded.
- `./lint.sh` at repo root — exit 0, **0 failures**. Re-measured at refine time: 372
  checks, 0 failures. These are `references/` files so the no-net-growth SKILL.md gate does
  not bind; run it anyway. Assert 0-failures + exit 0, never the drifting check count.
- No QA modality (doc-canon + script).

## SPLIT APPLIED (refine 2026-08-03) — this bead is now an EPIC

The filing's own body said "~520 judgments. SPLIT IT: this is several sittings, not one bead"
and named a 4-way batching. Refine executed that split, then split the two oversized batches
again at the sub-boundaries the filing itself named — **calibrated against the B1 precedent:
ac-gcj.10 covered 6 skills / ~60 judgments and closed in one sitting**, so a batch is sized to
land near that, and any batch that would still self-admit "several sittings" was cut.

| child | family | skills | ~judgments |
| ----- | ------ | -----: | ---------: |
| 1 | `ac-plan-*` | 5 | ~50 |
| 2 | `ac-qa-*` | 2 | ~20 |
| 3 | bead-lifecycle `ac-*` | 6 | ~60 |
| 4 | polish / publish `ac-*` | 4 | ~40 |
| 5 | remaining `ac-*` | 8 | ~80 |
| 6 | domain: agent-system + build-platform | 12 | ~120 |
| 7 | domain: testing / creative / publishing | 15 | ~150 |

5 + 2 + 6 + 4 + 8 + 12 + 15 = **52**, which is `ls -1 skills/*/SKILL.md` (**58**, executed at
HEAD 878a6f1) minus the 6 B1 conductors. Nothing dropped, nothing double-counted, no skill in
two batches (verified by set arithmetic this round). Each child carries its own full
enumeration, so no child needs to re-derive the partition.

**Residual imbalance is acknowledged, not hidden:** children 6 (12) and 7 (15) remain 2x and
2.5x the B1 precedent. They are NOT cut further because the next boundary down would be
arbitrary — each is already a single coherent family. Both say so in their own bodies and
budget two-to-three sittings.

**Dependency note:** the filing's `blocks` edge to ac-gcj.10 was REMOVED by this refine. The
blocker is closed (so the edge was inert) and a `blocks` edge with an epic endpoint is an I2
violation (`beads-standards` § Sequencing & parentage) — and this refine is what makes ac-kqpw
an epic, so keeping the edge would create the violation. ac-gcj.10's contribution survives as
the method below, which is present-tree, not as an edge.

**Children are deliberately NOT chained.** They are genuinely independent — a `blocks` chain
would be a false dependency, since no batch consumes any artifact another batch produces.

**Disjointness — premise corrected (2026-08-04, ac-kqpw.8; traced to source).** This paragraph
previously justified the non-chaining by asserting that ac-loop's file-set disjointness check
already stops two children touching the corpus at once. That over-states it. The mechanism is
real doctrine — `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md`, section "Disjointness check before dispatch — BOTH
tests must pass" (~line 709), whose remedy is literally "any overlap -> serialize those beads
behind each other". **But it is conductor-executed prose covering the ac-loop WIDTH>1 dispatch
path only** — not an automated gate. It does not fire for a human-run session, for a direct
`ac-implement` invocation, or for two independent `ac-loop` sessions. Corroborating: `bv
--robot-plan` carries no file-set data at all (pure dependency-graph antichain grouping) and
groups this epic plus all seven children into one track. So serialization across the seven
batches is a convention the conductor must honor, not a guarantee the children inherit.

Coordination hazard (carried into every child): all seven append to the **same** file,
`skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`. Concrete mitigation — before appending,
re-run the AC 2 awk to see which sections already exist; if a sibling landed since you started,
rebase and re-append rather than resolving in place; after committing, re-run AC 1 to confirm
YOUR family's sections survived. Append-only, one child in flight at a time, minimal
working-tree dwell.

## Method carried forward from B1 (its transferable output — binding on every child)

- **Explicit NOT-for exclusion clauses are what pass.** The only two B1 skills needing no fix
  were the two whose descriptions already carried one. Predicted failure profile: a skill with
  no NOT-for clause AND a generic verb in its trigger list.
- **Weight the negatives toward same-family near-misses.** Every B1 finding came from a
  phrasing sitting between two sibling skills; distant-domain negatives are free passes that
  prove nothing.
- **Expect stale descriptions, not just imprecise ones.** Two of four B1 failures were
  descriptions that had drifted against trunk-direct while their bodies were current.
- **These verdicts are a lower bound.** The judge is the same model being routed, reading its
  own text with the full registry in context — a cold router sees less. Say so in each section.
- Carried observation, unfixed by B1: bare bead-id tokens inside `description:` lines (e.g.
  ac-batch-close's `(bd-pwt44)`) cost router tokens and say nothing to a router. Each child
  sweeps them out of ITS OWN family's descriptions.

## Enumeration rule (binding on every child)

Enumerate from `skills/*/SKILL.md`, **NEVER** from `skills/*/`: `skills/_tools/` is a directory
with no SKILL.md and is not a skill, so a `*/` loop reports a phantom `MISSING _tools` forever
(verified 2026-08-03).

closed"** (`beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` § Types: epics stay open across
batches; do not force-close an epic just because its currently-open children are done). The
close criterion is coverage of `## Delivers`, and that is exactly what AC 1 measures — child
status is not a criterion at all.

- ac-plan-init
- ac-plan-lab

ac-batch-close, ac-merge, ac-land) are already covered and must not be re-judged — re-verified
this round: the corpus holds exactly those 6 sections and none of this family's.

**Sized just under the B1 precedent** (6 skills / ~60 judgments / one sitting), so it should
close in one sitting.

**Highest-value family for negatives:** these five sit closer together than any other group in
the registry (`ac-plan-refine-external` vs `ac-plan-refine-internal` especially). Per B1, every
finding came from a phrasing sitting *between* two siblings — so weight the should-NOT-activate
set heavily toward inter-sibling near-misses here, not toward distant domains.

Description sizes re-measured at HEAD 881e966 with the validator's OWN extractor
(`extract_description` in `validate-skill.sh` — round 2 caught an earlier undercount here):
ac-plan-lab **696**, ac-plan-refine-internal **502**, ac-plan-init **474**, ac-plan-clean
**364**, ac-plan-refine-external **326**. All far under Check 13's 1024 cap — this family
carries no budget constraint, so exclusion clauses can be added freely. Note the cap is
measured on the RAW YAML value INCLUDING its surrounding quotes; all five of these are
single-quoted scalars, in which every literal apostrophe is doubled and costs 2 chars.

## Per-skill work

For each skill above: >= 5 should-activate phrasings + >= 5 should-NOT-activate near-misses,
judged from the frontmatter `description:` **ALONE** (not the body), each carrying a recorded
verdict in the B1 row grammar (`- PASS` / `- FAIL` / `- PASS (after fix)`). Every
precision/recall failure gets a `description:` edit, re-judged afterwards, with both the edit
and the new verdict recorded. **The description must stay on ONE line** (Check 14 is
line-based — see Test Scope).

The epic's carried B1 observation about sweeping bare bead-id tokens out of descriptions
**has already been executed for this family and found nothing** (zero hits across all 17 skills
in B2-B5, 2026-08-04 — see Test Scope). No sweep work remains here.

Append `## <skill>` sections to `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`.
**Placement is specific, and "append" does NOT mean end-of-file** — verified this round by
appending a scratch section at EOF: the mechanical checks still pass (they are
position-independent), but the document goes incoherent, stranding B1's concluding
`## Method verdict` in the middle of the file.

- Put your new `## <skill>` sections at the **end of the skill-section RUN** — immediately
  BEFORE the `---` separator that precedes `## Findings and fixes`. Do not reorder or edit any
  existing skill section.
- Add one row per failure to the **existing shared** `## Findings and fixes` table; it already
  carries a `Skill` column, so B1 and later batches coexist in one table. A family with no
  failures adds no rows.
- **Update the header's Coverage sentence.** It currently reads "Coverage: batch B1 only — the
  6 pipeline conductors" and becomes FALSE the moment your sections land. Refine round 2 found
  this line was owned by no bead; it is now this bead's job. Extend it to name the batches
  covered after your work. Expect to touch the same line a sibling batch touches — it is one
  line and rebases trivially.

  executes under it rather than re-deciding it.

**Suggested order within B2-B5:** run **ac-kqpw.2** first — it is the smallest batch and its own
body designates it the calibration run, so its lessons are the cheapest to buy. `.1`, `.3` and
`.4` are order-independent after that. This is a suggestion, not a dependency: no batch consumes
another's output, so it is deliberately NOT encoded as a `blocks` edge (see Test Scope).

## Delivers

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — one `## <skill>` section for each of
  the 5 skills above, each with >= 5 + >= 5 recorded verdicts (AC 1 + AC 2 verify this)
- `description:` line fixes in whichever of those 5 `skills/*/SKILL.md` files fail
  precision/recall — possibly none, which is a legitimate outcome (AC 3 + AC 4 verify this)

## Consumes

- none. The method and the corpus file both landed with ac-gcj.10 (verified CLOSED this round;

  batch reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

Re-executed against HEAD 881e966 on 2026-08-04 (refine round 1). RED-now values measured
THIS round, not carried over from the filing.

1. All 5 skills have a section:
   `for s in ac-plan-clean ac-plan-init ac-plan-lab ac-plan-refine-external ac-plan-refine-internal; do grep -c "^## $s\$" skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md; done`
   returns **1** 5 times. RED now: **0** for all of them (executed 2026-08-04).

2. Every section carries >= 5 should-activate and >= 5 should-NOT-activate phrasings, each with
   a recorded verdict. **This IS mechanically checkable — the filing's "verify by reading each
   section" was wrong.** The corpus row grammar (`- PASS` / `- FAIL` / `- PASS (after fix)`)
   makes the count assertable per subsection:

       awk '
         /^## / { sec=substr($0,4); a=0; n=0; cur="";
                  if(sec=="Findings and fixes"||sec=="Method verdict") sec=""; next }
         sec=="" { next }
         /^should-activate/     { cur="A"; next }
         /^should-NOT-activate/ { cur="N"; next }
         /^- (PASS|FAIL)/ { if(cur=="A") a++; else if(cur=="N") n++;
                            secs[sec]=1; A[sec]=a; N[sec]=n }
         END { for (s in secs) printf "%-24s activate=%d not-activate=%d %s\n",
                                s, A[s], N[s], (A[s]>=5 && N[s]>=5 ? "OK" : "SHORT") }
       ' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | sort

   Every section this bead adds must print `OK`. **Executed at HEAD:** the 6 existing B1
   sections each print `activate=5 not-activate=5 OK`. **Bite-proofed:** deleting one
   should-activate row from ac-loop in a scratch copy flipped it to `activate=4 ... SHORT`.
   Limit of this check, stated honestly: it counts ROWS under the correct subsection and
   cannot judge whether a phrasing is a good near-miss — so ALSO read each section for
   semantic quality. The count is the floor, never the ceiling.

   **Quality bar, not just a count — round 3, flagged independently by 2 reviewers.** The row
   count is satisfiable by five lazy keyword-echo phrasings that never probe the collision this
   batch exists to test; verified by building a scratch section of nonsense rows, which printed
   `OK`. So: **at least 3 of the >= 5 should-NOT-activate probes in each section must be
   near-misses whose CORRECT destination is a named sibling in this batch or one of the
   cross-family confusables named above, and each such row must name that destination inline.**
   B1 already writes them this way — e.g. `- PASS — "run the loop" (routes to ac-loop; ...)`.
   Distant-domain negatives ("review my calendar") are free passes that prove nothing
   (trigger-corpus.md § Method verdict, item 3). This is a read-and-judge bar, not a mechanical
   one, and it is deliberate: the awk counts rows, a human or model reads quality.

3. Every precision/recall failure lists the `description:` edit that fixed it AND the re-judged
   verdict. **Mechanical check** (the B1 grammar puts the re-judgement inline on the FAIL row,
   `- FAIL (precision) -> PASS (after fix) — "..."`):

       grep '^- FAIL' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | grep -vc 'PASS (after fix)'

   must print **0**. **Executed at HEAD:** 4 FAIL rows, 0 unrejudged. **Bite-proofed:**
   stripping one row's `PASS (after fix)` in a scratch copy made it print 1. Same exit-code
   caveat as AC 4(a) below.

4. `git diff` over `skills/*/SKILL.md` changes ONLY `description:` lines:

       git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-][^+-]' | grep -vc 'description:'

   must print **0**. **Two executed caveats — read both before using this as a gate:**

   (a) `grep -vc` PRINTS `0` but EXITS `1` when the count is zero (verified: value 0, exit 1).
       Check the PRINTED VALUE. Never chain it with `&&`, never run it under `set -e` — the
       correct PASS reads as a failure.
   (b) **It guards the diff's SHAPE, never its OCCURRENCE.** Bite-proof executed on the live
       working tree, three cases: a body-line edit printed **1** (bites correctly); a
       description-only edit printed **0** with 2 total changed lines; and a **clean tree with
       no edit at all also printed 0**. A `0` here is therefore NOT evidence that any work
       happened — occurrence is proved by AC 1-3 alone. Report the total beside it:
       `git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -cE '^[+-][^+-]'` should equal
       2 x (number of fixes recorded under AC 3). A family that legitimately needs ZERO
       description fixes has an EMPTY diff here, and that is a PASS — B1 had 2 of 6 clean.

   count**, which drifts in this checkout (314 -> 372 -> **374**, measured at HEAD 881e966 on
   2026-08-04). Shares AC 4(b)'s occurrence blindness: lint is green on an untouched tree too.
   Check 13 (description budget) and Check 14 (per-file no-net-growth) are the two that bite —
   their executed mechanics are in Test Scope.

**Honest limit:** these verdicts are a **lower bound**. The judge is the same model being
routed, reading its own text with the full registry in context — a cold router sees less.
Record that caveat in each section rather than presenting the verdicts as measurement.

title: Trigger pass B6: remaining ac-* (8 skills)
description:
Trigger precision/recall pass over the **remaining `ac-*` skills** (8 skills, ~80 judgments) —
the ac-* files left after the conductor, plan, qa, bead-lifecycle and polish batches. Batch 5 of
7 in the ac-kqpw split — the parent epic **ac-kqpw** holds the B1 method (binding on this bead),
the enumeration rule, and the shared-file hazard. Read the epic first; this bead does not
restate them — **except where this refine round corrected the epic**, which is called out inline
below and is authoritative over the epic's wording.

discovered-from: ac-gcj.10

## Skills in scope (8 — exhaustive; re-verified present at HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04)

- ac-align
- ac-dashboard
- ac-human-session
- ac-hygiene
- ac-idea-lab
- ac-pipeline
- ac-prove
- ac-registry-audit

Nothing outside this list. This is the residual `ac-*` set: everything not a B1 conductor, not
`ac-plan-*`, not `ac-qa-*`, not bead-lifecycle (batch 3), not polish/publish (batch 4). Sized
just above the B1 precedent (6 skills), so one long sitting.

**Partition re-verified by set arithmetic this round (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20):**
`ls -1 skills/*/SKILL.md` = **58**; minus the 6 `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh` (ac-loop,
ac-implement, ac-review, ac-batch-close, ac-merge, ac-land) = **52** residual = 25 `ac-*`
(5+2+6+4+**8**, batches 1-5) + 27 non-`ac-*` (12+15, batches 6-7). No skill omitted, none
duplicated. These 8 are exactly the `ac-*` residual.

**Confusion clusters — weight negatives here (B1: every finding sat between siblings):**
`ac-hygiene` vs `ac-registry-audit` vs `ac-prove` (three ways to say "check the registry is
sound") · `ac-idea-lab` vs `ac-align` · `ac-pipeline` is a canon-holder rather than an action
skill, so its highest-value negatives are phrasings that should route to one of the conductors
it documents (`ac-loop`, `ac-implement`, ...) and must NOT wake it.

**Special care on `ac-pipeline`:** it is the shared-canon skill, so a description that reads
like an action ("run the pipeline") is a recall/precision trap by construction. If its
description cannot cleanly exclude the conductors' phrasings, that is a finding worth an edit,
not a note. **Budget caveat, measured this round — `ac-pipeline` is the tightest description in
this family at 821/1024 chars (203 headroom).** An explicit NOT-for exclusion clause costs
74-101 chars in the B1 precedent, so ac-pipeline fits **at most two** before it risks Check 13's
hard cap. If the clause you need would exceed the headroom, TIGHTEN the existing description
text in the same edit (net-neutral) rather than growing it — do not silently skip the fix, and
do not split it onto a second line (see the Check 14 corollary in Test Scope).

**Resume protocol across sittings (so a second sitting needs no reconstruction):** the corpus
file IS the state. At the end of a sitting, commit the completed `## <skill>` sections and post
a bead comment listing which of the 8 skills are DONE. To resume, run AC 1's per-skill loop —
every skill returning `0` is outstanding. Never leave a partially-written section on disk
uncommitted; a half-section is indistinguishable from a finished one at resume time. (Added by
refine round 1: .6 and .7 carried this and .5 did not, with no stated reason, despite sharing
the identical shared-file hazard.)

## Per-skill work

For each skill above: >= 5 should-activate phrasings + >= 5 should-NOT-activate near-misses,
judged from the frontmatter `description:` **ALONE** (not the body), each carrying a recorded
verdict. Every precision/recall failure gets a `description:` edit, re-judged afterwards, with
both the edit and the new verdict recorded.

**Bare bead-id sweep: EXECUTED this round, and it is a NO-OP for this family.** The regex
`\b(bd-[a-z0-9]{4,7}|ac-[a-z]*[0-9][a-z0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?\b` over the extracted `description:`
of all 8 skills returned **zero hits** (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20). Do not go hunting. Warning:
a naive `ac-[a-z-]+` regex FALSE-POSITIVES on sibling skill NAMES (ac-align, ac-prove...) —
those are legitimate cross-references and must NOT be stripped.

Append `## <skill>` sections to `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` —
**append only; do not start a second file and do not reorder existing sections.**

**Placement is NOT end-of-file** (corrected this round; the filing's bare "append" was
underspecified). The corpus is ordered: header / `---` / the skill sections / `---` /
`## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`. Verified at HEAD c6cda20 via
`grep -n '^## \|^---$'`. Your sections go at the **end of the skill-section run, immediately
BEFORE the `---` that precedes `## Findings and fixes`**. Appending at true EOF strands
`## Method verdict` mid-file.

- **Update the header's Coverage sentence** (`skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`, ~line 16).
  It is a live, growing sentence: as of HEAD c6cda20 it names B1 plus B2-B5, because those
  batches landed while this bead was being refined. **Read it before editing — do not trust any
  quotation of it, including this one.** Extend it to name YOUR batch; it becomes FALSE for your
  skills the moment your sections land. Refine found this line was owned by no bead; it is now a
  shared job across all seven batch beads, and that is deliberate — each batch appends its own
  clause. It is one line and rebases trivially; batches B2-B5 already did exactly this without
  conflict. **Re-wrap the whole paragraph when you edit it.** Four sequential appends have left
  it ragged — orphaned single-word lines ("The" / "remaining" / "batches;") — because each batch
  appended its clause without reflowing. Verified at HEAD c6cda20. Reflow to the file's normal
  width as part of your edit; that is not scope creep, it is leaving the line you own readable.
  **Cheapest safe way to get the claim right:** derive it from the file itself rather than from
  memory or from this bead — `grep -c '^## ' <corpus>` minus the two non-skill sections
  (`## Findings and fixes`, `## Method verdict`) is the true count of skills covered, and
  `grep -oE '^## [a-z0-9-]+' <corpus>` lists them. Reconcile the sentence against that.
- Do **NOT** add a second `## Method verdict`. B1's verdict (GO) already governs; this batch
  executes under it rather than re-deciding it.

## Delivers

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — one `## <skill>` section for each of
  the 8 skills above, each with >= 5 + >= 5 recorded verdicts, plus the updated Coverage line
- `description:` line fixes in whichever of those 8 `skills/*/SKILL.md` files fail

## Consumes

- none. The method and the corpus file both landed with ac-gcj.10 (CLOSED); no open blocker.

## Acceptance Criteria

Re-executed against HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04 (refine round 1). RED-now values measured THIS
round, not carried over from the filing.

1. All 8 skills have a section:
   `for s in ac-align ac-dashboard ac-human-session ac-hygiene ac-idea-lab ac-pipeline ac-prove ac-registry-audit; do grep -c "^## $s\$" skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md; done`
   returns **1** eight times. RED now: **0** for all 8 (executed 2026-08-04).

2. Every section carries >= 5 should-activate and >= 5 should-NOT-activate phrasings, each with
   a recorded verdict. **This IS mechanically checkable — the filing's "verify by reading each
   section; a count-only grep would pass on empty rows" was WRONG and is retracted.** The corpus
   row grammar (`- PASS` / `- FAIL` / `- PASS (after fix)`) makes the count assertable per
   subsection:

       awk '
         /^## / { sec=substr($0,4); a=0; n=0; cur="";
                  if(sec=="Findings and fixes"||sec=="Method verdict") sec=""; next }
         sec=="" { next }
         /^should-activate/     { cur="A"; next }
         /^should-NOT-activate/ { cur="N"; next }
         /^- (PASS|FAIL)/ { if(cur=="A") a++; else if(cur=="N") n++;
                            secs[sec]=1; A[sec]=a; N[sec]=n }
         END { for (s in secs) printf "%-24s activate=%d not-activate=%d %s\n",
                                s, A[s], N[s], (A[s]>=5 && N[s]>=5 ? "OK" : "SHORT") }
       ' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | sort

   Every section this bead adds must print `OK`. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20 (exit 0):** the 6
   existing B1 sections each print `activate=5 not-activate=5 OK`. **Bite-proofed by the sibling
   refine:** deleting one should-activate row from ac-loop in a scratch copy flipped it to
   `activate=4 not-activate=5 SHORT`. Limit, stated honestly: it counts ROWS under the correct
   subsection and cannot judge whether a phrasing is a good near-miss — so ALSO read each
   section. The count is the floor, never the ceiling.

   **Quality bar, not just a count.** The row count is satisfiable by five lazy keyword-echo
   phrasings that never probe the collision this batch exists to test (verified: a scratch
   section of nonsense rows printed `OK`). So: **at least 3 of the >= 5 should-NOT-activate
   probes in each section must be near-misses whose CORRECT destination is a named sibling in
   this batch or one of the cross-family confusables named above, and each such row must name
   that destination inline.** B1 already writes them this way — e.g.
   `- PASS — "run the loop" (routes to ac-loop; ...)`. Distant-domain negatives ("review my
   calendar") are free passes that prove nothing (trigger-corpus.md § Method verdict, item 3).
   This is a read-and-judge bar, not a mechanical one, and it is deliberate.

   **Template off B2-B5, NOT off B1** (measured two independent ways in refine round 3, same
   verdict). B1 predates this bar and does not meet it — counting should-NOT rows that name a
   destination inline, B1's six sections score **0-1 out of 5** (`ac-loop`, `ac-review`,
   `ac-batch-close`, `ac-merge`, `ac-land` all 0; `ac-implement` 1). The 17 sections landed by
   batches B2-B5 were built under this bar and score materially higher — spot-measured
   `ac-tidy` 4/5, `ac-ui-polish` 4/5, `ac-qa-browser` 3/5, `ac-plan-refine-external` 2/5.
   So copy the SHAPE from B1 if you like, but copy the STANDARD from B2-B5 — an implementer
   pattern-matching on B1 alone will under-deliver and not notice.

3. Every precision/recall failure lists the `description:` edit that fixed it AND the re-judged
   verdict. **Mechanical check** (the B1 grammar puts the re-judgement inline on the FAIL row,
   `- FAIL (precision) -> PASS (after fix) — "..."`):

       grep '^- FAIL' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | grep -vc 'PASS (after fix)'

   must print **0**. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20:** prints `0` (4 FAIL rows, all re-judged
   inline). **Bite-proofed by the sibling refine:** stripping one row's `PASS (after fix)` in a
   scratch copy made it print `1`. Same exit-code caveat as AC 4(a) below — this command PRINTS
   `0` and EXITS `1`; read the printed value.

4. `git diff` over `skills/*/SKILL.md` changes ONLY `description:` lines:

       git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-][^+-]' | grep -vc 'description:'

   must print **0**. **Two executed caveats — read both before using this as a gate:**

   (a) `grep -vc` PRINTS `0` but EXITS `1` when the count is zero (verified this round:
       `printf "" | grep -vc 'description:'` prints 0, exit 1). Check the PRINTED VALUE. Never
       chain it with `&&`, never run it under `set -e` — the correct PASS reads as a failure.
   (b) **It guards the diff's SHAPE, never its OCCURRENCE.** Bite-proof executed by the sibling
       refine on the live working tree, three cases: a body-line edit printed **1** (bites
       correctly); a description-only edit printed **0** with 2 total changed lines; and a
       **clean tree with no edit at all also printed 0**. A `0` here is therefore NOT evidence
       that any work happened — occurrence is proved by AC 1-3 alone. Report the total beside
       it: `git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -cE '^[+-][^+-]'` should equal
       2 x (number of fixes recorded under AC 3). A family that legitimately needs ZERO
       description fixes has an EMPTY diff here, and that is a PASS — B1 had 2 of 6 clean.

5. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the exit code ONLY — never the check
   count**, which drifts in this checkout (314 -> 372 -> 374 -> **390**, measured at HEAD
    on 2026-08-04). Executed this round: `exit=0`, `lint: 390 checks, 0 failures`.
   Shares AC 4(b)'s occurrence blindness: lint is green on an untouched tree too. Check 13
   (description budget) and Check 14 (per-file no-net-growth) are the two that bite — their
   executed mechanics are in Test Scope.

**Honest limit:** these verdicts are a **lower bound**. The judge is the same model being
routed, reading its own text with the full registry in context — a cold router sees less.
Record that caveat in each section rather than presenting the verdicts as measurement.

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-align/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-dashboard/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-human-session/SKILL.md`,
  `skills/ac-hygiene/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-idea-lab/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md`,
  `skills/ac-prove/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-registry-audit/SKILL.md` — all 8 grep-verified present
  at HEAD c6cda20; `description:` line editable, nothing else.
- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — exists at HEAD c6cda20 (created by
  ac-gcj.10). APPEND target. **Re-verified at HEAD c6cda20 (2026-08-04, refine round 2):
  690 lines, 23 skill sections — B1's 6 conductors PLUS batches B2-B5 (17 skills), which
  landed mid-refine.** An earlier draft of this bead said the corpus held "only the 6 B1
  sections"; that is now FALSE and is retracted. What still holds, and is what actually matters:
  **zero overlap with THIS family** — all of this bead's skills were re-checked against the
  live corpus this round and none has a section yet, so nothing here has been judged before.
  Structure confirmed intact after the sibling landings: `---` / skill sections / `---` /
  `## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`, i.e. the placement rule above was honored and
  works.
- **Check 13 = a per-skill 1024-char HARD cap on the description VALUE** (`len=${#desc}` in
  `skills/skill-builder/scripts/validate-skill.sh`). The cap counts the RAW YAML value
  INCLUDING quotes; measure with the validator's own `extract_description` awk function, NOT a
  re-implementation that strips quotes (a python re-implementation gave numbers 10-20 chars low
  in the sibling refine). **Measured this round with the validator's extractor, HEAD c6cda20:**
  ac-pipeline 821, ac-idea-lab 639, ac-registry-audit 619, ac-prove 562, ac-dashboard 554,
  ac-human-session 460, ac-hygiene 460, ac-align 341. Only `ac-pipeline` (203 headroom) is
  budget-constrained; the other 7 have >= 385 chars of room.
- **Check 14 is LINE-based, not char-based** — each file's own net line delta must be <= 0
  absent a `net-growth-ok:` stamp. A single-line description rewrite nets 0 lines and passes at
  any legal char length. **Corollary, and the easiest way to break this bead: the rewritten
  `description:` MUST STAY ON ONE LINE.** Wrapping it onto a second line converts a safe edit
  into a Check 14 HARD FAIL.
- **Check 15 conductor tier — RESOLVED, no action needed.** `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh`
  (~line 827) was read at HEAD c6cda20: it is EXACTLY the 6 B1 conductors. **None of this
  bead's 8 skills is conductor-tier**; all are STANDARD (730-line ceiling), and Check 15 counts
  LINES, which a description edit does not change.
- No unit harness exists — the recorded verdicts ARE the artifact, so an unrecorded judgment is
  an unverifiable one.
- **Shared-file hazard — premise corrected (refine round 1, 2026-08-04).** The epic states that
  "ac-loop's file-set disjointness check already prevents two children touching the corpus
  concurrently". Verified against the source: the check is real doctrine —
  `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md`, section "Disjointness check before dispatch — BOTH tests must pass"
  (~line 709), whose remedy is literally "any overlap -> serialize those beads behind each
  other". **But it is conductor-executed prose covering the ac-loop WIDTH>1 dispatch path
  only** — not an automated gate, and it does not fire for a human session or a direct
  `ac-implement` invocation. `bv --robot-plan` carries no file-set data at all. Treat
  serialization as a convention you must honor, not a guarantee you inherit. Concrete
  mitigation: before appending, re-run the AC 2 awk to see which sections already exist; if a
  sibling landed since you started, rebase and re-append rather than resolving in place; after
  committing, re-run AC 1 to confirm YOUR family's sections survived. Commit the instant they
  verify — minimal working-tree dwell. **The seven batch beads are deliberately NOT chained by
  `blocks` edges, and that is correct**: no batch consumes any artifact another produces, so a
  `blocks` edge would misencode a scheduling convention as a data dependency
  (`beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` §Bead I/O contract). The epic's own wording
  of this justification is tracked for correction by **ac-kqpw.8**; this bead's text above
  supersedes it.

title: Trigger pass B7: domain agent-system + build-platform (12 skills)
description:
Trigger precision/recall pass over the **agent-system + build-platform domain skills**
(12 skills, ~120 judgments). Batch 6 of 7 in the ac-kqpw split — the parent epic **ac-kqpw**
holds the B1 method (binding on this bead), the enumeration rule, and the shared-file hazard.
Read the epic first; this bead does not restate them — **except where this refine round
corrected the epic**, which is called out inline below and is authoritative over the epic's
wording.

discovered-from: ac-gcj.10

## Skills in scope (12 — exhaustive; re-verified present at HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04)

- agent-mail
- beads-standards
- capacitor
- context-engineering
- dream
- openrouter
- planning
- prompt-enhance
- reflect
- skill-builder
- supabase
- workflow-builder

Nothing outside this list. The other 15 non-`ac-*` skills belong to batch 7.

**Partition re-verified by set arithmetic this round (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20):**
`ls -1 skills/*/SKILL.md` = **58**; minus the 6 `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh` = **52**
residual = 25 `ac-*` (batches 1-5) + 27 non-`ac-*` (**12** here + 15 in batch 7). No skill
omitted, none duplicated.

**Size note — honest:** at ~120 judgments this is 2x the B1 precedent (6 skills / ~60 / one
sitting). It is not split further because the next boundary down would be arbitrary: 7 of these
12 fall into the three named confusion clusters below, but the remaining 5 (`agent-mail`,
`beads-standards`, `capacitor`, `openrouter`, `supabase`) have no named confusion-cluster
relationship to each other, so any sub-split would cut a coherent family and leave an
unmotivated remainder. (Re-litigated and re-affirmed by refine round 1, which DID find a clean
sub-partition for batch 7 but explicitly not for this one.) Expect two sittings; do not leave a
skill half-judged across them.

**Resume protocol across sittings (so the second sitting needs no reconstruction):** the corpus
file IS the state. At the end of a sitting, commit the completed `## <skill>` sections and post
a bead comment listing which of the 12 skills are DONE. To resume, run AC 1's per-skill loop —
every skill returning `0` is outstanding. Never leave a partially-written section on disk
uncommitted; a half-section is indistinguishable from a finished one at resume time.

**Confusion clusters — weight negatives here (B1: every finding sat between siblings):**
`context-engineering` vs `reflect` vs `dream` (three memory/learning surfaces — the sharpest
cluster in this batch; "save this learning" must route to exactly one) · `skill-builder` vs
`workflow-builder` · `planning` vs `prompt-enhance` · `beads-standards` against every `ac-bead-*`
skill (batch 3 — reference them as negative targets, do NOT judge them here).

**This batch is where B1's "stale, not just imprecise" failure is most likely to recur** —
domain skills change hands less often than pipeline conductors, so read each `description:`
against what the body actually does *today* before judging it. Two of B1's four failures were
staleness, not imprecision.

**Budget caveat, measured this round — `beads-standards` is the tightest description in this
family at 793/1024 chars (231 headroom).** An explicit NOT-for exclusion clause costs 74-101
chars in the B1 precedent, so it fits **at most two** before it risks Check 13's hard cap. If
the clause you need would exceed the headroom, TIGHTEN the existing description text in the
same edit (net-neutral) rather than growing it — do not silently skip the fix, and do not split
it onto a second line (see the Check 14 corollary in Test Scope). Every other skill here has
>= 395 chars of room.

## Per-skill work

For each skill above: >= 5 should-activate phrasings + >= 5 should-NOT-activate near-misses,
judged from the frontmatter `description:` **ALONE** (not the body), each carrying a recorded
verdict. Every precision/recall failure gets a `description:` edit, re-judged afterwards, with
both the edit and the new verdict recorded.

**Bare bead-id sweep: EXECUTED this round, and it is a NO-OP for this family.** The regex
`\b(bd-[a-z0-9]{4,7}|ac-[a-z]*[0-9][a-z0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?\b` over the extracted `description:`
of all 12 skills returned **zero hits** (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20). Do not go hunting. Warning:
a naive `ac-[a-z-]+` regex FALSE-POSITIVES on sibling skill NAMES — those are legitimate
cross-references and must NOT be stripped.

Append `## <skill>` sections to `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` —
**append only; do not start a second file and do not reorder existing sections.**

**Placement is NOT end-of-file** (corrected this round; the filing's bare "append" was
underspecified). The corpus is ordered: header / `---` / the skill sections / `---` /
`## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`. Verified at HEAD c6cda20 via
`grep -n '^## \|^---$'`. Your sections go at the **end of the skill-section run, immediately
BEFORE the `---` that precedes `## Findings and fixes`**. Appending at true EOF strands
`## Method verdict` mid-file.

- **Update the header's Coverage sentence** (`skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`, ~line 16).
  It is a live, growing sentence: as of HEAD c6cda20 it names B1 plus B2-B5, because those
  batches landed while this bead was being refined. **Read it before editing — do not trust any
  quotation of it, including this one.** Extend it to name YOUR batch; it becomes FALSE for your
  skills the moment your sections land. Refine found this line was owned by no bead; it is now a
  shared job across all seven batch beads, and that is deliberate — each batch appends its own
  clause. It is one line and rebases trivially; batches B2-B5 already did exactly this without
  conflict. **Re-wrap the whole paragraph when you edit it.** Four sequential appends have left
  it ragged — orphaned single-word lines ("The" / "remaining" / "batches;") — because each batch
  appended its clause without reflowing. Verified at HEAD c6cda20. Reflow to the file's normal
  width as part of your edit; that is not scope creep, it is leaving the line you own readable.
  **Cheapest safe way to get the claim right:** derive it from the file itself rather than from
  memory or from this bead — `grep -c '^## ' <corpus>` minus the two non-skill sections
  (`## Findings and fixes`, `## Method verdict`) is the true count of skills covered, and
  `grep -oE '^## [a-z0-9-]+' <corpus>` lists them. Reconcile the sentence against that.
- Do **NOT** add a second `## Method verdict`. B1's verdict (GO) already governs; this batch
  executes under it rather than re-deciding it.

## Delivers

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — one `## <skill>` section for each of
  the 12 skills above, each with >= 5 + >= 5 recorded verdicts, plus the updated Coverage line
- `description:` line fixes in whichever of those 12 `skills/*/SKILL.md` files fail

## Consumes

- none. The method and the corpus file both landed with ac-gcj.10 (CLOSED); no open blocker.

## Acceptance Criteria

Re-executed against HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04 (refine round 1). RED-now values measured THIS
round, not carried over from the filing.

1. All 12 skills have a section:
   `for s in agent-mail beads-standards capacitor context-engineering dream openrouter planning prompt-enhance reflect skill-builder supabase workflow-builder; do grep -c "^## $s\$" skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md; done`
   returns **1** twelve times. RED now: **0** for all 12 (executed 2026-08-04).

2. Every section carries >= 5 should-activate and >= 5 should-NOT-activate phrasings, each with
   a recorded verdict. **This IS mechanically checkable — the filing's "verify by reading each
   section; a count-only grep would pass on empty rows" was WRONG and is retracted.** The corpus
   row grammar (`- PASS` / `- FAIL` / `- PASS (after fix)`) makes the count assertable per
   subsection:

       awk '
         /^## / { sec=substr($0,4); a=0; n=0; cur="";
                  if(sec=="Findings and fixes"||sec=="Method verdict") sec=""; next }
         sec=="" { next }
         /^should-activate/     { cur="A"; next }
         /^should-NOT-activate/ { cur="N"; next }
         /^- (PASS|FAIL)/ { if(cur=="A") a++; else if(cur=="N") n++;
                            secs[sec]=1; A[sec]=a; N[sec]=n }
         END { for (s in secs) printf "%-24s activate=%d not-activate=%d %s\n",
                                s, A[s], N[s], (A[s]>=5 && N[s]>=5 ? "OK" : "SHORT") }
       ' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | sort

   Every section this bead adds must print `OK`. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20 (exit 0):** the 6
   existing B1 sections each print `activate=5 not-activate=5 OK`. **Bite-proofed by the sibling
   refine:** deleting one should-activate row from ac-loop in a scratch copy flipped it to
   `activate=4 not-activate=5 SHORT`. Limit, stated honestly: it counts ROWS under the correct
   subsection and cannot judge whether a phrasing is a good near-miss — so ALSO read each
   section. The count is the floor, never the ceiling.

   **Quality bar, not just a count.** The row count is satisfiable by five lazy keyword-echo
   phrasings that never probe the collision this batch exists to test (verified: a scratch
   section of nonsense rows printed `OK`). So: **at least 3 of the >= 5 should-NOT-activate
   probes in each section must be near-misses whose CORRECT destination is a named sibling in
   this batch or one of the cross-family confusables named above, and each such row must name
   that destination inline.** B1 already writes them this way — e.g.
   `- PASS — "run the loop" (routes to ac-loop; ...)`. Distant-domain negatives ("review my
   calendar") are free passes that prove nothing (trigger-corpus.md § Method verdict, item 3).
   This is a read-and-judge bar, not a mechanical one, and it is deliberate.

   **Template off B2-B5, NOT off B1** (measured two independent ways in refine round 3, same
   verdict). B1 predates this bar and does not meet it — counting should-NOT rows that name a
   destination inline, B1's six sections score **0-1 out of 5** (`ac-loop`, `ac-review`,
   `ac-batch-close`, `ac-merge`, `ac-land` all 0; `ac-implement` 1). The 17 sections landed by
   batches B2-B5 were built under this bar and score materially higher — spot-measured
   `ac-tidy` 4/5, `ac-ui-polish` 4/5, `ac-qa-browser` 3/5, `ac-plan-refine-external` 2/5.
   So copy the SHAPE from B1 if you like, but copy the STANDARD from B2-B5 — an implementer
   pattern-matching on B1 alone will under-deliver and not notice.

3. Every precision/recall failure lists the `description:` edit that fixed it AND the re-judged
   verdict. **Mechanical check** (the B1 grammar puts the re-judgement inline on the FAIL row,
   `- FAIL (precision) -> PASS (after fix) — "..."`):

       grep '^- FAIL' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | grep -vc 'PASS (after fix)'

   must print **0**. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20:** prints `0` (4 FAIL rows, all re-judged
   inline). **Bite-proofed by the sibling refine:** stripping one row's `PASS (after fix)` in a
   scratch copy made it print `1`. Same exit-code caveat as AC 4(a) below — this command PRINTS
   `0` and EXITS `1`; read the printed value.

4. `git diff` over `skills/*/SKILL.md` changes ONLY `description:` lines:

       git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-][^+-]' | grep -vc 'description:'

   must print **0**. **Two executed caveats — read both before using this as a gate:**

   (a) `grep -vc` PRINTS `0` but EXITS `1` when the count is zero (verified this round:
       `printf "" | grep -vc 'description:'` prints 0, exit 1). Check the PRINTED VALUE. Never
       chain it with `&&`, never run it under `set -e` — the correct PASS reads as a failure.
   (b) **It guards the diff's SHAPE, never its OCCURRENCE.** Bite-proof executed by the sibling
       refine on the live working tree, three cases: a body-line edit printed **1** (bites
       correctly); a description-only edit printed **0** with 2 total changed lines; and a
       **clean tree with no edit at all also printed 0**. A `0` here is therefore NOT evidence
       that any work happened — occurrence is proved by AC 1-3 alone. Report the total beside
       it: `git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -cE '^[+-][^+-]'` should equal
       2 x (number of fixes recorded under AC 3). A family that legitimately needs ZERO
       description fixes has an EMPTY diff here, and that is a PASS — B1 had 2 of 6 clean.

5. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the exit code ONLY — never the check
   count**, which drifts in this checkout (314 -> 372 -> 374 -> **390**, measured at HEAD
    on 2026-08-04). Executed this round: `exit=0`, `lint: 390 checks, 0 failures`.
   Shares AC 4(b)'s occurrence blindness: lint is green on an untouched tree too. Check 13
   (description budget) and Check 14 (per-file no-net-growth) are the two that bite — their
   executed mechanics are in Test Scope.

**Honest limit:** these verdicts are a **lower bound**. The judge is the same model being
routed, reading its own text with the full registry in context — a cold router sees less.
`skill-builder` is a special case of this: it is the skill that owns the corpus file being
written, so judging it is self-referential. Say so in its section.

## Test Scope

- The 12 `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` files listed above — all grep-verified present at HEAD
  ; `description:` line editable, nothing else.
- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — exists at HEAD c6cda20 (created by
  ac-gcj.10). APPEND target. **Re-verified at HEAD c6cda20 (2026-08-04, refine round 2):
  690 lines, 23 skill sections — B1's 6 conductors PLUS batches B2-B5 (17 skills), which
  landed mid-refine.** An earlier draft of this bead said the corpus held "only the 6 B1
  sections"; that is now FALSE and is retracted. What still holds, and is what actually matters:
  **zero overlap with THIS family** — all of this bead's skills were re-checked against the
  live corpus this round and none has a section yet, so nothing here has been judged before.
  Structure confirmed intact after the sibling landings: `---` / skill sections / `---` /
  `## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`, i.e. the placement rule above was honored and
  works.
- READ-ONLY negative targets owned by sibling batches: `skills/ac-bead-capture/SKILL.md`,
  `skills/ac-bead-refine/SKILL.md`, `skills/ac-beadify/SKILL.md` (batch 3).
- **Check 13 = a per-skill 1024-char HARD cap on the description VALUE** (`len=${#desc}` in
  `skills/skill-builder/scripts/validate-skill.sh`). The cap counts the RAW YAML value
  INCLUDING quotes; measure with the validator's own `extract_description` awk function, NOT a
  re-implementation that strips quotes (a python re-implementation gave numbers 10-20 chars low
  in the sibling refine). **Measured this round with the validator's extractor, HEAD c6cda20:**
  beads-standards 793, capacitor 629, workflow-builder 623, agent-mail 606, skill-builder 589,
  dream 518, supabase 494, context-engineering 476, planning 458, reflect 364, openrouter 334,
  prompt-enhance 322. Only `beads-standards` (231 headroom) is budget-constrained.
- **Check 14 is LINE-based, not char-based** — each file's own net line delta must be <= 0
  absent a `net-growth-ok:` stamp. A single-line description rewrite nets 0 lines and passes at
  any legal char length. **Corollary, and the easiest way to break this bead: the rewritten
  `description:` MUST STAY ON ONE LINE.** Wrapping it onto a second line converts a safe edit
  into a Check 14 HARD FAIL.
- **Check 15 conductor tier — RESOLVED, no action needed.** `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh`
  (~line 827) was read at HEAD c6cda20: it is EXACTLY the 6 B1 conductors. **None of this
  bead's 12 skills is conductor-tier**; all are STANDARD (730-line ceiling), and Check 15 counts
  LINES, which a description edit does not change.
- No unit harness exists — the recorded verdicts ARE the artifact, so an unrecorded judgment is
  an unverifiable one.
- **Shared-file hazard — premise corrected (refine round 1, 2026-08-04).** The epic states that
  "ac-loop's file-set disjointness check already prevents two children touching the corpus
  concurrently". Verified against the source: the check is real doctrine —
  `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md`, section "Disjointness check before dispatch — BOTH tests must pass"
  (~line 709), whose remedy is literally "any overlap -> serialize those beads behind each
  other". **But it is conductor-executed prose covering the ac-loop WIDTH>1 dispatch path
  only** — not an automated gate, and it does not fire for a human session or a direct
  `ac-implement` invocation. `bv --robot-plan` carries no file-set data at all. Treat
  serialization as a convention you must honor, not a guarantee you inherit. Concrete
  mitigation: before appending, re-run the AC 2 awk to see which sections already exist; if a
  sibling landed since you started, rebase and re-append rather than resolving in place; after
  committing, re-run AC 1 to confirm YOUR family's sections survived. Commit the instant they
  verify — minimal working-tree dwell. **The seven batch beads are deliberately NOT chained by
  `blocks` edges, and that is correct**: no batch consumes any artifact another produces, so a
  `blocks` edge would misencode a scheduling convention as a data dependency
  (`beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` §Bead I/O contract). The epic's own wording
  of this justification is tracked for correction by **ac-kqpw.8**; this bead's text above
  supersedes it.

AC4a prints 0, AC4b totals 18 = 2 x 9 description edits. AC5 lint exit 0. Two STALENESS findings, the class the bead predicted: context-engineering routed to a phantom 'librarian' and supabase to a phantom 'design-system' — neither exists in agent-compounds/skills nor the root agent home (root is a symlink into this registry), so both exclusions were decorative; repointed at live destinations. beads-standards 793->949 stayed inside its 231 headroom; all 12 under the 1024 cap, every edit one line.   re-judged inline), exit 1 — the exit-code trap is now documented on the AC itself.
- ac-command-fixed: AC 4's two undisclosed defects documented. (a) `grep -vc` PRINTS 0 but EXITS
  1 when the count is zero — re-verified here on a clean tree. (b) it guards diff SHAPE, never
  OCCURRENCE; a clean tree with no edit also prints 0. Occurrence reassigned to AC 1-3 plus a
  total-lines cross-check, whose arithmetic ("2 x number of fixes") was bite-tested this round

  before the `---` preceding `## Findings and fixes` — NOT EOF, which would strand

- premise-false: the epic's no-chain justification — "ac-loop's file-set disjointness check

New this round, specific to this family:
