title: Trigger pass B8: domain testing/creative/publishing (15 skills)
description:
Trigger precision/recall pass over the **testing / creative / publishing domain skills**
(15 skills, ~150 judgments). Batch 7 of 7 in the ac-kqpw split — the parent epic **ac-kqpw**
holds the B1 method (binding on this bead), the enumeration rule, and the shared-file hazard.
Read the epic first; this bead does not restate them — **except where this refine round
corrected the epic**, which is called out inline below and is authoritative over the epic's
wording.

discovered-from: ac-gcj.10

## Skills in scope (15 — exhaustive; re-verified present at HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04)

- app-store-screenshots
- audit
- brainstorming
- browser-testing
- device-testing
- expert-consensus
- jef-flywheel
- jef-prompts
- screenshot-refresh
- seo-metadata
- testing
- ui-brainstorm
- ui-debug
- web-design-guidelines
- wiki

Nothing outside this list. The other 12 non-`ac-*` skills belong to batch 6.

**Partition re-verified by set arithmetic this round (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20):**
`ls -1 skills/*/SKILL.md` = **58**; minus the 6 `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh` = **52**
residual = 25 `ac-*` (batches 1-5) + 27 non-`ac-*` (12 in batch 6 + **15** here). No skill
omitted, none duplicated.

**Size note — honest, and revised by refine round 1.** At ~150 judgments this is the largest of
the seven batches, 2.5x the B1 precedent (6 skills / ~60 / one sitting). The epic's stated
reason for not cutting it further — "the next boundary down would be arbitrary" — is **weaker
here than the epic implies**: this bead's own confusion clusters do name a clean, balanced
5/5/5 sub-partition (verification / creative-ideation / publishing-content; see below), each
landing on the B1 one-sitting precedent. It is kept as ONE bead for now because splitting it
would require re-writing the parent epic's 7-child coverage table, which is outside the stamp
scope of the refine that found this. **Treat the three clusters below as the execution order and
the natural sitting boundaries** — finish one cluster completely, commit, then start the next.
That captures most of the split's value without restructuring the epic.

**Resume protocol across sittings (so the next sitting needs no reconstruction):** the corpus
file IS the state. At the end of a sitting, commit the completed `## <skill>` sections and post
a bead comment listing which of the 15 skills are DONE. To resume, run AC 1's per-skill loop —
every skill returning `0` is outstanding. Never leave a partially-written section on disk
uncommitted; a half-section is indistinguishable from a finished one at resume time.

**Confusion clusters — weight negatives here (B1: every finding sat between siblings). These
also partition the batch 5/5/5 and are the recommended sitting boundaries:**

1. **verification (5):** `testing` vs `browser-testing` vs `device-testing` vs `ui-debug` vs
   `audit` — five overlapping verification surfaces, and all five must also exclude
   `ac-qa-browser` / `ac-qa-device` (batch 2; reference them as negative targets, do NOT judge
   them here).
2. **creative / ideation (5):** `brainstorming` vs `ui-brainstorm` vs `expert-consensus`, plus
   `app-store-screenshots` vs `screenshot-refresh`.
3. **publishing / content (5):** `seo-metadata` vs `web-design-guidelines`, `jef-flywheel` vs
   `jef-prompts`, and `wiki`.

**Generic-verb risk is highest here.** B1's predicted failure profile — no NOT-for clause AND a
generic verb in the trigger list — describes `testing` and `audit` almost exactly. Expect both
to fail on recall-side over-triggering and to need an explicit NOT-for clause; that was the one
fix shape that passed in B1. **Budget is comfortable for that**: measured this round, the
tightest description in this family is `wiki` at 624/1024 (400 headroom) and `testing` itself
has 724 chars of room, so an exclusion clause (74-101 chars) fits everywhere here. No
net-neutral rewrite is forced in this batch.

## Per-skill work

For each skill above: >= 5 should-activate phrasings + >= 5 should-NOT-activate near-misses,
judged from the frontmatter `description:` **ALONE** (not the body), each carrying a recorded
verdict. Every precision/recall failure gets a `description:` edit, re-judged afterwards, with
both the edit and the new verdict recorded.

**Bare bead-id sweep: EXECUTED this round, and it is a NO-OP for this family.** The regex
`\b(bd-[a-z0-9]{4,7}|ac-[a-z]*[0-9][a-z0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?\b` over the extracted `description:`
of all 15 skills returned **zero hits** (2026-08-04, HEAD c6cda20). Do not go hunting. Warning:
a naive `ac-[a-z-]+` regex FALSE-POSITIVES on sibling skill NAMES — those are legitimate
cross-references and must NOT be stripped.

Append `## <skill>` sections to `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` —
**append only; do not start a second file and do not reorder existing sections.**

**Placement is NOT end-of-file** (corrected this round; the filing's bare "append" was
underspecified). The corpus is ordered: header / `---` / the skill sections / `---` /
`## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`. Verified at HEAD c6cda20 via
`grep -n '^## \|^---$'`. Your sections go at the **end of the skill-section run, immediately
BEFORE the `---` that precedes `## Findings and fixes`**. Appending at true EOF strands
`## Method verdict` mid-file.

- **Update the header's Coverage sentence** (`skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md`, ~line 16).
  It is a live, growing sentence: as of HEAD c6cda20 it names B1 plus B2-B5, because those
  batches landed while this bead was being refined. **Read it before editing — do not trust any
  quotation of it, including this one.** Extend it to name YOUR batch; it becomes FALSE for your
  skills the moment your sections land. Refine found this line was owned by no bead; it is now a
  shared job across all seven batch beads, and that is deliberate — each batch appends its own
  clause. It is one line and rebases trivially; batches B2-B5 already did exactly this without
  conflict. **Re-wrap the whole paragraph when you edit it.** Four sequential appends have left
  it ragged — orphaned single-word lines ("The" / "remaining" / "batches;") — because each batch
  appended its clause without reflowing. Verified at HEAD c6cda20. Reflow to the file's normal
  width as part of your edit; that is not scope creep, it is leaving the line you own readable.
  **Cheapest safe way to get the claim right:** derive it from the file itself rather than from
  memory or from this bead — `grep -c '^## ' <corpus>` minus the two non-skill sections
  (`## Findings and fixes`, `## Method verdict`) is the true count of skills covered, and
  `grep -oE '^## [a-z0-9-]+' <corpus>` lists them. Reconcile the sentence against that.
- Do **NOT** add a second `## Method verdict`. B1's verdict (GO) already governs; this batch
  executes under it rather than re-deciding it.

## Delivers

- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — one `## <skill>` section for each of
  the 15 skills above, each with >= 5 + >= 5 recorded verdicts, plus the updated Coverage line
- `description:` line fixes in whichever of those 15 `skills/*/SKILL.md` files fail

## Consumes

- none. The method and the corpus file both landed with ac-gcj.10 (CLOSED); no open blocker.

## Acceptance Criteria

Re-executed against HEAD c6cda20 on 2026-08-04 (refine round 1). RED-now values measured THIS
round, not carried over from the filing.

1. All 15 skills have a section — **this bead's own gate, and it depends on no sibling:**
   `for s in app-store-screenshots audit brainstorming browser-testing device-testing expert-consensus jef-flywheel jef-prompts screenshot-refresh seo-metadata testing ui-brainstorm ui-debug web-design-guidelines wiki; do grep -c "^## $s\$" skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md; done`
   returns **1** fifteen times. RED now: **0** for all 15 (executed 2026-08-04).

   *(Informational, NOT a gate on this bead — deliberately demoted by refine round 1. The
   filing put a whole-residual `comm` check in the AC-1 position and told the implementer to
   "run AFTER batch 6 has landed", which re-introduces as prose the batch ordering the epic's
   refine explicitly rejected as a `blocks` edge. Nothing here waits on batch 6. Once BOTH
   batch 6 and this batch have landed, the epic-level coverage check is:*

       ls -1 skills/*/SKILL.md | sed 's|skills/||; s|/SKILL.md||' | grep -v '^ac-' | sort > /tmp/expected-domain.txt
       grep -oE '^## [a-z0-9-]+' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md \
         | sed 's/^## //' | sort -u > /tmp/covered.txt
       comm -23 /tmp/expected-domain.txt /tmp/covered.txt   # must be EMPTY

   *`/tmp/expected-domain.txt` has **27** lines at HEAD c6cda20 (executed) — 12 from batch 6
   plus these 15. That check belongs to the epic's coverage criteria, not to this bead.)*

2. Every section carries >= 5 should-activate and >= 5 should-NOT-activate phrasings, each with
   a recorded verdict. **This IS mechanically checkable — the filing's "verify by reading each
   section; a count-only grep would pass on empty rows" was WRONG and is retracted.** The corpus
   row grammar (`- PASS` / `- FAIL` / `- PASS (after fix)`) makes the count assertable per
   subsection:

       awk '
         /^## / { sec=substr($0,4); a=0; n=0; cur="";
                  if(sec=="Findings and fixes"||sec=="Method verdict") sec=""; next }
         sec=="" { next }
         /^should-activate/     { cur="A"; next }
         /^should-NOT-activate/ { cur="N"; next }
         /^- (PASS|FAIL)/ { if(cur=="A") a++; else if(cur=="N") n++;
                            secs[sec]=1; A[sec]=a; N[sec]=n }
         END { for (s in secs) printf "%-24s activate=%d not-activate=%d %s\n",
                                s, A[s], N[s], (A[s]>=5 && N[s]>=5 ? "OK" : "SHORT") }
       ' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | sort

   Every section this bead adds must print `OK`. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20 (exit 0):** the 6
   existing B1 sections each print `activate=5 not-activate=5 OK`. **Bite-proofed by the sibling
   refine:** deleting one should-activate row from ac-loop in a scratch copy flipped it to
   `activate=4 not-activate=5 SHORT`. Limit, stated honestly: it counts ROWS under the correct
   subsection and cannot judge whether a phrasing is a good near-miss — so ALSO read each
   section. The count is the floor, never the ceiling.

   **Quality bar, not just a count.** The row count is satisfiable by five lazy keyword-echo
   phrasings that never probe the collision this batch exists to test (verified: a scratch
   section of nonsense rows printed `OK`). So: **at least 3 of the >= 5 should-NOT-activate
   probes in each section must be near-misses whose CORRECT destination is a named sibling in
   this batch or one of the cross-family confusables named above, and each such row must name
   that destination inline.** B1 already writes them this way — e.g.
   `- PASS — "run the loop" (routes to ac-loop; ...)`. Distant-domain negatives ("review my
   calendar") are free passes that prove nothing (trigger-corpus.md § Method verdict, item 3).
   This is a read-and-judge bar, not a mechanical one, and it is deliberate.

   **Template off B2-B5, NOT off B1** (measured two independent ways in refine round 3, same
   verdict). B1 predates this bar and does not meet it — counting should-NOT rows that name a
   destination inline, B1's six sections score **0-1 out of 5** (`ac-loop`, `ac-review`,
   `ac-batch-close`, `ac-merge`, `ac-land` all 0; `ac-implement` 1). The 17 sections landed by
   batches B2-B5 were built under this bar and score materially higher — spot-measured
   `ac-tidy` 4/5, `ac-ui-polish` 4/5, `ac-qa-browser` 3/5, `ac-plan-refine-external` 2/5.
   So copy the SHAPE from B1 if you like, but copy the STANDARD from B2-B5 — an implementer
   pattern-matching on B1 alone will under-deliver and not notice.

3. Every precision/recall failure lists the `description:` edit that fixed it AND the re-judged
   verdict. **Mechanical check** (the B1 grammar puts the re-judgement inline on the FAIL row,
   `- FAIL (precision) -> PASS (after fix) — "..."`):

       grep '^- FAIL' skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md | grep -vc 'PASS (after fix)'

   must print **0**. **Executed at HEAD c6cda20:** prints `0` (4 FAIL rows, all re-judged
   inline). **Bite-proofed by the sibling refine:** stripping one row's `PASS (after fix)` in a
   scratch copy made it print `1`. Same exit-code caveat as AC 4(a) below — this command PRINTS
   `0` and EXITS `1`; read the printed value.

4. `git diff` over `skills/*/SKILL.md` changes ONLY `description:` lines:

       git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-][^+-]' | grep -vc 'description:'

   must print **0**. **Two executed caveats — read both before using this as a gate:**

   (a) `grep -vc` PRINTS `0` but EXITS `1` when the count is zero (verified this round:
       `printf "" | grep -vc 'description:'` prints 0, exit 1). Check the PRINTED VALUE. Never
       chain it with `&&`, never run it under `set -e` — the correct PASS reads as a failure.
   (b) **It guards the diff's SHAPE, never its OCCURRENCE.** Bite-proof executed by the sibling
       refine on the live working tree, three cases: a body-line edit printed **1** (bites
       correctly); a description-only edit printed **0** with 2 total changed lines; and a
       **clean tree with no edit at all also printed 0**. A `0` here is therefore NOT evidence
       that any work happened — occurrence is proved by AC 1-3 alone. Report the total beside
       it: `git diff -U0 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md' | grep -cE '^[+-][^+-]'` should equal
       2 x (number of fixes recorded under AC 3). A family that legitimately needs ZERO
       description fixes has an EMPTY diff here, and that is a PASS — B1 had 2 of 6 clean.

5. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the exit code ONLY — never the check
   count**, which drifts in this checkout (314 -> 372 -> 374 -> **390**, measured at HEAD
    on 2026-08-04). Executed this round: `exit=0`, `lint: 390 checks, 0 failures`.
   Shares AC 4(b)'s occurrence blindness: lint is green on an untouched tree too. Check 13
   (description budget) and Check 14 (per-file no-net-growth) are the two that bite — their
   executed mechanics are in Test Scope.

**Honest limit:** these verdicts are a **lower bound**. The judge is the same model being
routed, reading its own text with the full registry in context — a cold router sees less.
Record that caveat in each section rather than presenting the verdicts as measurement.

## Test Scope

- The 15 `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` files listed above — all grep-verified present at HEAD
  ; `description:` line editable, nothing else.
- `skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md` — exists at HEAD c6cda20 (created by
  ac-gcj.10). APPEND target. **Re-verified at HEAD c6cda20 (2026-08-04, refine round 2):
  690 lines, 23 skill sections — B1's 6 conductors PLUS batches B2-B5 (17 skills), which
  landed mid-refine.** An earlier draft of this bead said the corpus held "only the 6 B1
  sections"; that is now FALSE and is retracted. What still holds, and is what actually matters:
  **zero overlap with THIS family** — all of this bead's skills were re-checked against the
  live corpus this round and none has a section yet, so nothing here has been judged before.
  Structure confirmed intact after the sibling landings: `---` / skill sections / `---` /
  `## Findings and fixes` / `## Method verdict`, i.e. the placement rule above was honored and
  works.
- READ-ONLY negative targets owned by sibling batches: `skills/ac-qa-browser/SKILL.md`,
  `skills/ac-qa-device/SKILL.md` (batch 2), `skills/ac-ui-polish/SKILL.md`,
  `skills/ac-site-polish/SKILL.md` (batch 4).
- **Check 13 = a per-skill 1024-char HARD cap on the description VALUE** (`len=${#desc}` in
  `skills/skill-builder/scripts/validate-skill.sh`). The cap counts the RAW YAML value
  INCLUDING quotes; measure with the validator's own `extract_description` awk function, NOT a
  re-implementation that strips quotes (a python re-implementation gave numbers 10-20 chars low
  in the sibling refine). **Measured this round with the validator's extractor, HEAD c6cda20:**
  wiki 624, device-testing 608, audit 604, seo-metadata 592, ui-brainstorm 576,
  web-design-guidelines 564, jef-flywheel 454, expert-consensus 444, browser-testing 433,
  app-store-screenshots 433, brainstorming 430, screenshot-refresh 413, jef-prompts 410,
  ui-debug 383, testing 300. **Every one has >= 400 chars of headroom** — no budget constraint
  in this family.
- **Check 14 is LINE-based, not char-based** — each file's own net line delta must be <= 0
  absent a `net-growth-ok:` stamp. A single-line description rewrite nets 0 lines and passes at
  any legal char length. **Corollary, and the easiest way to break this bead: the rewritten
  `description:` MUST STAY ON ONE LINE.** Wrapping it onto a second line converts a safe edit
  into a Check 14 HARD FAIL.
- **Check 15 conductor tier — RESOLVED, no action needed.** `CONDUCTOR_SKILLS` in `lint.sh`
  (~line 827) was read at HEAD c6cda20: it is EXACTLY the 6 B1 conductors. **None of this
  bead's 15 skills is conductor-tier**; all are STANDARD (730-line ceiling), and Check 15 counts
  LINES, which a description edit does not change.
- No unit harness exists — the recorded verdicts ARE the artifact, so an unrecorded judgment is
  an unverifiable one.
- **Shared-file hazard — premise corrected (refine round 1, 2026-08-04).** The epic states that
  "ac-loop's file-set disjointness check already prevents two children touching the corpus
  concurrently". Verified against the source: the check is real doctrine —
  `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md`, section "Disjointness check before dispatch — BOTH tests must pass"
  (~line 709), whose remedy is literally "any overlap -> serialize those beads behind each
  other". **But it is conductor-executed prose covering the ac-loop WIDTH>1 dispatch path
  only** — not an automated gate, and it does not fire for a human session or a direct
  `ac-implement` invocation. `bv --robot-plan` carries no file-set data at all. Treat
  serialization as a convention you must honor, not a guarantee you inherit. Concrete
  mitigation: before appending, re-run the AC 2 awk to see which sections already exist; if a
  sibling landed since you started, rebase and re-append rather than resolving in place; after
  committing, re-run AC 1 to confirm YOUR family's sections survived. Commit the instant they
  verify — minimal working-tree dwell. **The seven batch beads are deliberately NOT chained by
  `blocks` edges, and that is correct**: no batch consumes any artifact another produces, so a
  `blocks` edge would misencode a scheduling convention as a data dependency
  (`beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md` §Bead I/O contract). The epic's own wording
  of this justification is tracked for correction by **ac-kqpw.8**; this bead's text above
  supersedes it.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. AC1 all 15 sections present (1 x15, post-commit). AC2 zero SHORT across all 58 corpus sections; >=3 should-NOT rows per section name a sibling destination inline. AC3 prints 0 (11 FAIL rows all re-judged inline). AC4a prints 0. AC5 lint exit 0. AC4b reads 30 not 16 — deliberate and explained below. Worked as one sitting in the bead's recorded cluster order (verification / creative / publishing); the 3-way split stayed REJECTED. Prediction refuted honestly: audit did NOT fail (its four-destination clause held); only testing fit the generic-verb profile. Delivered: skills/skill-builder/references/trigger-corpus.md (15 sections, Coverage line at 58 skills = complete registry, 35 Findings-table rows for B6/B7/B8 plus B6/B7/B8 score paragraphs), description: fixes in skills/testing, device-testing, ui-debug, brainstorming, expert-consensus, jef-flywheel, jef-prompts, wiki SKILL.md; browser-testing, audit, ui-brainstorm, app-store-screenshots, screenshot-refresh, seo-metadata, web-design-guidelines judged clean

Scope note: this bead inherited its method text from the epic and NEVER received the 11
corrections the sibling refine applied to ac-kqpw.1-.4 (it was still `unrefined` when that pass
ran). Those are ported here, RE-EXECUTED at this HEAD rather than copied on trust, plus 5 new
findings this family surfaced on its own.

Ported from the .1-.4 refine, each re-executed here:

- ac-command-fixed: AC 2 said "verify by reading each section; a count-only grep would pass on
  empty rows". FALSE, and retracted. Replaced with the awk row-counter split by
  should-activate / should-NOT-activate. EXECUTED at HEAD c6cda20: all 23 landed sections print
  `activate=5 not-activate=5 OK`, exit 0. Also extracted the awk verbatim from `br show` output

title: lint.sh Check 3 blind to intra-frontmatter corruption — validate SKILL.md frontmatter block integrity
description:
lint.sh Check 3 is blind to intra-frontmatter corruption. Discovered during an ac-loop-lite
refine (2026-08-02): `./lint.sh` passed 314/0 while `skills/ac-distribute/SKILL.md` and
`skills/ac-site-polish/SKILL.md` each carried a prose sentence mis-inserted INSIDE the YAML
frontmatter block, between `name:` and `description:` — invalid YAML. Check 3
(`lint.sh:121-142`) only greps `^name:` and `^description:` for presence, so a foreign line
elsewhere inside the block is invisible to it.

discovered-from: ac-uvj

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03)

- Check 3's blindness is REAL and unfixed — `lint.sh:121-142` does exactly two `grep -m1`
  presence tests per SKILL.md and nothing else.
- Blocker ac-uvj is CLOSED and its repair landed: both `skills/ac-distribute/SKILL.md` and
  `skills/ac-site-polish/SKILL.md` now have clean 4-line frontmatter
  (`---` / `name:` / `description:` / `---`). The new check will therefore start green.
- **The original work statement was WRONG and is corrected below.** It asked the check to
  assert the block "contains ONLY `name:` and `description:` keys". That rule is falsified
  at HEAD: SIX SKILL.md files legitimately carry additional keys (seven extra key LINES —
  ac-idea-lab carries two) —
  `ac-idea-lab` (`accessory:`, `disable-model-invocation:`), `ac-pipeline`
  (`disable-model-invocation:`), `ac-plan-lab` (`accessory:`), `ac-registry-audit`
  (`disable-model-invocation:`), `expert-consensus` (`tools:`), `openrouter` (`tools:`).
  A literal ONLY-check hard-fails all of them on day one. Note that in `ac-idea-lab` the
  extra keys sit BETWEEN `name:` and `description:` — the same position as the real
  corruption — so "line position" is not the discriminator either. The only sound
  discriminator is **key-shaped line vs. prose line**.

## Work

Extend `lint.sh` (Check 3, or a new numbered check placed with it) to validate the
STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY of every `skills/*/SKILL.md` first frontmatter block: the block must
open with `---` on line 1, close with the next `---`, and every non-blank line between them
must be a syntactically valid YAML mapping entry — i.e. match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:`
at line start, or be an indented continuation/list line (`^[[:space:]]`). Any other
non-blank line (bare prose) is a hard FAIL naming the file and the offending line number.
Key COUNT and key IDENTITY are explicitly not constrained — extra keys are legitimate.

Repair of already-corrupted files was ac-uvj's scope (closed, verified), not this bead's.
This bead is the guard that stops the class recurring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `lint.sh` contains a frontmatter block-integrity assertion over `skills/*/SKILL.md`.
      Check: `grep -n 'frontmatter' lint.sh` shows the new logic inside/adjacent to Check 3.
- [ ] The check FAILS on a stray prose line inside the block, at any position.
      Check (bite-proof, must be run): create a throwaway fixture
      `skills/<tmp>/SKILL.md` (or a temp copy of the skills dir) whose frontmatter is
      `---` / `name: x` / `A stray sentence.` / `description: y` / `---`, run `./lint.sh`,
      confirm non-zero exit naming that file and line; then remove the fixture.
- [ ] The check PASSES on all SIX legitimately multi-key skills. Check:
      `./lint.sh` exits 0 at HEAD, and the run reports no failure for ac-idea-lab,
      ac-pipeline, ac-plan-lab, ac-registry-audit, expert-consensus, openrouter.
- [ ] The check PASSES on the two formerly-corrupted files (ac-uvj's repair holds).
      Check: covered by the whole-run exit 0 above; spot-verify with
      `sed -n '1,4p' skills/ac-distribute/SKILL.md skills/ac-site-polish/SKILL.md`.
- [ ] `./lint.sh` exits 0 at HEAD with the new check in place.
      Check: `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`.

## Test Scope

- `lint.sh` (Check 3 block, `lint.sh:121-142`, plus any new check body)
- Corpus under test: `skills/*/SKILL.md` (58 files at HEAD — `skills/_tools/` is a
  directory with no SKILL.md and is NOT a skill; source the loop from `skills/*/SKILL.md`,
  never from `skills/*/`)
- Verification: `./lint.sh` must exit 0 at HEAD; plus the RED fixture above, which must make
  it exit non-zero. Both legs are required — a check that only ever passes proves nothing.
- Seam note: the check (writer of the assertion) and the corpus (the 58 SKILL.md files) are
  the two sides here. The RED fixture is what exercises the seam; a green-only run does not.
- `scripts/lint-net-growth.test.sh` is the only existing lint test harness (Check 14 only) —
  do not assume a Check-3 harness exists.

## Delivers

- `lint.sh` frontmatter block-integrity check: fails on any non-key-shaped, non-blank line
  inside a `skills/*/SKILL.md` first frontmatter block, at any position, without
  constraining which or how many keys appear

## Consumes

- ac-uvj -> repaired frontmatter in `skills/ac-distribute/SKILL.md` and
  `skills/ac-site-polish/SKILL.md` (CLOSED; repair verified present at HEAD, so the new
  check starts green)
close_reason: Implemented and tested. Check 3 now asserts frontmatter BLOCK integrity per skills/*/SKILL.md: opens with --- on line 1, closes at the next ---, every non-blank line between is a key-shaped YAML mapping entry or an indented continuation. Key count/identity unconstrained — the six legit multi-key skills (ac-idea-lab, ac-pipeline, ac-plan-lab, ac-registry-audit, expert-consensus, openrouter) all pass. RED proof executed in a /tmp repo copy: a stray prose line inserted at frontmatter line 3 made lint exit 1 naming the file and line. lint.sh exits 0 at HEAD, 372 checks / 0 failures (was 314 — one new per-skill check x58). Delivered: lint.sh Check 3 frontmatter block-integrity assertion. Commit aafe33a.

title: Proposal: new mechanical ac-loop gates need a live multi-batch dry-run in their shipping ceremony (skills/ac-pipeline-builder/SKILL.md)
description:
## Decision memo
**Target:** skills/ac-pipeline-builder/SKILL.md (or a _shared testing-doctrine note) — the meta-skill governing how new mechanical pipeline gates ship.

**Evidence (RUN 20260719-185059-58770, cost: material):** The freshly-shipped ac-514 beads-closed-gate (skills/_shared/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh) shipped with two scoping defects found only at live ceremony use, not by its unit tests: (1) single --progress file vs parallel-wave children -> ac-0wi; (2) identity-lifetime vs batch scope -> ac-0i1. Both fixed same-run but cost ~2 extra child-spawns + 2 ceremony delays. Root cause: the gate's unit tests did not exercise ac-loop's own documented multi-batch / parallel-wave run shapes.

**Proposed change:** Add a rule to ac-pipeline-builder: a new mechanical gate wired into ac-loop must include a live multi-batch dry-run against ac-loop's documented run shapes (parallel-wave, multi-batch identity-lifetime) in its OWN shipping ceremony, not just unit tests.

**Counter-argument (Phase 2 retrospective, sonnet analyst, full-context REJECT):** Both gaps cost ~1 CLI flag + a handful of tests each, were resolved within ~1 hour, folded into ceremonies already running, with zero reverts and zero incorrect output shipped. title: ac-batch-close Act 3 report selector: teach a conductor-scope mode — content-grep assumes pending Range base == anchor, FATALs on pre-supplied artifacts scoped off a stale mark
description:
discovered-from: ac-znk.2

Observed RUN 20260802-084558-9799 (ac-znk.2): a pre-supplied `ac-review` artifact carried a conductor-defined Range (`7998b71..5891d96`; the review-mark had been stale since 2026-07-19). Act 3's content-grep selector requires the report's `Range:` BASE to equal the batch anchor, so it would have matched 0 reports and FATALed. The child used the sanctioned hand-selection escape and documented it. Fix: promote that escape into a first-class, guarded **conductor-scope mode** instead of leaving it as prose an operator must notice and apply by hand.

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03; the filing carried no anchors)

- The selector lives in `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md`, Act 3 ("Commit the Batch Report"), in the fenced bash block that begins `CARRIED=""`. Locate by grep: `grep -n 'PENDING_REPORT=' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` (`:536` on 2026-08-03 — `ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` is under active edit in a shared checkout, so grep, do not pin).
- The matcher is `PENDING_REPORT=$(grep -lE "Range:.*${ANCHOR:0:8}[0-9a-f]*\.\." .claude/reviews/pending/*.md 2>/dev/null)` — it hard-requires `Range:` base == batch anchor. Premise CONFIRMED.
- The FATAL + `exit 1` fires when the match count != 1.
- **The escape hatch already EXISTS as prose**, in the FATAL's own stderr text: "Only after verifying a report's Range actually covers $BATCH_RANGE may a conductor set PENDING_REPORT by hand." So this bead PROMOTES an existing, already-sanctioned escape into a guarded mode — it is not inventing a new bypass, and it must not weaken the "unknown never collapses to ok" rule stated two lines above it.
- The producer side is healthy: `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` § Report Destination makes the `**Range:** <base>..<head>` line MANDATORY and machine-parsed (full 40-char SHAs) in every report. So a conductor-supplied report is guaranteed to carry a parseable Range to verify against. Chain verified — no false dependency.
- The block carries an inline `net-growth-ok: bd-f72as` stamp. That stamp is ALREADY COMMITTED, so it does **not** satisfy Check 14 for a new edit — see AC 4.

## Delivers

- doc: `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` Act 3 selector — a **conductor-scope mode**: when the conductor hands down an explicit report path (e.g. `CONDUCTOR_PENDING_REPORT`) together with the batch range it was scoped against, the selector uses it INSTEAD of the anchor-equality content-grep, but only after verifying that report's own `**Range:**` line COVERS the batch range **by git ancestry** (see the coverage definition below). A report that fails that coverage check still FATALs — the mode changes which report is *considered*, never whether an unverified report may be *accepted*.

## Two hazards the fix MUST handle (found at refine round 2 — do not skip these)

**(a) `$BATCH_RANGE` is NOT in scope at the selector.** `BATCH_RANGE="$ANCHOR..HEAD"` is assigned in the *Determine the Batch Anchor* block (`grep -n 'BATCH_RANGE=' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` -> one assignment only), and only `ANCHOR` is persisted to `$STATE`. The Act 3 selector is a SEPARATE fenced bash block, so `$BATCH_RANGE` may well be empty there — this is exactly the `PROJECT_ROOT` bug class ac-vqf reproduced and ac-ji5 is fixing one file over. Note the existing FATAL text already *mentions* `\$BATCH_RANGE` (escaped, so it is prose, not an expansion) — the variable is referenced without ever being guaranteed live. **Re-derive it at the selector** (`BATCH_RANGE="${BATCH_RANGE:-$ANCHOR..HEAD}"`), and FATAL if `ANCHOR` itself is empty rather than silently computing `..HEAD`.

**(b) "covers" must be a git-ancestry test, not a string compare.** A conductor-supplied report claims `<base>..<head>`. It covers this batch iff `base` is an ancestor-or-equal of `$ANCHOR` AND `head` is a descendant-or-equal of the batch head — i.e. `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$rbase" "$ANCHOR"` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "<batch head>" "$rhead"` both exit 0. Comparing SHA text (the shape the existing anchor-equality grep uses) would accept any report whose base string happens to match and reject every legitimately wider one — which is the entire defect being fixed.

## Consumes

- none

The `**Range:**` line this mode verifies is already produced unconditionally by `ac-review` (§ Report Destination, mandatory + machine-parsed) at HEAD — there is no upstream blocker to wait on, so no `blocks` edge is warranted.

## Acceptance Criteria

Commands below were EXECUTED against HEAD on 2026-08-03; RED-now values are measured.

1. The mode exists and is named: `grep -c 'CONDUCTOR_PENDING_REPORT' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns at least 1 (RED now: **0** — executed). (The exact variable name is the implementer's choice; if a different name is chosen, update this AC's literal to match rather than leaving it stale.)
2. **The guard survives — the mode must not become an unchecked override.** The FATAL path is still reachable and still refuses unknowns: `grep -c 'unknown must never collapse to ok' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns at least 1 (currently **1** — executed), and the new mode's text explicitly states that a conductor-supplied report whose Range does NOT cover the batch range is rejected with the same FATAL.
2a. **Hazard (a) closed:** `grep -c 'BATCH_RANGE:-' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns at least 1 (RED now: **0** — executed), i.e. the selector re-derives the range instead of assuming a prior block's assignment survived. Bite-proof: run the extracted selector under `env -u BATCH_RANGE`; it must still resolve, and must FATAL (not silently proceed) when `ANCHOR` is empty.
2b. **Hazard (b) closed:** `grep -c 'merge-base --is-ancestor' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns at least 1 (RED now: **0** — executed), i.e. coverage is decided by git ancestry rather than SHA-string equality.
3. **Seam proof — this is the load-bearing AC; a doc-diff check alone is NOT sufficient.** The selector is the CONSUMER half of a producer/consumer seam whose producer is `ac-review`'s `**Range:**` writer. Extract the selector block into a scratch script (the same awk/eval extraction pattern `scripts/lint-net-growth.test.sh` uses on `lint.sh`) and drive it against three synthetic fixtures in a literal `/tmp` dir:
   - **(a) conductor mode, covering:** a pending report whose `Range:` base != `$ANCHOR` but whose range DOES cover `$BATCH_RANGE`, with the conductor variable set -> selected, no FATAL. (Goes RED if the coverage-verification half is reverted.)
   - **(b) conductor mode, NOT covering:** same but the Range does not cover `$BATCH_RANGE` -> still FATAL, exit 1. (Goes RED if the mode degrades into a blind override — this is the case a text-only AC cannot catch.)
   - **(c) legacy mode, variable unset:** existing anchor-equality content-grep behavior is unchanged — 1 match selects, 0 or 2 matches FATAL with exit 1. (Regression guard.)
   All three must be present; (a) and (b) together are what make the check fail if EITHER side of the seam alone is reverted. If the extraction proves infeasible, say so explicitly in the AC and state what is being accepted instead — do not silently downgrade to a grep.
4. **lint Check 14 (no-net-growth, per-file).** `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` is a conductor SKILL.md under the ratchet, and this bead ADDS lines to it. `lint.sh` requires a net-positive SKILL.md to carry, **in its own diff, as an ADDED line**, the literal token `<!-- net-growth-ok: <reason> -->`; a shrink in another file does not offset it and the block's pre-existing `net-growth-ok: bd-f72as` stamp does NOT count (it is already committed, not an added line in this diff). So either land the edit net <= 0 lines on that file, or add a FRESH stamp in the same diff. Verify with `git diff --numstat -- skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` plus `./lint.sh`.
5. `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` -> `exit=0`. **Assert the EXIT CODE only — never the check count.** The count drifts constantly in this shared checkout (`314` at 13:00 on 2026-08-03, `372` an hour later after siblings landed a new check).

## Test Scope

- `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` — Act 3, the `CARRIED=""` / `PENDING_REPORT=` selector block and its FATAL branch. Locate by grep (`PENDING_REPORT=`, `unknown must never collapse to ok`, `net-growth-ok: bd-f72as`), NOT by line number: this file is under concurrent edit in a shared checkout and its anchors moved during refine.
- `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` § Report Destination — READ-ONLY, as the producer contract the coverage check relies on (the mandatory `**Range:**` line).
- Fixture harness: none exists for Act 3 today (`skills/ac-batch-close/` has no `scripts/` or test file — verified). AC 3 requires building a throwaway one in `/tmp`, modelled on `scripts/lint-net-growth.test.sh`'s extract-and-drive pattern. That harness is scratch, not a deliverable.
- `./lint.sh` — Check 14 leg for AC 4, whole run for AC 5.
close_reason: Implemented and tested. Delivered: skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md Act 3 selector — CONDUCTOR_PENDING_REPORT conductor-scope mode, ancestry-verified coverage (git merge-base --is-ancestor both legs), BATCH_RANGE re-derived at the selector with a FATAL on empty ANCHOR. Seam proof (AC 3): extracted selector driven against 6 fixtures in a throwaway git repo — conductor-covering selects, conductor-NOT-covering FATALs, legacy 1/2/0-match unchanged, empty ANCHOR FATALs; 6 passed 0 failed. Check 14 satisfied by a fresh added net-growth-ok stamp. lint exit 0; commit 75bedc0

title: ac-review panel reviewer used git stash inside a worktree and leaked a planted SQL-injection + unaudited-release into the shared main checkout
description:
During the ac-review COMPLETION pass over `79a94149..b4f6f35e` (2026-07-31,
TealPuma-reviewAA), a panel reviewer spawned with worktree isolation **planted an exploitable
vulnerability into the SHARED main checkout** and left it there uncommitted. It was found and
reverted only because the conductor read the agents' self-reports and ran `git status`.

## What happened

The `guard-evasion` probe agent was given an isolated git worktree and told explicitly:
"NEVER touch the main checkout ... (read-only to you)". It nonetheless used **`git stash push`**
to park a probe. Stashes are a **repo-global** resource shared across all worktrees of the same
repository. A concurrent session popped that stash, materialising the planted code into the
main working tree at `scripts/curate-foods/lib/split-sql.ts`:

- `escalationToRelease?: string` added to `SplitSqlParams`
- an `escalationRelease` fragment emitting
  `UPDATE bca.curator_pending_escalations SET resolved_at = now() WHERE escalation_id = '${params.escalationToRelease}'`
- that fragment interpolated into the returned transaction

Two independent harms in ~14 lines: (a) it reinstates the **exact unaudited escalation-release
path** that commit `2ed92ddc` was written to delete, and (b) the interpolation is **not**
`requireValidUuid`-gated, unlike every other interpolation in that builder — a live SQL
injection into a privileged transaction.

It was undetectable by the repo's own defences: the structural guard test passes 3/3 with the
planted code present (that evasion is the subject of the sibling bead), and `pnpm type-check`
does not cover `scripts/**` (bd-jkqok).

A SECOND reviewer in the same run (`contracts`) independently ran `git checkout 79a94149 -- .`
against the shared tree, overwriting it with stale content, then repaired it with
`git show HEAD:<path>` + `git stash pop`. A THIRD (`security`) reported seeing a fully staged
revert of all six batch commits in the index mid-run.

## Why the existing doctrine did not prevent it

`ac-review`'s isolation discipline (SKILL.md § test-quality METHOD, and
`references/review-dimensions.md`) says: "All destructive probes run in a disposable worktree —
`git worktree add`, probe there, `git worktree remove --force`. To you, the shared tree is
read-only."

That is necessary but **not sufficient**. It does not name the repo-global escape hatches, and
an agent that believes it is inside an isolated worktree reasonably assumes every git operation
is also isolated. It is not:
- **`git stash` / `git stash pop`** — the stash stack is shared repo-wide.
- **`git checkout <ref> -- <path>`** — overwrites the working tree (dcg blocks this
  interactively, but not from every harness/agent).
- **`git add` / index writes** — the index is per-worktree, but a staged revert was still
  observed escaping.

Note this checkout already carries 17 stashes accumulated from prior sessions, so a stray
`git stash pop` picking up the wrong entry is a live, recurring hazard, not a one-off.

## Proposed fix (agent-compounds, `skills/ac-review/`)

1. **Name the banned operations explicitly** in the isolation-discipline block, not just the
   principle: *"`git stash`, `git stash pop`, and `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` are BANNED even
   inside a worktree — the stash stack is repo-global and checkout overwrites the shared tree.
   To park state, copy files to `/tmp`. To restore, `git show <ref>:<path> | tee <path>`."*
2. Add the same block to `_shared/delegation-contract.md` so every skill that spawns probing
   subagents inherits it, not just ac-review.
3. **Add a conductor post-panel tree check** to ac-review Phase 3: after the panel returns and
   BEFORE synthesis, run `git status --short` and diff any unexpected working-tree change
   against the reviewed range. A planted probe that escapes must be caught by the ceremony, not
   by luck. This run caught it only because two agents volunteered confessions in their reports.
4. Consider a dcg rule blocking `git stash` outright in agent sessions (this repo's own
   environment contract already bans it by prose — prose is not enforcement).

## Acceptance

- The banned-operations list appears in `ac-review/SKILL.md` and
  `_shared/delegation-contract.md`, grep-verifiable by the string `git stash`.
- ac-review Phase 3 contains a mandatory `git status --short` tree check with a documented
  action on non-empty unexpected output.
- A dry-run of ac-review on a trivial range shows the tree check executing.

title: ac-review VERDICT grammar is ambiguous for an APPROVED-after-auto-fix panel
description:
discovered-from: unknown (surfaced by ac-batch-close Act 1 on batch ac-gcj.6-20260803)

ac-review's per-bead verdict-comment grammar defines `VERDICT: passed:` for a "clean APPROVED"
and `VERDICT: failed:` "when the panel surfaced a merge-blocking finding". Those two clauses
OVERLAP: the normal, healthy ac-review outcome is a panel that surfaces Critical/High findings,
auto-fixes them in place, and lands `VERDICT: APPROVED`. Both clauses then apply, and the
reader picks one.

Live consequence in maintenance batch 2: the review child stamped all five closed beads with
`VERDICT: failed: ac-review batch-2 panel ... merge-blocking findings auto-fixed in-place`
while its own report reads `**VERDICT:** APPROVED`. A downstream reader (bv triage, ac-tidy, a
human scanning `br show`) sees a failed verdict on a bead that passed. ac-batch-close Act 1 had
to write superseding `VERDICT: passed:` comments (RUN_ID 20260803-113231-34132, batch
ac-gcj.6-20260803). Recurrence count for this anchor is 2 (batch-2 review child + the Phase-2
retrospective, which independently re-derived the same defect).

## Root cause (refine, 2026-08-03)

`passed`/`failed`/`blocked` are OUTCOME verbs. ac-review's rule keys two of the three on a
CONDITION ("the panel surfaced a merge-blocking finding") rather than on the ceremony's
outcome — so a reader with findings-that-were-fixed matches the condition and writes `failed:`.
ac-batch-close's parallel section does NOT have this defect: it keys every token on the CI
dispatch OUTCOME (green / red-X / stalled).

Executed at refine: ac-review's emitted outcome set is exactly two tokens — `VERDICT: APPROVED`
and `VERDICT: NEEDS_DECISION` (`grep -n "VERDICT: NEEDS_DECISION\|VERDICT: APPROVED"
skills/ac-review/SKILL.md`). There is NO ac-review outcome that produces `failed:`. The grammar
offers a three-token vocabulary to a two-outcome ceremony and never says which token the
unreachable third belongs to.

## RECOMMENDATION (refine's decidable answer)

Rewrite ac-review's verdict-comment rule to key on the emitted `VERDICT:` OUTCOME, mirroring
ac-batch-close:
- `VERDICT: APPROVED`        -> `VERDICT: passed:`   — INCLUDING APPROVED-after-auto-fix. The
  ceremony's outcome is what the token reports; findings existing is not failure, the ceremony
  resolving them IS the pass. Put the fixed-findings detail in the `<detail>` field.
- `VERDICT: NEEDS_DECISION`  -> `VERDICT: blocked:`  — the partial-failure / escalation gate.
- `failed:`                  -> NOT emitted by ac-review at all. Say so explicitly, and say
  what it IS for (a verifier ceremony whose subject is a pass/fail run: CI red in
  ac-batch-close, a QA repro). An unreachable token that is not labelled unreachable is exactly
  what got picked.
Keep the token set itself unchanged — `beads-standards` § Verification verdicts owns it and is
under LABEL-FREEZE; this bead disambiguates the MAPPING, it does not add or rename a token.

## Evidence (grep-anchored — do NOT re-add line numbers)

Line-number anchors are struck from this bead. The filing cited
`skills/ac-review/SKILL.md:544-545`; a later comment cited 568-570; at refine time the passage
sat at 584. This file was edited several times on 2026-08-03 (it gained a stale-mark ladder).
Anchor by grep only:
- `grep -c "VERDICT: passed:\` for a clean \`APPROVED\`" skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` = 1 — the
  overlapping clause (both tokens are on that single line). VERIFIED at refine, HEAD a5ab150.
- `grep -c "### Verdict comment (VERDICT grammar)" skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` = 1 — the owning
  section. VERIFIED at refine.
- `grep -c "### Verdict comment (VERDICT grammar)" skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` = 1 — the
  parallel section that must stay consistent. VERIFIED at refine.
- `grep -c "## Verification verdicts (structured comments)" skills/beads-standards/SKILL.md` = 1
  — the owning canon for the token set. VERIFIED at refine.
- Report: `.claude/reviews/batch/2026-08-03-1350-maintenance-batch-2.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The overlapping clause is gone.
   `grep -c "VERDICT: passed:\` for a clean \`APPROVED\`" skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns 0.
   EXECUTED at refine: returns 1 — bites.

2. The replacement states, inside ac-review's `### Verdict comment (VERDICT grammar)` section,
   that an APPROVED panel writes `passed:` even when findings were auto-fixed, and states what
   `failed:` is reserved for. Section-scoped check (a whole-file grep would pass vacuously —
   `APPROVED` appears many times in the file):
       awk '/^### Verdict comment \(VERDICT grammar\)/{f=1;next} f && /^#{1,4} /{exit} f' \
         skills/ac-review/SKILL.md | grep -ci 'auto-fix'
   must return >= 1. EXECUTED at refine: returns 0 — bites.
   USE THE FLAG-BASED awk ABOVE, NOT an awk RANGE. Refine first drafted
   `awk '/^### Verdict comment .../,/^### /'` and executed it: it returns exactly ONE line (the
   header), because the range's START pattern also matches its END pattern, so the range closes
   on the line it opened. That form returns 0 whether or not the fix landed — a non-biting AC.
   The flag-based form was executed and returns the full 14-line section; bite-proof confirmed

title: ac-tidy Tier-2 archive gate is unsound — proposal beads satisfy N_matching
description:
BUG — premise RE-VERIFIED LIVE against HEAD 2026-08-03 (refine RUN 20260803-113231-34132).

## Problem

ac-tidy's Tier-2 auto-archive gate treats ANY bead that references a plan as positive proof
the plan was implemented. `pipeline-proposal` beads — which ac-tidy itself emits nightly, and
which name plans in their "explicitly not proposed / withheld" lists — satisfy the predicate.
The gate is self-certifying: tonight's proposal to withhold becomes tomorrow's proof to
archive. It DEGRADES over time: as real implementation beads close, proposal beads become the
only remaining matches, at which point the gate passes by construction.

**The toggle is currently ON** (`skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:27` — "Tier-2 auto-archive: ON"), so
this is live, not dormant. Four consecutive nights the arithmetic said "archive" and only a
run reading the matching bead's BODY prevented archiving an un-beadified loop-ready plan.

## Anchors — FOUR independent statement sites (all verified at HEAD 2026-08-03)

A fix touching fewer than four leaves a live divergent copy. Site 5 is the file the scheduled
heartbeat actually executes.

| # | file:line | current text (verbatim fragment) |
| - | --------- | -------------------------------- |
| 1 | `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:27` | `- **Tier-2 auto-archive: ON**` — the toggle (context, NOT an edit site) |
| 2 | `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:28` | `**Positive proof, never empty-parse.** Before any Tier-2 archive: require ``N_matching > 0`` **and** ``N_closed == N_matching`` **and** the ``br list --json`` result parsed to a non-empty, expected shape.` |
| 3 | `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:119` | Phase 2b — `**Condition:** Plan frontmatter ``status: beadified`` OR plan is referenced by beads in ``br`` AND all those beads exist` |
| 4 | `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:134` | Phase 2c — `**Condition:** Plan has matching beads AND all matching beads are closed` |
| 5 | `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:95` | `positive-proof gate (``N_matching > 0`` AND ``N_closed == N_matching`` AND parseable non-empty` |

Sites 3 and 4 are the *producers* — they define what "matching" means. Sites 2 and 5 are
downstream restatements. Patching only the guardrail prose (site 2) leaves the real match
query untouched; patching only SKILL.md leaves the nightly heartbeat running the old logic.

## Approach

**(a) is REQUIRED — this is not an implementer's choice.** Exclude beads carrying the
`pipeline-proposal` label from `N_matching`, at sites 2–5. AC 2 below is a line-located grep for
`pipeline-proposal`; an implementer who instead picks (b) satisfies the bug's *intent* but FAILS
AC 2 as written. (Round-3 correction: the earlier phrasing offered (a)/(b) as equal options while
the ACs only accepted (a) — a criterion both branches don't satisfy identically gates nothing,
`bead-conventions.md` § Falsifiable ACs.)

**(b) is an optional STRENGTHENING on top of (a), never a substitute:** additionally require at
least one matching bead to be an *implementation* bead (`issue_type` ∈ task/bug/feature), never a
`decision`-typed proposal/withhold record. If you want (b) INSTEAD of (a), amend the ACs first —
do not silently swap.

Preferred secondary cleanup: collapse `nightly.md:95`'s restatement into a pointer at the
single SKILL.md guardrail, so the predicate has ONE home and cannot drift a fifth time.

**Line numbers drift as you edit.** The table above pins each site by line AND by verbatim text
at HEAD 2026-08-03. Anchor on the TEXT; re-run AC 1's grep after each edit to re-locate the
remaining sites rather than trusting the original line numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All four edit sites carry the exclusion.** The definition of a matching bead at
   `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:28`, `:119`, `:134` and `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:95`
   excludes `pipeline-proposal`-labelled beads — OR nightly.md's copy is replaced by a pointer
   to the single SKILL.md definition, leaving no second predicate anywhere.
   Check (EXECUTED at HEAD 2026-08-03, currently RED — this is the RED-before-GREEN baseline):
   `grep -rn 'N_matching\|matching beads\|referenced by beads' skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md`
   → today returns exactly 4 hits (SKILL.md:28, :119, :134, nightly.md:95), **none** of them
   mentioning `pipeline-proposal`. After the fix every surviving hit must sit adjacent to an
   exclusion clause, or be gone.
2. **The exclusion reaches the gate, not just the emit path.**
   Check (EXECUTED at HEAD, baseline = `2`): `grep -n 'pipeline-proposal' skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md`
   → today returns exactly lines **19** and **287**, both about *emitting* proposal beads,
   neither in a gate predicate. After the fix this grep must return a hit on **each** of lines
   28, 119 and 134 (or on whatever lines those three predicates then occupy). A bare count
   increase does NOT satisfy this — an unrelated mention elsewhere in the file would raise the
   count while leaving the gate unsound. The assertion is line-located, not counted.
3. **A worked negative example is recorded in the SKILL text.** The 2026-07-28 case (sole
   match `bd-pzlhv`, N_matching=1 / N_closed=1, for BOTH remaining loop-ready plans) must not
   arm the gate under the new predicate, and the derivation is stated inline in the guardrail
   bullet so a future reader can re-check it without this bead.
4. **The gate is narrowed, not silently disabled.** After the fix, a plan whose only matching
   beads are `pipeline-proposal` beads falls through to a **Tier-3 proposal** (the existing
   documented fall-through at `SKILL.md:18` / `nightly.md:100`), never to a silent no-op and
   never to an archive.

## Test Scope

- Doc/skill-text change. **NO executable test harness exists for this gate** —
  EXECUTED at HEAD: `find skills/ac-tidy -iname '*test*'` → empty; `ls skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/`
  → bead-refine-concurrent-dir.test.sh, beads-closed-gate.sh, beads-closed-gate.test.sh,
  ci-gate-health.test.sh, claim-race-harness.sh, run-id-concurrent-dir.test.sh,
  validate-qa-run.sh, verification-gate-class.test.sh — none covers ac-tidy.
- Verification is therefore **grep-based** (ACs 1–2, both runnable in-repo and RED today)
  plus a **read-through** of the four sites (ACs 3–4).
- **UNRUNNABLE HERE (explicitly labelled, do not fake it):** end-to-end proof needs a real
  nightly ac-tidy run against a board where a plan's only match is a proposal bead. No AC
  above claims to execute that.
- OPTIONAL follow-up, NOT required to close: a
  `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/ac-tidy-gate-proposal-exclusion.test.sh` asserting the predicate
  text at all four sites. File separately if wanted; do not block this bead on it.

## Delivers
- doc: skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md — NIGHTLY Guardrails positive-proof gate (:28) + Phase 2b (:119) / 2c (:134) match conditions, with proposal-bead exclusion
- doc: skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md — Tier-2 bullet (:95), same exclusion or collapsed to a pointer

## Evidence

  (path verified present; supersedes `2026-07-25/app-local-ac-tidy-matching-defects.md` §3)
- `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/last-run.json` — the recurrence record and the standing
  recommendation to flip the toggle OFF
- Recurrences: 2026-07-24 (sole match `bd-b917c`, withheld correctly) · 2026-07-26 (sole match
  `bd-pzlhv`; fix recommended, unapplied) · 2026-07-28 session 3f835ebf (gate PASSED for BOTH
  remaining loop-ready plans, 1/1 each) · 2026-07-29 reflect-gap session 25c3e9d5
  (entry-floating-corner-controls, 1/1)
- **Board note (round-2 correction):** `bd-b917c`, `bd-pzlhv` and `bd-89vfd` are **not on this
  repo's board** — VERIFIED at HEAD 2026-08-03: `br show <id>` fails for all three here. They
  live on the **body-compass-app** board (`~/Repos/neometa/software/body-compass-app/.beads/`),
  which is where ac-tidy runs nightly. Resolve them there when re-deriving AC 3's worked
  example; do not read their absence here as a falsified premise.

title: ac-triage scheduled-daily: give it ac-tidy's worktree preflight, removing the branch-guard abort's cause
description:
BUG — premise RE-VERIFIED LIVE against HEAD 2026-08-03 (refine RUN 20260803-113231-34132).
Latent, not a live outage: the detached checkout that triggered it has since self-resolved.
The structural asymmetry that let it happen is unchanged.

## Problem

ac-triage's scheduled daily run aborts wholesale on a branch-guard failure it has no way to
survive, and the abort is designed so it cannot file the bead that would escalate itself.

**What happened (2026-07-27, body-compass-app, reflect-gap session d35cfce4):** the daily run
aborted at step 0. `git branch --show-current` did not equal `main` — the app checkout was in
detached HEAD at `df29cfe8` while main was at `4fc66cfd`. Zero sources fetched, zero
watermarks advanced, no beads, no `triage-last-run.md`. The detached state persisted across at
least three sessions that night (d35cfce4, 2530fb78, 3f835ebf — all logged `@HEAD`), so the
abort repeated every cycle while pulling no signal.

**DEFECT (in scope) — the asymmetry.** ac-tidy already solved this class by running NIGHTLY
inside an isolated worktree cut from fresh `origin/main`; its own workflow states the
branch-guard aborts "can no longer fire" as a result. ac-triage has NO worktree isolation, so
it stays vulnerable to a condition its sibling is structurally immune to. Triage is read-mostly
(fetch sources, advance a watermark, file beads), making it an EASIER worktree candidate than
tidy, not a harder one.

**DEFECT 2 (conditional — see § Scope below) — the abort eats its own escalation.** The
skeleton says anything needing a human becomes an ops/`human-gate` bead + a Slack mention,
never a prompt. But filing a bead writes `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which the zero-write abort
forbids. So the one failure that trips the guard is exactly the one that cannot produce a bead;
Slack becomes the sole escalation channel, and if Slack delivery fails the abort is completely
silent.

## Anchors (verified at HEAD 2026-08-03)

| file:line | verbatim / state |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| `skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md:22-24` | `- **Branch guard (first, before any reads or writes):** ``git branch --show-current`` must equal ``main``. If it doesn't — **ABORT the entire run**: Slack ``degraded`` with reason ``branch-guard: <branch> checked out``, zero writes, retry next cycle.` |
| `skills/ac-triage/` (whole tree) | contains **no** worktree isolation — EXECUTED at HEAD: `grep -rln worktree skills/ac-triage/` returns nothing. Files present: SKILL.md, triage.template.md, workflows/scheduled-daily.md, references/feedback-adapter.md |
| `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:23-68` | the pattern to copy — `git worktree add --detach` off fresh `origin/main` into `$TIDY_WT`, abort-with-ops-bead if it cannot be created, `cd "$TIDY_WT"`, mandatory teardown at step 8 on **every** exit path, **and the beads-DB rehydration bullet at :63-68** (do NOT stop the copy at :49 — see AC 5) |
| `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:126-136` | the commit/push shape a detached worktree needs — `AGENT_NAME=<name> git commit … -- <exact files>` then `git push --no-verify origin HEAD:main` (see AC 6) |
| `skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md:63-70` | § 4 Commit + push, currently "Commit on `main` with `AGENT_NAME=<name>` inline" — stale the moment step 0 goes detached (AC 6) |
| `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:47` | the consequence sentence the original filing cited: "the old dirty-live-tree / branch-guard aborts can no longer fire". Minor anchor drift, recorded not smoothed: the isolation **setup** starts at :23-44; `:47` is the consequence, not the setup. Immaterial to the claim. |

## Scope — what "done" means (this was ambiguous in the original filing; it is now single-valued)

**This bead is DONE when DEFECT 1 lands: ac-triage gets ac-tidy's worktree preflight.** That
fix removes the branch guard's reason to exist rather than making the guard smarter, and it
moots **the branch-guard instance** of DEFECT 2 — inside a fresh clean worktree there is no
branch-guard abort left to suppress the escalation.

**Precision (round-2 correction — the earlier "moots DEFECT 2" was too broad):** one pre-write
abort path SURVIVES by design — worktree *creation* failure (AC 4). That is accepted precedent,
not a residual bug: `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:38-41` handles tidy's own
worktree-creation failure with a Slack/ops escalation and `exit 0`, deliberately writing
nothing into the app checkout. Verified against the full `scheduled-daily.md`: the branch guard
is the ONLY current pre-write abort (source-fetch failures already file beads, per § 1). So
DEFECT 2's *general* shape is closed by DEFECT 1 everywhere except the creation-failure path,
which AC 4 covers explicitly.

**DEFECT 2 is a conditional fallback, not additional required work.** Do NOT implement it
alongside DEFECT 1. If DEFECT 1 is deferred or judged too large, file DEFECT 2 as its own bead
(narrow carve-out in the zero-write rule: one ops bead describing the abort, written on a temp
branch/worktree cut from `origin/<default>` so it never touches the detached checkout) and say
so in a comment here. A guard that suppresses its own alarm is worse than a guard that writes
one file — but the right fix is to delete the guard's cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` § 0 Preflight creates an isolated
   worktree** cut from fresh `origin/<default-branch>`, and every subsequent step runs with
   `cwd` inside it — mirroring `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:23-68` IN FULL (see AC 5 — do not stop at :49).

   **ADAPT, do not transcribe (round-4 finding).** ac-tidy's block hardcodes its own app root
   at `nightly.md:33`: `BCA="$HOME/Repos/neometa/software/body-compass-app"`. ac-triage is
   **app-generic** — `scheduled-daily.md` runs `cwd`'d into whichever app scheduled it (see its
   own § 0 Slack-probe note, "absolute path — this job runs `cwd`'d into the app"). Copying
   tidy's line verbatim would pin ac-triage to body-compass-app. Capture the root from the
   invocation instead, BEFORE any `cd`:
   `APP_ROOT="$(git -C "$(pwd)" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`, then fetch/worktree from
   `$APP_ROOT`. Same substitution applies to every other `$BCA` reference in the copied block.
   Check (EXECUTED at HEAD 2026-08-03, currently RED — baseline is zero hits):
   `grep -rln worktree skills/ac-triage/` → must return at least
   `skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md`.
2. **The branch guard at `scheduled-daily.md:22-24` is REMOVED or demoted**, with the removal
   justified inline the way `nightly.md:44-48` justifies tidy's ("the old branch-guard aborts
   can no longer fire; the real single-writer guard is now the fresh-checkout isolation").
   Check: `grep -n 'show-current' skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` → today
   returns line 22; after the fix it returns nothing, or only a line inside the worktree-setup
   block.
3. **Teardown is mandatory on EVERY exit path**, including aborts — the worktree is removed
   before the run exits, matching tidy's step-8 rule. State it explicitly; a leaked `/tmp`
   worktree per day is its own defect.
4. **Worktree-creation failure has its own abort path** that does NOT depend on writing into
   the app checkout — mirror `nightly.md:38-41` (Slack/ops escalation, `exit 0`, retry next
   cycle). This is the one place the zero-write concern legitimately survives; name it.
   **Use ac-triage's OWN Slack vocabulary, not tidy's flags** (round-4 finding): the existing
   skeleton escalates with a plain `TRIAGE DEGRADED: <reason>` line and has no `--card`/
   `--status` idiom. Run `slack-send --help` and match what ac-triage already emits rather than
   copying tidy's invocation shape. (Known standing gap: `slack-send` has no `--dry-run` — the
   § 0 probe prints "unrecognized arguments" AND exits 0. Do not add a new dependency on it.)
5. **BEADS DB REHYDRATION — the silent-regression trap (round-3 finding; without this the fix
   ships a NEW daily defect).** `br`'s local SQLite DB is **gitignored**, so a fresh worktree
   starts with only the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` and no `.db`. ac-triage's whole Phase-3
   value is *dedupe against open beads* — against an empty DB that dedup **false-misses on every
   run**, silently re-filing the same beads daily. The fix MUST carry over
   `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:63-68` verbatim in intent: run `br sync` (or `br list`)
   once from inside the worktree **before any `br create`/`br close`**, and keep all `br` ops in
   the worktree so step 4 commits the flushed `.beads/issues.jsonl` from there.
   Check: `grep -n 'br sync\|Rehydrate' skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` → today
   (EXECUTED at HEAD 2026-08-03) returns nothing; after the fix it must return the rehydration
   step, positioned before the first `br create`.
6. **§ 4 Commit + push is updated for a detached worktree.**
   `skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md:69` currently says "Commit on `main` with
   `AGENT_NAME=<name>` inline" — that is stale prose the moment step 0 checks out detached.
   Mirror `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:126-136`: commit inside the worktree with
   `AGENT_NAME` inline and a pathspec-scoped `--` file list (never `git add -A`), then
   `git push --no-verify origin HEAD:main`, then verify the origin SHA equals local HEAD.
   Check: `grep -n 'HEAD:main' skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md` → today returns
   nothing; after the fix it must return the push line.
7. **The symlink caveat is carried over.** `.claude/skills/ac-triage` is a *relative* symlink
   into agent-compounds and does NOT resolve from inside a `/tmp` worktree — the fix must
   reference skill files via the live checkout path, exactly as `nightly.md:56-63` warns for
   ac-tidy. A worktree fix that ignores this breaks the run on the first read.

## Test Scope

- Doc/skill-text change to a scheduled workflow. **No proof-script family exists for
  ac-triage** — EXECUTED at HEAD: `ls skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/` contains nothing ac-triage
  related (bead-refine-concurrent-dir.test.sh, beads-closed-gate.sh, beads-closed-gate.test.sh,
  ci-gate-health.test.sh, claim-race-harness.sh, run-id-concurrent-dir.test.sh,
  validate-qa-run.sh, verification-gate-class.test.sh). Do not invent an anchor in it.
- Verification is **grep-based** (ACs 1–2, both runnable in-repo and RED today) plus a
  **read-through diff against `skills/ac-tidy/workflows/nightly.md:23-68` and `:126-136`** confirming ACs 3–7
  each have a named counterpart.
- **UNRUNNABLE HERE (explicitly labelled):** proving the abort no longer fires requires a real
  scheduled ac-triage run against a genuinely detached app checkout. No AC above claims to
  execute that. The first post-fix nightly `triage-last-run.md` is the real-world confirmation.

## Delivers
- doc: skills/ac-triage/workflows/scheduled-daily.md — § 0 Preflight worktree isolation (cut from fresh origin/default, mandatory teardown, worktree-creation abort path), branch guard removed/demoted

## Consumes

title: Proposal: dcg guard false-positives block legitimate scratch-dir cleanup + descriptive prose (global PreToolUse hook)
description:
## Decision memo
**Target:** global destructive-command-guard PreToolUse hook (configured in ~/.claude settings; doctrine ref: skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md). NOT an agent-compounds in-repo script — HUMAN-gated because it edits live agent policy with no downstream CI gate.

**Evidence (this session, RUN 20260716-111224-31570):** the dcg guard false-positived 3-4 times across waves, each costing a blocked call + reissue:
- implement tt9.1 (snapshot-clone): guard blocked recursive-force deletion of a session-owned scratch /tmp dir; forced clone-to-fresh-dir workaround. Guard ALSO pattern-matched the friction-note prose describing the block.
- refine ac-ap2 (disposition-comment): guard false-positived on descriptive prose that merely QUOTED a destructive command inside a bead comment body; workaround was br comments add -f <file>.
- implement ac-d29 (cleanup): guard blocked bulk-deletion idioms on the session's OWN /tmp probe dirs; forced per-file explicit-path deletion then empty-dir removal (explicitly logged as 'second guard-prose false-positive this run').

**Recurrence:** appears 3-4x in a single run; two distinct failure modes (a) real deletes of session-owned scratch /tmp dirs, (b) descriptive prose that merely names a destructive command. Clears the T2 objective bar on material aggregate cost + intra-run recurrence.

**Proposed change (options for Craig):**
1. Scope-exempt session-owned /tmp scratch dirs (bead-work-*, *-probe, timestamped clones) from the recursive-delete block, OR
2. Only pattern-match ACTUAL tool invocations, not descriptive prose inside comment/heredoc bodies (the prose false-positive is the higher-frequency, lower-risk mode), OR
3. Document the two sanctioned workarounds (clone-to-fresh-dir; -f file for comment bodies) in 10_dcg.md so agents stop rediscovering them.

**Recommendation:** apply-modified — pursue (2) as lowest-risk highest-yield (prose false-positives are pure noise), and adopt (3) as a cheap immediate mitigation regardless. (1) needs care (scratch-dir allowlist must be tight). Demoted friction siblings this land: recurring Worker-cost handoff gap (batch-close closer never receives per-child token totals); refine premise-check on since-retired doctrine; schema-optional != runtime-accepts-null — all filed as T3 memory observations.
close_reason: Decided: option 3 done in 10_dcg.md; options 1+2 upstream as ac-f1i (Craig 2026-07-17). Guard config untouched.

The rule advertises the find-under-temp form as an allowed alternative, but it is still blocked in practice, so the headless teardown sweep cannot run — RUN_ID-scoped /tmp dirs were left for a future age-gate to reap. Bonus self-demonstration of the descriptive-prose false-positive class: an initial attempt to file THIS very comment was itself blocked because the prose quoted the two dangerous command literals verbatim (rule fired on the quoted argument text of a br command). Also blocked a benign env-probe earlier this land (redirect-truncate FP on a piped sed).

comments.text:
DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-17): **option 3 locally now; options 1 AND 2 go upstream** — amended from the memo's ranking after live verification of dcg's config surface.

Verified 2026-07-17 (dcg 0.6.5): the local allowlist is RULE-granular only (`dcg allow <rule-id>`, optional expiry, user/project scope) — no path patterns. So option 1 (exempt session-owned scratch dirs) cannot be done tightly locally: allowlisting the recursive-delete rule would disable it everywhere. Option 2 (match invocations, not quoted prose) is a parser change inside a third-party compiled binary — an upstream feature, not a local edit.

Executed at close:
- Option 3: sanctioned workarounds documented in skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md ("Known False-Positives — Sanctioned Workarounds"): (a) pass prose bodies by file (br comments add -f <file>), (b) per-file delete + rmdir, or clone-to-fresh-dir, for session scratch dirs — plus an explicit warning NOT to allowlist whole rules for this.
- Options 1+2: upstream ask filed as ac-f1i (check newest dcg release first — 0.6.5 may be behind).

No live guard config was changed — the guard stays at full strength.

title: ac-review SKILL.md hardcodes .claude/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py — wrong path in the registry repo where canon lives under skills/
description:
discovered-from: ac-znk.2

Observed RUN 20260802-084558-9799 (ac-znk.2): a review child's Phase 3 consensus invocation failed once because `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` builds `CONSENSUS` from the repo root plus `.claude/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py`; in agent-compounds (the canonical registry) the script lives at `skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py`. The harness-agnostic rule also applies — never hardcode `.claude/` paths in shared skills (memory: `harness-agnostic-skill-text`).

**ANCHOR PINNED at refine round 1, re-verified round 2 (2026-08-03, at HEAD):**

- The single defective line is `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md:487`.
- The other `.claude/` references in that file were audited and are NOT in scope: they are genuine runtime artifact paths (`.claude/reviews/...`) or prose SKILL_HINT examples that are meant to read as a consuming app's layout.
- Layout evidence for the fix: agent-compounds has a top-level `skills/` dir and no `.claude/skills/ac-review`; consuming apps (e.g. body-compass-app — confirmed: no top-level `skills/`) have `.claude/skills/ac-review` symlinked back to `agent-compounds/skills/ac-review`. A probe-both-roots resolution was DRY-RUN in both layouts during refine round 2 and resolves correctly in each.
- `python3 skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py --help` exits 0 at HEAD (executed 2026-08-03) — the script itself is healthy; only its path resolution is wrong.

**DECISION (refine round 1) — the original body offered two unreconciled fixes ('resolve relative to the SKILL.md's own location OR probe both roots'). Pinned to probe-both-roots.** A markdown skill file has no reliable self-path at bash runtime, so the relative-to-own-location option is dropped.

**DECISION (refine round 2) — keep the file's existing `PROJECT_ROOT` NAME, do NOT mint a new variable.** `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md:35` already sets `PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`, and the sibling `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md:143` uses the same name. An earlier draft of this bead pinned `REPO_ROOT`, which would have failed a fixer who correctly followed the file's own convention.

**CORRECTION (refine round 3) — `PROJECT_ROOT` must be RE-DERIVED inside the snippet; do not assume it is still set.** Round 2's rationale ("in scope through Phase 3 in the same continuous conductor session") conflated *conductor session* with *shell process* and was wrong. `:35` and `:487` sit in different fenced bash blocks separated by ~10 more blocks and the Phase-2 subagent spawns; the same file states at `:747` and `:910` that exports do not survive across bash calls. Reproduced during refine round 3: running the if/else with `PROJECT_ROOT` unset resolved `CONSENSUS` to `/.claude/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py` and `python3 "$CONSENSUS" --help` exited 2 — the exact failure class this bead exists to close, moved one variable later. Fix uses the mint-if-absent shape already conventional in this file for `RUN_ID`. Verified 2026-08-03 in a fresh shell with `PROJECT_ROOT` unset: resolves to the registry path, `--help` exit 0.

## Delivers

- doc: `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md:487` — `CONSENSUS` resolved by a both-roots probe off the file's existing `PROJECT_ROOT` (registry layout preferred, harness layout as fallback), no single hardcoded `.claude/` path

## Consumes

- none — single-line doc fix; no upstream blocker

## Approach (advisory)

Reference shape (dry-run in both layouts during refine round 2; the mint-if-absent line re-verified in a fresh shell during round 3):

```
PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"
if [ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py" ]; then
  CONSENSUS="$PROJECT_ROOT/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py"
else
  CONSENSUS="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py"
fi
```

## Acceptance Criteria

Every command below was EXECUTED against HEAD on 2026-08-03; the RED-now results are measured.

1. `grep -c 'PROJECT_ROOT/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns at least 1.
   RED now: returns `0` (executed 2026-08-03). NOTE — an absence-only AC would be wrong here: the sanctioned fix legitimately KEEPS a `.claude/skills/...` string as the fallback branch, so the check must be the presence of the registry-first branch, never the absence of `.claude/`.
2. The resolution block, run from the agent-compounds root, resolves to a file that exists, and `python3 "$CONSENSUS" --help` exits 0. Executed at HEAD 2026-08-03 against `skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py`: exit 0, prints `usage: consensus.py [-h] --artifacts-dir ARTIFACTS_DIR [--round ROUND] [--expect EXPECT]`.
3. No new root variable is introduced: `grep -c 'REPO_ROOT' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns `0` (its value at HEAD 2026-08-03, so this AC must stay true rather than become true; verified literally — `PROJECT_ROOT` does not substring-match `REPO_ROOT`).
4. **`PROJECT_ROOT` is re-derived inside the block, not inherited.** Check: `grep -cE 'PROJECT_ROOT:[-=]' skills/ac-review/SKILL.md` returns at least 1. RED now: `0` (executed 2026-08-03). The check is **idiom-agnostic on purpose** — it accepts both `"${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(…)}"` and the equally-correct `: "${PROJECT_ROOT:=$(…)}"`; an exact-string grep for only the first was rejected at refine round 4 as over-tight (it fails a correct fix). Bite-proof: with `PROJECT_ROOT` unset in a fresh shell, the block must still resolve to an existing file and `python3 "$CONSENSUS" --help` must exit 0 — measured 2026-08-03, resolves to `<repo>/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py`, exit 0; WITHOUT the mint-if-absent line the same probe resolved to `/.claude/skills/ac-review/scripts/consensus.py` and exited 2.
5. `./lint.sh` stays green. Measured at HEAD 2026-08-03: `lint: 314 checks, 0 failures`.
6. **OUT OF SCOPE, do not edit under this bead:** `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md:383` hardcodes `$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh` — the same defect class, different skill. Verified present at HEAD 2026-08-03 and captured separately as ac-ji5; a fix that also edits ac-loop fails this bead's scope, and a reviewer must not read that line's survival as this bead being incomplete.

## Test Scope
