description:
discovered-from: ac-j4u

Doctrine-delta check-0 (provenance leak) flagged added skill text carrying the edit's
story. Reviewers DISAGREED at filing, so this routed to refine. **Refine has now decided
the general rule and executed the test per-site — this bead is a mechanical apply.**

## The rule (DECIDED at refine, 2026-08-03 — do not re-litigate site-by-site)

Canon is `skills/skill-builder/references/structure-standard.md` § "Provenance never lives
in skill text":

> Exemptions, kept MINIMAL: machine-read tokens (`net-growth-ok:` — bare token + tersest
> reason; `diet:`/`mirror:` markers), and a bare rule-ID **only when other files grep it
> as a name** (e.g. an invariant's `bd-*` handle). A date, a director, or a narrative
> clause is never exempt.

Applied: **strip the tail, keep the rule.** A bead-ID wrapped in a narrative clause
("decision X", "harm-scoped by Y", "dream Z", "MODE (W)") is a narrative clause and is
never exempt — the >1-file proxy the filing proposed is WEAKER than canon and refine
rejects it: what earns exemption is another file grepping the ID **as a rule name**, not
the same prose leak appearing twice.

**Machine-token forms are EXEMPT and MUST SURVIVE untouched.**

## Decided site list (criterion EXECUTED at refine time, 2026-08-03)

`grep -rl -- "<id>" skills/` run per ID. All results: 1 file each, except ac-ewgr.7.

| Site | File | Anchor to grep | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (HIGH) | `skills/ac-pipeline/SKILL.md` | `20260719-185059-58770` | **STRIP** — 1 file; bare RUN id is pure provenance, greps nowhere else. Also strip the surrounding "Motivating incident ... considered and REJECTED (decision ac-n7h) ... self-healed within ~1h through the bug lane with zero reverts" narrative. Keep the RULE the block teaches. |
| 2 | `skills/ac-land/SKILL.md` | `harm-scoped by` | **STRIP** the clause "(decision `ac-4an`, harm-scoped by `ac-zqj`)". Both IDs: 1 file each. Keep "**Pre-commit guard.**" and its rule text. |
| 3 | `skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` | `CONDUCTOR-SCOPE MODE (ac-nsb)` | **STRIP** the ` (ac-nsb)` only. 1 file. NOTE: `grep -c "CONDUCTOR-SCOPE MODE"` returns 2 — the other hit is an internal cross-reference carrying no bead-ID; leave it alone. |
| 4 | `skills/jef-flywheel/lessons/10_dcg.md` | `probe matrix re-run` | **STRIP** the bare dates: "(probe matrix re-run 2026-08-03)" and "decision ac-umq, 2026-07-17". A date is never exempt. Keep "Refreshed against **dcg 0.6.7**" — a version is behaviour-relevant, not provenance. |
| 5 | `skills/ac-loop/SKILL.md` | `dream ac-fxq` | **STRIP the prose clause only** — "(precondition check, dream ac-fxq)". `grep -c` returns 2: the OTHER hit is `<!-- net-growth-ok: dream ac-fxq Phase-0 tooling-bug precondition check -->`, the **sanctioned machine-token exemption under structure-standard § Provenance**. Do NOT strip it — it is not a leak, it is the exempt form, and it is the artifact this whole rule protects. (Refine round-2 correction: an earlier draft claimed removing it would HARD-FAIL lint Check 14. That is FALSE and was verified false by reading `lint.sh` — Check 14 PASSes any net-neutral-or-shrinking file diff without consulting the stamp, so a lone deletion would pass silently. | 6 | `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` | `decision ac-ewgr.7` | **STRIP** the clause. |
| 7 | `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md` | `decision ac-ewgr.7` | **STRIP** the clause. |

**ac-ewgr.7 adjudication (refine, executed):** `grep -rl -- "ac-ewgr.7" skills/` returns 3

`skills/ac-bead-refine/FRICTIONS.md`. It does NOT earn the exemption: sites 6 and 7 are the

one of the sanctioned provenance channels canon names**, so it legitimately keeps the ID
and must be left untouched. Strip 6 and 7; do not edit FRICTIONS.md.

A split by file/gate was proposed. Rejected: the bead's own coherence requirement is
"decide the general rule first, then apply it to all sites at once — do not fix
site-by-site with different answers." The rule is now decided above, which is what made
the split's rationale moot. The net-growth sequencing concern is handled by the dep edge
instead (this bead now blocks ac-i5l9.1).

  must remain **1**. This pair is the bite-proof, and it is load-bearing precisely because

- No QA modality (doc-canon only).

title: ac-implement Phase 0: make the per-child bead-work discriminator UNCONDITIONAL (currently comment-only opt-in) + add bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh
description:
BUG — **PARTIAL PREMISE FAILURE, RESCOPED by refine 2026-08-03** (RUN 20260803-113231-34132).
The original body described the whole fix as outstanding. Half of it shipped the same day
(commit `3532347`). Everything below is the verified residue; do not re-derive the landed half.

## What ALREADY SHIPPED (verified at HEAD 2026-08-03 — do NOT redo)

- `skills/ac-pipeline/references/run-id.md:103` — the fan-out corollary is extended to the
  `bead-work` prefix and names this bead by id: "The same corollary binds `bead-work` under
  fan-out (ac-wno: two implement children over ONE claimed batch derived the identical
  `/tmp/bead-work-<claim-id>-<RUN_ID>` and collided on progress.md — benign only by timing):
  an implement child that knows it is one of N appends its own `<AGENT_NAME>-$$`
  discriminator." **The doctrine half is DONE.**
- `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md:213-216` — a four-line `#`-commented FAN-OUT note documenting
  the discriminator. **Documented, but see below: this is opt-in, not the parity the bead asks
  for.**

## The residue — what is ACTUALLY still broken

**(1) The derivation is OPT-IN, not unconditional — it does not match the precedent this bead
cites.** `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md:212` still reads, as live instruction:

    ARTIFACTS_DIR="/tmp/bead-work-${CLAIM_ID}${RUN_ID:+-$RUN_ID}"

…and the discriminator arrives only via `:216`, which is a **shell comment**:

    # ARTIFACTS_DIR="${ARTIFACTS_DIR}-${AGENT_NAME}-$$"

guarded by a `:213` comment that begins "FAN-OUT (one of N children over ONE claimed batch —
the delegation prompt says so)". So the safety fires only if the child both notices the note
and correctly self-identifies as one of N. That is the *exact* failure mode that produced the
original collision: an agent under context pressure not tracking that it is one of N.

The sibling fix this bead explicitly cites as its model (bd-baudw, bead-refine) is
**unconditional** — `skills/ac-bead-refine/SKILL.md:34-35` and
`skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md:64-71` key `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` on
`<AGENT_NAME>-<pid>` *always*, for every child, fanned out or not, with `RUN_ID` trailing so
the run-scoped glob still works. ac-implement does not. "Apply the corollary the same way
bd-baudw fixed bead-refine" is therefore not yet satisfied.

**(2) No proof script exists.** EXECUTED at HEAD: `ls skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/ | grep -i bead-work`
returns nothing. The two existing dir-collision scripts do NOT cover this case:
`bead-refine-concurrent-dir.test.sh` covers the bead-refine prefix, and
`run-id-concurrent-dir.test.sh` covers cross-conductor collisions (different CLAIM_ID or
different RUN_ID) — neither covers **same-batch sibling children** (identical CLAIM_ID *and*
identical RUN_ID), which is precisely the collision observed.

## Original observation (unchanged, for context)

RUN `20260802-084558-9799` (ac-znk.2 loop-lite ablation): the conductor split one claimed batch
(claim id `ac-gcj.8-20260802`) across 2 parallel ac-implement children; both derived the SAME
`/tmp/bead-work-ac-gcj.8-20260802-20260802-084558-9799`, because claim-id and RUN_ID are
batch/run-scoped, not child-scoped. The collision was benign only because the children appended
to `progress.md` at non-overlapping moments; concurrent writes could clobber per-bead entries
and hard-fail — or worse, distort — the `beads-closed-gate --progress` completeness check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The discriminator is UNCONDITIONAL in ac-implement Phase 0, and `RUN_ID` trails LAST.**
   `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` § Phase 0 computes `ARTIFACTS_DIR` with a per-child
   discriminator the child derives for itself (`<AGENT_NAME>-$$`), for every implement session
   — not behind a "if the delegation prompt says you are one of N" comment.

   **The commented line at `:216` is ITSELF WRONG — do not simply uncomment it.** It reads
   `# ARTIFACTS_DIR="${ARTIFACTS_DIR}-${AGENT_NAME}-$$"`, appending the discriminator *after*
   the `RUN_ID` suffix that `:212` already built. That yields
   `/tmp/bead-work-<claim>-<run-id>-<agent>-<pid>`, which the run-scoped glob
   `/tmp/bead-work-*-$RUN_ID` **does not match** (VERIFIED by shell `case` at HEAD 2026-08-03:
   `/tmp/bead-work-claim1-20260803-1132-AgentX-999` vs pattern `/tmp/bead-work-*-20260803-1132`
   → NO MATCH), silently breaking ac-land's gathering (`run-id.md:80`, `:138`). The correct
   shape composes the child key BEFORE the RUN_ID suffix, exactly as the cited precedent does
   at `skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md:64-71`:

       CHILD_ID="$(printf '%s' "${AGENT_NAME:-anon}" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9')-$$"
       ARTIFACTS_DIR="/tmp/bead-work-${CLAIM_ID}-${CHILD_ID}${RUN_ID:+-$RUN_ID}"

   **Ordering note (round-4, sanity-check don't assume):** this reads `$AGENT_NAME` at Phase 0,
   *before* ac-implement's own "Register Session Identity" step further down `SKILL.md`
   (:219-226). The `${AGENT_NAME:-anon}` fallback plus `$$` means the key is still unique when
   the name is not yet exported — and this is exactly the shipped, regression-tested
   ac-bead-refine precedent — but confirm it holds under ac-implement's ordering rather than
   inferring it by analogy. If it does not, either move the identity mint ahead of Phase 0 or
   note the fallback behaviour explicitly in the SKILL text.

   Check (EXECUTED at HEAD 2026-08-03, currently RED):
   `grep -n 'ARTIFACTS_DIR' skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` → today line 212 is the live
   assignment with no discriminator and line 216 is the RUN_ID-breaking variant behind a
   leading `#`. After the fix, the live (uncommented) assignment must itself contain the
   discriminator with `RUN_ID` last, and no `#`-prefixed conditional variant may remain as the
   only carrier.
2. **A proof script exists and passes.** New
   `skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/bead-work-concurrent-dir.test.sh`.
   **Clone base — use `run-id-concurrent-dir.test.sh`, NOT the bead-refine one** (round-3

skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md, in its "moved to ac-publish" list, says:

      (feature-branch / on-demand) and becomes ac-publish's heavy pre-tag gate (bd-pwt44.6);
      batch-close keeps only the single light VERDICT pass described in Act 2 below.

The parenthetical is stale. ac-review is DUAL-MODE at HEAD:

- `main` is the PRIMARY (trunk-direct) mode and the feature branch is LEGACY;

that panel is what gates batch-close on trunk. Found by ac-review's contracts lens; not
auto-fixed because the file sits outside the originating batch's pathspec.

Retarget the parenthetical to current reality — name BOTH modes (trunk-direct batch on `main`
= primary; feature branch = legacy) and keep the `ac-publish` pre-tag-gate clause intact. Do
NOT delete the bullet.

lint.sh's no-net-growth check FAILS any net-positive SKILL.md diff that does not carry its own
stamp. Keep this edit net-zero or net-negative in line count; if it must grow, the growing

## 1. Per-line fork cost (perf)

The loop runs `printf '%s' "$fm_line" | grep -Eq '^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:'` once per non-blank,
non-indented frontmatter line, plus one `sed -n 1p` and one process-substitution `tail` per
skill.

- 59 skill dirs; 123 frontmatter lines scanned in total (NOT the ~300 the filing implies as
  line count; ~360 is the fork count).
- Isolated Check-3 loop: 0.66s / 0.90s / 0.98s across three runs.
- Full `bash lint.sh`: 12.9s / 17.8s / 16.1s across three runs (machine under concurrent
  multi-agent load).

Medium at best. The filing's "1.2-1.8s added to every lint.sh run" over-states the isolated cost
by ~2x and, more importantly, omits the denominator. It is worth fixing as a side-effect of the
correctness rewrite; it is NOT worth a standalone perf bead.

## 2. Residual key-shape gap (correctness)

The tightened test `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:` now rejects sentence-case prose ("Note: ...",
"TODO: ...") and any multi-word prose (the space breaks the key pattern). Still passing: a
SINGLE lowercase word followed by a colon — `todo: fix this`, `note: see below`.

PROVEN END-TO-END at refine, in a disposable worktree, keyed on the Check-3 FAIL message:
    baseline                                     Check3 FAIL lines: 0
    inject "todo: fix this"                      Check3 FAIL lines: 0   <-- the gap
    inject "Note: prose that carries a colon"    Check3 FAIL lines: 1
    inject "bare prose with no colon"            Check3 FAIL lines: 1
    inject "  indented: value" above any key     Check3 FAIL lines: 1
    clean again                                  Check3 FAIL lines: 0

## RECOMMENDATION (refine's decidable answer — this is a task, not a decision)

The filing framed item 2 as an open design choice. It is not, once the option set is priced:
- A real YAML parse was already REJECTED (pyyaml is not guaranteed in CI; a
  parser-if-available check is a non-deterministic gate).
- That leaves the known-key allowlist, and the allowlist is TINY. Census of every
  column-0 frontmatter key across all 59 SKILL.md at HEAD (executed at refine):
      58 name · 58 description · 3 disable-model-invocation · 2 tools · 2 accessory
  Five keys. Nothing else. (lint.sh's own comment claims `model`, `memory` and
  `permissionMode` are also in use — stale; none appear. Fix that comment in the same edit.)

So: replace the per-line `printf | grep` with a shell-native `case "${fm_line%%:*}" in ...`
membership test against an explicit `FM_ALLOWED_KEYS` list (name, description, accessory,
tools, disable-model-invocation — plus `model` and `permissionMode` as sanctioned headroom if
wanted). Escape hatch for a genuinely new key: add it to `FM_ALLOWED_KEYS` in the same commit
that introduces it, which is a reviewable one-line diff rather than a silent widening. Zero
forks, deterministic in CI, and `todo:` / `note:` fail closed.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (refine round 1, structure lens): splitting item 2 into a
`decision`-typed + `human-gate` bead. Round 2's structure lens independently adjudicated the
rejection SOUND — the YAML-parse alternative is not a live competitor (already rejected on
CI-determinism grounds), leaving exactly one candidate, so there is no choice-without-a-superior
-answer for the design-decision gate to fire on. Round 2's implementability lens built and
probed the proposed `case "${fm_line%%:*}"` shape against a no-colon line and against
prefix-key collisions: both fail closed correctly, so the recommendation is implementable as
written. Recorded so the override is visible rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The per-line grep fork is gone.
   `grep -c "grep -Eq '\^\[a-z\]\[A-Za-z0-9_-\]\*:'" lint.sh` returns 0.
   EXECUTED at refine: returns 1 (lint.sh line 191) — bites.

2. `todo: fix this` inserted as a frontmatter line now trips Check 3.
   Probe in a DISPOSABLE WORKTREE and assert on the Check-3 FAIL MESSAGE, never on exit code:
       git worktree add /tmp/<probe> HEAD --detach
       cp <probe>/skills/wiki/SKILL.md /tmp/<probe>-pristine.md
       perl -i -pe 'print "todo: fix this\n" if $. == 3 && !$done++' <probe>/skills/wiki/SKILL.md
       bash lint.sh 2>&1 | grep -c 'frontmatter block integrity'   # must be >= 1 after the fix
       cp /tmp/<probe>-pristine.md <probe>/skills/wiki/SKILL.md
   EXECUTED at refine on unfixed HEAD: returns 0 — bites.
   CRITICAL — WHY THE EXIT-CODE FORM IS WRONG: any probe that INSERTS a line into a SKILL.md
   makes that file net-positive, which trips lint.sh's separate no-net-growth check and turns
   `bash lint.sh` red for the WRONG reason. Executed at refine: the `todo:` probe exits 1 with
   "FAIL: no-net-growth: net-positive SKILL.md file(s) without their OWN net-growth-ok stamp"
   and ZERO Check-3 failures. An exit-code-only assertion would have reported this bead's
   defect as already fixed. The filing's four "verified RED" regression cases were all
   insertion probes and are therefore RED-for-the-wrong-reason as written — re-verify them in
   the message-keyed form.
   Also: restore the probe file with `cp` from a pristine copy — `git checkout --` and
   unscoped `git stash` are both dcg-blocked.

3. The regression set still trips Check 3 (message-keyed, same probe form):
   "Note: prose that carries a colon" · "bare prose with no colon" · an indented line above
   any mapping key · SKILL.md replaced by a symlink.
   EXECUTED at refine round 1 (first three): 1 Check-3 FAIL line each. The symlink case was
   confirmed at refine round 3, in a disposable worktree, against a fully built version of the
   recommended `FM_ALLOWED_KEYS` + `case` replacement: all six cases (unmodified 0 · `todo:` 1 ·
   `Note:` 1 · bare-prose 1 · orphan-indent 1 · symlink 1) match this table exactly, the full
   registry stays green (`bash lint.sh` exit 0, "0 failures"), and a prefix collision (`tool:`
   against the real key `tools:`) fails closed with no false positive. The recommendation is
   proven implementable, not merely plausible.

4. Unmodified registry stays green: `bash lint.sh` exit 0, "0 failures".
   EXECUTED at refine: exit 0.
   DO NOT assert the literal "372 checks" the filing carried. The check COUNT is
   environment-dependent — 372 in the live checkout, 370 in a disposable worktree, because
   Check 5's gitignored `_plans/` diagram path is absent there. The filing asserted 372 while
   mandating the probe run in a worktree, i.e. the AC could not pass in its own required
   environment. Assert exit code + "0 failures" only.

5. Perf: report full-run wall clock before/after. No isolated-loop threshold — lint.sh emits no
   per-check timing, so an isolated number is not reproducible from the CLI. Expect a small
   improvement (Check 3 is 5-8% of the run); do NOT gate the bead on a timing number.

## Test Scope

No unit-test suite; lint.sh IS the executable guard. All probes run in a DISPOSABLE WORKTREE
(`git worktree add /tmp/<probe> HEAD --detach`) — never sabotage the shared checkout.
- Anchor (verified present at refine, HEAD a5ab150): `grep -c "Frontmatter BLOCK INTEGRITY"
  lint.sh` = 1.
- Anchor (verified present at refine): `grep -c "grep -Eq '\^\[a-z\]\[A-Za-z0-9_-\]\*:'"
  lint.sh` = 1 — the fork being removed.
- Probe assertion form: `bash lint.sh 2>&1 | grep -c 'frontmatter block integrity'`. NEVER the
  bare exit code (see AC 2).
- Green baseline: `bash lint.sh` exit 0, "0 failures" — no literal check count.
- No browser/device/QA modality; this surface has no user-facing component.

## Delivers

- file: lint.sh — Check 3 frontmatter block-integrity loop rewritten to a fork-free,
  allowlist-based key test (`FM_ALLOWED_KEYS`), closing the single-lowercase-word prose gap
- doc: lint.sh — the Check 3 comment block, corrected (it currently names `model`, `memory`
  and `permissionMode` as in-use keys; none are)

## Consumes

- none

title: Child-spawn preamble now has 3 divergent embedding forms with no fidelity check
description:
discovered-from: ac-08k (verbatim preamble backfill, commit 5963b7c)

Architecture + performance lenses agreed at the same location. The child-spawn ENVIRONMENT
CONTRACT preamble (canon: `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md`
§ Child-spawn preamble) is embedded three different ways across the registry:

1. **CANON** — the blockquoted source in `delegation-contract.md`.
2. **STATIC VERBATIM COPY** — files that paste the block into their own prompt-construction
   text, each carrying an advisory `mirror:` HTML-comment marker naming the canon section.
3. **POINTER** — consumers that only reference `delegation-contract.md` by path.

Nothing enforces that form 2 stays byte-identical to form 1: `grep -c "mirror" lint.sh`
returns **0** (re-verified at refine time). The canon's own rule says a pointer is
explicitly INSUFFICIENT for this block, so form 3 is doctrinally non-compliant wherever it
is the only carrier.

## Corpus RE-MEASURED at refine time (2026-08-03) — the filing's numbers are superseded

ac-syct (this bead's `blocks` dependency) **closed today** and rolled the preamble to 12
more sites, moving every count in the original filing by up to an order of magnitude:

| Measure | Filed as | Actual at refine time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| files carrying a `mirror:` marker | 2 | **18** (carrying **23** markers — 3 files carry 2-4 each) |
| files carrying the preamble verbatim | 2 | **15** |
| files referencing `delegation-contract` by path | "~20" | **31** |

Commands (re-run these; do not trust the table if HEAD has moved):
`grep -rl "<!-- mirror:" skills/ --include="*.md" | wc -l` -> 18;
`grep -rl "ENVIRONMENT CONTRACT (non-negotiable)" skills/ | wc -l` -> 15;
`grep -rl "delegation-contract" skills/ --include="*.md" | wc -l` -> 31.

## Question (b) is ANSWERED — refine closes it, no human gate needed

(b) asked: should the ~20 pointer-only consumers be backfilled, or is the "pointer
insufficient" rule scoped only to files that CONSTRUCT child prompts?

ac-syct answered it **empirically by what it did**: it backfilled exactly the
prompt-constructing files and left the rest as pointers. Every file that constructs a child
prompt now carries the block (15/15). The rule's real scope is therefore
**files that construct child prompts**, and the remaining pointer-only consumers are
correct as-is. The residual work is to write that scope sentence into the canon so the next
reader does not re-derive it. Mechanical.

## Marker taxonomy the check MUST respect (refine round 2 — enumerated, not assumed)

The 23 markers are NOT one homogeneous corpus. A check written to the naive spec ("diff the
block that follows each marker against its cited section") fails its own GREEN probe on
first run. Three distinctions, each verified by enumerating all 23:

1. **Two fidelity contracts.**
   - **VERBATIM class — 14 markers**, all citing
     `ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md § Child-spawn preamble`. Canon mandates
     "paste ... VERBATIM"; ac-syct verified these byte-identical. These are the check's scope.
   - **PARAPHRASE class — 8 markers**, citing `review-consensus.md` (5),
     `verification-gate.md` (2), `bead-conventions.md` (1). These are deliberate prose
     restatements, not copies — `structure-standard.md` documents the marker as being for a
     skill that must "restate a block **in prose**." Byte-diffing them fails on unmodified
     HEAD. **Exclude them; do not "fix" them into copies.**
   - Split command: `grep -rc "mirror: ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md" skills/ --include="*.md"`
     summed -> 14; the complement is 9 (8 paraphrase + 1 below).
2. **One marker is the SYNTAX DOCUMENTATION, not a mirror.**
   `skills/skill-builder/references/structure-standard.md` contains the literal example
   `<!-- mirror: <owner>/references/x.md — edit there first -->` inside backticks. A parser
   that treats it as a real marker will try to open a file named `<owner>/references/x.md`.
   It must be excluded (it is inside a code span, and its path is a placeholder).
3. **Position and section-anchor syntax both vary.**
   - All 14 verbatim-class markers are PREFIX (marker, then the block). Position in the
     **paraphrase class is NOT uniform** and must not be assumed: of its 8 markers, 5 sit
     immediately after the prose they restate (`ac-merge/SKILL.md` x2,
     `ac-review/SKILL.md` x2, `ac-hygiene/SKILL.md:319`) and 3 are preceded by a blank line
     (`ac-hygiene/SKILL.md` x3), making their association ambiguous from position alone.
     Do NOT encode a "4 suffix sites" or "8 suffix sites" rule — refine drafted both counts
     and neither survived inspection. The safe statement: **"the block that follows the
     marker" is only reliable for the verbatim class**, which is why the check is scoped
     there. Any later generalization to the paraphrase class must first define how a marker
     binds to its block, because the corpus does not answer it consistently.
   - The `§` anchor appears both with and without a following space (`§ Child-spawn
     preamble` vs `§Design-decision gate`), and **2 markers carry no `§` section at all**
     (`ac-merge/SKILL.md` citing `bead-conventions.md`, plus the doc example). A parser
     requiring `§ ` with a space silently skips real markers.

## Question (a) is DECIDED — build the mirror-lint

(a) asked whether a generic check diffing each `<!-- mirror: <path> § <section> -->` block
against its cited canon section is worth building. Refine decides **yes**, as an
AUTO_IMPLEMENT, not a human gate: the canon *mandates* duplication (a pointer is declared
insufficient), 18 marker sites now exist, and **nothing whatsoever enforces fidelity**. A
mandated duplicate with no drift check is a guaranteed future divergence — the check is the
only thing that makes the mandate safe. That is question (c)'s cost argument resolving in
favour of building it, so (c) is not a separate deliverable: it is the rationale, recorded
here.

Retyped `investigation` -> `task` at refine: all three questions now have answers, so what
remains is execution, not inquiry.

## Delivers

- `file: lint.sh` — a mirror-fidelity check over the **verbatim class only** (see the
  marker taxonomy below): for each of the 14 `<!-- mirror: ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md
  § Child-spawn preamble -->` markers, compare the preamble block in that file against the
  canon section byte-for-byte; fail naming the drifted file. Paraphrase-class markers are
  SKIPPED by name, and the check must say so in its output rather than silently ignoring
  them.
- `doc: skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble — an
  explicit scope sentence stating the "pointer is insufficient" rule binds **files that
  construct child prompts**, and that pointer-only reference is correct elsewhere.

## Consumes

- none blocking. ac-syct is CLOSED (its `blocks` edge is satisfied); it is retained as the
  provenance of the re-measured corpus.
- **File-set adjacency (not a dependency):** ac-kfjc also ships a check over the same
  preamble corpus (anchor presence in prompt bodies). Different property — anchor presence
  vs block fidelity — so they do not conflict, but if both land in `lint.sh` keep them as
  two independently-named checks and re-run the full suite after the second one lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `lint.sh` gains a mirror-fidelity check covering the 14 verbatim-class markers,
   byte-comparing each file's preamble block against
   `ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble.
2. The check ACCOUNTS for all 23 markers — 14 checked, 8 paraphrase-class named as skipped,
   1 syntax-documentation example excluded. It never silently drops a marker it cannot parse.
3. It parses `§` with and without a following space, and does not crash on the 2 markers
   carrying no `§` section.
4. RED probe passes: a mutated verbatim-class block makes the check FAIL and name the file.
   Anti-false-green probe passes: a mutated paraphrase-class block leaves it GREEN.
5. `skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` § Child-spawn preamble gains the
   scope sentence naming BOTH halves of the boundary (binds prompt-constructing files;
   pointer-only reference correct elsewhere).
6. `./lint.sh` exits 0 with 0 failures on an unmodified tree.

Commands and RED baselines are in `## Test Scope`.

## Test Scope

Mechanically testable in a disposable worktree. Baselines RE-MEASURED at refine time.

- `grep -c "mirror" lint.sh` — currently **0** (RED baseline re-verified at refine time).
  Must be >=1 after the check lands.
- **Corpus enumeration.** Count FILES with `-rl`, markers with `-rc`; the two differ and the
  distinction matters (the check iterates markers, not files):
  `grep -rl "<!-- mirror:" skills/ --include="*.md" | wc -l` -> **18 files**;
  `grep -rc "<!-- mirror:" skills/ --include="*.md" | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s}'` ->
  **23 markers**. Do NOT use `grep -rn ... | wc -l` for the file count — it returns 23, and
  an earlier draft of this bead did exactly that. Of the 23: **14 verbatim-class (the
  check's scope)**, 8 paraphrase-class (skipped by name), 1 syntax-documentation (excluded).
  The check must ACCOUNT for all 23 — visiting 14, naming 9 as skipped — because a check
  that silently drops markers it cannot parse is a false green.
- **RED probe (bite-proof — required, this is the bead's sole evidence):** in a disposable
  `git worktree add`, mutate one word inside the mirrored preamble block in a copy of
  `skills/ac-beadify/references/validators.md` (a verbatim-class site) -> the new check must
  FAIL and must name that file. A check that cannot be shown RED does not enforce anything.
- **Anti-false-green probe:** mutate one word inside a PARAPHRASE-class block (e.g. the
  `review-consensus.md §Design-decision gate` mirror in `skills/ac-review/SKILL.md`) -> the
  check must stay GREEN and report that marker as skipped. If it goes RED, the scope
  boundary was not implemented and the GREEN probe below will fail on unmodified HEAD.
- **GREEN probe:** unmodified registry -> `./lint.sh` exit 0, **0 failures**. Re-measured at
  refine time: 372 checks, 0 failures. Assert 0-failures + exit 0, never the drifting count.
- **Scope-sentence verification:** `grep -c "construct" skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md`
  returns **1** at refine time — that hit is pre-existing and is NOT the scope sentence, so
  a bare word-count is not a usable AC here. Refine drafted TWO such greps and executed
  both: `construct` -> 1 and `pointer-only` -> 2, i.e. both would have been GREEN before any
  work was done. Use instead these phrases, each EXECUTED at refine time and confirmed
  **0** (genuinely RED):
  `grep -c "construct child prompts" skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` -> 0
  and `grep -c "pointer-only reference is correct" skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md` -> 0.
  The new scope sentence must name BOTH halves of the boundary — that the rule binds
  prompt-CONSTRUCTING files, and that pointer-only reference is correct elsewhere — so both
  greps must return >=1 afterwards. Also read the § Child-spawn preamble section to confirm
  the sentence is placed there and not merely appended somewhere in the file.
- No QA modality (lint + doc-canon, no user-facing surface).
close_reason: Implemented and tested. lint.sh Check 16 byte-compares all 14 verbatim-class mirrors against canon, names the 8 paraphrase-class as skipped and excludes the 1 syntax example (23/23 accounted). RED probe: mutated verbatim block FAILs naming the file. Anti-false-green: mutated paraphrase block stays GREEN. Duplication-cost record in the check header. Delivered: lint.sh, skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md. Commit d61f0e1

derived". The bead's own text already contains the answer and refine adopts it: KEEP the
hand-set constant (a fully derived ceiling can never catch a batch that bloats every skill at
once, which is why the constant exists) and ADD a one-way self-check that recomputes the
derived value at run time and FAILS when the constant EXCEEDS it. The constant becomes a cache
of a derived value that may only be tighter, never looser. No design call remains.

    constant exceeds the derived value; it must NEVER be read as licence to raise the constant
    to meet a grown derived value. State that explicitly in the code comment, because the
    check cannot enforce it: monotonicity across time needs the committed constant as its own

title: Proposal: enforce progress.md completeness via gate (ac-implement/ac-batch-close)
description:
## Decision memo
**Target:** skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md (progress.md append + 'COMPLETED: n/N' requirement, ~L597-611) and/or an enforcement gate (beads-closed-gate.sh Phase 0, or ac-batch-close Phase 0).

**Evidence (this session, RUN 20260716-111224-31570):** progress.md completeness was followed unevenly across the 7 waves — 4/7 (bugs, mengto-tt91, ycr, standards) carried full per-bead results + COMPLETED n/N; 3/7 (ap2, r3, d29) contained ONLY a 3-line claim header (claim/title/beads), with no correlation to wave size or type (r3 was a 6-bead wave). This broke the explicit design contract at ac-loop/SKILL.md ('the retrospective reads every progress.md'), forcing the Phase 2 retrospective to reconstruct 3 waves' outcomes from git log instead of the intended artifact-of-record.

**Proposed change:** enforce progress.md completeness with a mechanical gate rather than prose alone — e.g. at bead-close/batch-close, assert the wave's progress.md contains a per-bead result line + a COMPLETED n/N tally, failing the close if absent. (Mechanical implementation rides beads-closed-gate.test.sh, but the policy — should a missing/thin progress.md BLOCK a close? — is the human call, since an over-strict gate could stall legitimate investigation-only waves whose 'result' is a one-line verdict.)

**Recommendation:** apply-modified — favour a WARN-and-record gate over a hard block for investigation/singleton waves (ap2/d29 were legitimate one-line-verdict investigations; only r3's thin multi-bead header is a genuine miss). Source: Phase 2 retrospective, RUN 20260716-111224-31570.

comments.author: craigvanheerden
comments.text:
DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-17): **apply-modified — conditional WARN/FAIL gate.**

Policy: at the BEADS-CLOSED-GATE / ac-batch-close checkpoint, parse the wave's progress.md:
- multi-bead wave (N>1): HARD-FAIL the close if progress.md lacks a per-bead result line for each bead + the COMPLETED n/N tally.
- single-bead / investigation-only wave (N==1): WARN-and-record, never block — a one-line verdict is a legitimate complete result there.

This blocks the observed failure mode (r3: a 6-bead wave shipping a 3-line claim header, forcing the retrospective to reconstruct from git log) without stalling benign investigation waves (ap2/d29 were fine). Keep it proportionate: a few lines in the existing gate script, not a new subsystem.

Implementation filed as ac-514 (rides skills/_shared/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh + its test file).

title: ac-review auto-fix commit rides inside the batch range but outside the reviewed range
description:
## Problem

When ac-review auto-fixes findings, its Phase 6 commit (the fixes + the staged report) lands
on main AFTER the range the report claims to cover. ac-batch-close then closes a batch whose
range INCLUDES that commit, while the review artifact attests only to `base..pre-fix-head`.
The review's own edits are therefore inside a range marked reviewed, but were never reviewed
by anything.

## Observed

observed: 2026-08-03 · RUN_ID 20260803-113231-34132 (batches 3+4 combined close)
- report Range: 44717df..e11a0e3
- batch range closed: 44717df..09725d5 (09725d5 = 'review: batches 3+4 — 6 issues fixed, 2 filed as beads')
- 09725d5 touches 9 skill files (re-counted at HEAD 8fc9e36 via
  `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r 09725d5` — the earlier "8" was wrong),
  including two conductor-core SKILL.md files (ac-batch-close, ac-land).

## Why the guards did not catch it

Act 3's content-grep (SKILL.md:597) selects the pending report by its Range BASE only
(`Range:.*${ANCHOR:0:8}[0-9a-f]*\.\.`). A base match passes regardless of how far HEAD has
moved past the report's head. The ancestry check that WOULD catch it exists only on the
`CONDUCTOR_PENDING_REPORT` path (SKILL.md:580-595, ac-nsb), and even there only requires the
report head to be a DESCENDANT-or-equal of the batch head — i.e. wider-is-fine,
never narrower-is-caught. Both confirmed by reading HEAD 8fc9e36.

## Decision (refine, 2026-08-03) — direction 1

Candidate direction 1 is adopted; 2 and 3 are recorded below as rejected. Rationale:
- **Direction 2 (ac-review re-stamps its Range head to its own fix commit)** requires the fix
  commit's SHA before it exists — `ac-review/SKILL.md` Phase 6 commits the fixes and the
  report in the SAME commit, so it needs a commit-then-amend dance, and it moves the fix into
  a DIFFERENT skill file. Higher blast radius, no better coverage.
- **Direction 3 (accept the seam as doctrine)** leaves `unknown` collapsing to `ok` on the
  non-conductor path, which is the exact failure this bead names.
- **Direction 1** extends the ancestry pattern that already exists at SKILL.md:580-595 to the
  common path, stays inside `ac-batch-close/SKILL.md`, and is replayable against real history.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **(mechanical)** Act 3's non-conductor selector gains a Range-HEAD ancestry assert:
  after the Range-BASE match at SKILL.md:597, the report's Range HEAD (`RHEAD`) is checked
  against `$BATCH_HEAD`. `grep -n 'RHEAD' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` shows at least one
  hit in the NON-conductor branch (i.e. after the `else` at SKILL.md:596), not only inside
  the `CONDUCTOR_PENDING_REPORT` branch. Bite-proof — executed at HEAD 8fc9e36, `RHEAD`
  appears ONLY at lines 584/587 (both inside the conductor branch), so the check fails today.
- **Behaviour, RHEAD == BATCH_HEAD:** proceed silently (no seam line). This is the ordinary
  case and must not regress.
- **Behaviour, RHEAD a STRICT ancestor of BATCH_HEAD (the defect):** every commit in
  `(RHEAD, BATCH_HEAD]` must have a subject matching `^review:`. If so, Act 3 PROCEEDS and
  the batch report gains an explicit `Review seam:` line naming each gap SHA + subject as
  covered-but-unreviewed. If ANY gap commit is not `review:`-prefixed, Act 3 STOPS with the
  same FATAL shape as the unidentifiable-artifact case — unknown must never collapse to ok.
- **Behaviour, RHEAD NOT an ancestor of BATCH_HEAD** (report claims a head off this line of
  history): FATAL, same as above.
- **(mechanical)** The seam line's exact wording is anchored:
  `grep -c 'Review seam:' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns `>= 1`.
  Bite-proof — executed at HEAD 8fc9e36 during refine, returns `0`.
- **(mechanical) Fence the new logic so it is mechanically extractable.** Bracket the new
  selector+assert logic (and ONLY that logic — no `git mv` / `git commit` / `git push`, so
  the harness has no side effects) with literal marker comments:
      # BEGIN Act3-rhead-assert
      # END Act3-rhead-assert
  Check: `grep -c 'Act3-rhead-assert' skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md` returns `2`.
  Bite-proof — returns `0` at HEAD 8fc9e36. Without these markers the replay ACs below are
  not mechanically runnable: the non-conductor branch spans SKILL.md:596-626 and naively
  sourcing that span would fire real git mv/commit/push against a fixture.
- **(executed, seam-proof) Three-case replay — drive the AMENDED block, not raw git.**
  Hand-running `merge-base`/`rev-list`/`log|grep` proves the HISTORY, not the
  implementation: a reviewer could confirm every number while the new check never ran.
  Extract and drive the fenced harness:
      cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
      sed -n '/# BEGIN Act3-rhead-assert/,/# END Act3-rhead-assert/p' \
        skills/ac-batch-close/SKILL.md | tee /tmp/act3-rhead-assert.sh
      bash -c 'RHEAD=09725d5 BATCH_HEAD=09725d5; . /tmp/act3-rhead-assert.sh'; echo "exit=$?"
      bash -c 'RHEAD=e11a0e3 BATCH_HEAD=09725d5; . /tmp/act3-rhead-assert.sh'; echo "exit=$?"
      bash -c 'RHEAD=1b1767b BATCH_HEAD=e11a0e3; . /tmp/act3-rhead-assert.sh'; echo "exit=$?"
  Required, and all three MUST differ (identical output across cases means the check is not
  biting — fix it before closing):
  - **Case A, RHEAD == BATCH_HEAD (the ORDINARY path, most common):** exit 0, and NO
    `Review seam:` line. This is the regression case — an implementation that always takes
    the strict-ancestor branch would emit a spurious seam on every normal batch close and
    would still satisfy cases B and C.
  - **Case B, strict ancestor, whole gap `review:`-authored:** exit 0 AND the output
    contains `Review seam:` naming `09725d5 review: batches 3+4 …`. PROCEED-with-seam,
    NOT reject.
  - **Case C, strict ancestor, a non-`review:` commit in the gap** (`e11a0e3` subject is
    `docs(jef-flywheel): refresh 10_dcg false-positives for dcg 0.6.7`): NON-ZERO exit,
    FATAL on stderr, and NO `Review seam:` line.
  Paste all three outputs + exit codes in the close reason. A reference implementation of
  the fenced harness was written and EXECUTED during refine at HEAD 8fc9e36 against a /tmp
  fixture and produced exactly: A -> exit 0, silent; B -> exit 0 +
  `Review seam: 09725d5 review: batches 3+4 — 6 issues fixed, 2 filed as beads`;
  C -> exit 1 + `FATAL: non-review commits inside the closed-but-unreviewed gap`.
  Underlying history facts (oracle only, NOT the AC — all executed during refine):
      git merge-base --is-ancestor e11a0e3 09725d5                 -> true
      git rev-list --count e11a0e3..09725d5                        -> 1
      git log --format='%s' e11a0e3..09725d5 | grep -c '^review:'   -> 1
      git rev-list --count 09725d5..09725d5                        -> 0
      git log --format='%s' 1b1767b..e11a0e3 | grep -c '^review:'   -> 0
- **(lint gate — read BEFORE editing)** `lint.sh` Check 14 (`no-net-growth`, HARD,
  per-file) fails any net-positive line delta in a `skills/**/SKILL.md` diff vs merge-base
  unless THAT FILE'S OWN diff adds a line carrying the literal token `net-growth-ok:`
  (lint.sh:684 greps `^\+[^+].*net-growth-ok:`). The stamps already present do NOT count — the
  stamp must be an ADDED line in your diff. This bead adds an assert block, so it will grow
  the file. Add, in the same diff:
      # net-growth-ok: ac-ya71.1 — the narrower-range seam check belongs at the selector site
  **Comment FORM is by location, and getting it wrong breaks the build or your own tests:**

title: Two-tier Agent Mail identity model — doctrine + wiring (ratified 2026-07-14)
description:
DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-14, this session): adopt the TWO-TIER identity model, replacing agent-identity.md's unwired mint-or-inherit doctrine. Rationale recorded so this isn't relitigated:
- Identity is the lock grain; the grain must match the WRITER-CONCURRENCY boundary. At PARALLEL_WIDTH>1 the parallel ac-implement children are independent concurrent writers in one shared checkout — inheriting one loop identity would put multiple writers under one name (forbidden by agent-identity.md's own corollary). Below the boundary, workers never commit/reserve, so per-worker identity is pure ceremony. The inherit model was written for a serial world; the width dial obsoleted it.
- TIER 1 (unique minted identity — mint via macro_start_session, reserve at work grain, release, self-deregister at exit): any session that CLAIMS BEADS or EDITS PRODUCT CODE — loop conductor (claims only), each ac-implement child, ac-review (auto-fix engineer edits code), ac-batch-close (fix-forward). Plan-family skills already conform.
- TIER 2 (FoggyCreek as EXPLICIT shared chore identity, not accidental fallback): serial low-contention writers — scheduled jobs (tidy/align/dream), ac-land sweep/report commits. HARD RULE = tier boundary AND safety guard: FoggyCreek may commit chore files but may NEVER claim beads or reserve files.
- Deregistration = 3 layers: (1) minter self-deregisters at own exit; (2) ac-land sweeps the identity roster handed by the loop (VERIFIED 2026-07-14 against live schemas: deregister_agent/retire_agent take registration_token as OPTIONAL — sweep by name works; force_release_file_reservation exists for stale holds); (3) next-run Phase-0 stale sweep + reservation TTL floor.
- Claim-visibility chain (CLAIM_ASSIGNEE threading + beads-closed-gate union + fail-closed) is solid and UNCHANGED by this epic.
Audit that produced this: 5 gaps — exit-land can't release/deregister identities never handed to it; stages never deregister; agent-identity.md contradicts live per-stage model; engineer wip-commit hatch collides with pre-commit guard; FoggyCreek fallback silently misattributes claims. Children implement; doctrine-rewrite child blocks the rest.

title: DECISION: cross-session identity deregistration mechanism — retire/deregister reject name-only calls at runtime (ac-ycr.5 premise falsified)
description:
## Context
ac-ycr.5 (deregistration layers 2+3) and agent-identity.md's Deregistration table rest on the epic-ratified premise ("verified against live schemas 2026-07-14"): retire_agent/deregister_agent take registration_token as OPTIONAL, so ac-land can sweep the handed roster BY NAME without token custody.

Runtime re-verification (ac-bead-refine round 2, 2026-07-16) contradicts this. The token IS optional in the SCHEMA (anyOf string/null, default null) — so the schema-level check was correct — but the tool REJECTS name-only calls at RUNTIME: "requires registration_token unless this MCP session has already authenticated as that agent." ac-land, and next-run ac-loop Phase 0, are freshly spawned sessions that never registered the roster's identities, so they hold no tokens for them. Cross-session retire/deregister BY NAME therefore fails. agent-identity.md's own "Call-scoped facts #1" already states tokens live with the minting session and do not transfer — consistent with the runtime rejection, inconsistent with the table's "sweep by name works" note.

Impact is narrow: ONLY cross-session IDENTITY deregistration (layer-2 identity-retire, layer-3 identity-retire). Sound and unaffected: layer-1 self-deregister (minting session holds its own token); force_release_file_reservation (schema + description confirm it releases ANOTHER agent's reservation by name via abandonment heuristics); reservation TTL floor (7200s). Note: there is NO TTL for identities today — only reservations expire.

## Options
- A. Roster carries tokens: children + loop report their registration_tokens (not just names) in summaries; ac-land retires by token. Cost: tokens transit summaries/prompts; agent-identity.md says tokens shouldn't transfer; mild secret-handling concern in a public-repo skill.
- B (recommended). Drop cross-session identity dereg; rely on layer-1 self-deregister for the happy path. ac-land layer-2 shrinks to force_release_file_reservation only (identities not retired cross-session). Accept that sessions which CRASH before self-deregister leave a retired-eligible identity with no automatic reaper (no identity TTL exists). Pair with option D as an upstream ask.
- C. ac-land re-registers (authenticates as) each roster identity, then deregisters it. Cost: hacky; resurrect-then-kill semantics unverified.
- D. Request an mcp-agent-mail capability: a project-scoped admin sweep that retires stale agents by name (a real cross-session teardown primitive). Cost: upstream dependency.

## Recommendation
B now (self-deregister is the honest primitive given the auth model; reservations still swept by force_release_file_reservation), and file D as an upstream ask so identity cleanup eventually gets a proper primitive. Once decided, reframe ac-ycr.5: layer-2 = force_release_file_reservation sweep only; identity cleanup = layer-1 self + (future) D. Also fold the ac-ycr.5 round-2 sub-finding here: ac-review/ac-batch-close delegation prompts never request their minted identity back, so those 2 of 5 Tier-1 identities never reach the roster anyway — under option B they self-deregister (layer 1), so roster omission is harmless; under A/C the delegation prompts would need to return the identity+token.

## Delivers
- decision: the chosen cross-session identity-cleanup mechanism recorded here, after which ac-ycr.5 is reframed to match and unblocked.
- doc: skills/_shared/agent-identity.md — the stale "verified against live schemas ... sweep by name works" paragraph (lines ~89-91) and Layer-2/3 Wiring cells corrected to the decided mechanism (the false premise this bead quotes and falsifies).
close_reason: Decided: option B+D (Craig 2026-07-17). Doc fixed in agent-identity.md; ycr.5 reframed; upstream ask ac-rjh filed.

DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-17): **Option B + D.**

- B: drop cross-session identity deregistration. Identity cleanup = layer-1 self-deregister only; ac-land layer 2 and ac-loop Phase-0 layer 3 shrink to reservation sweeps (force_release_file_reservation), which work cross-session by name.
- D: upstream ask filed as ac-rjh — request a project-scoped admin sweep primitive from mcp-agent-mail.

Premise re-verified live this session before ratifying: retire_agent name-only against a stale identity (AmberBrook) was rejected at runtime — "requires registration_token ... unless this MCP session has already authenticated as that agent" — exactly as this bead states. Schema-optional but runtime-required-or-authenticated confirmed.

Rationale: option A (tokens transit summaries) violates the token-custody doctrine (agent-identity.md call-scoped fact #1) and puts secrets in prompts in a public-repo skill; option C (re-register to impersonate, then kill) is unverified and hacky. title: dcg custom-pack schema unknown — blocks the unscoped-stash guard; and a bad pack loads SILENTLY as a no-op
description:
Blocks the ac-7rf (P0) fix. The design is settled and the proof harness is built and
committed (agent-compounds e29da3d, tools/dcg/). The ONLY missing piece is dcg's
custom-pack YAML schema.

THE DESIGN (agreed with Craig, do not re-litigate)
Add ONE additive rule via a dcg custom pack: block the UNSCOPED stash save, allow
everything else. Do NOT block `git stash` wholesale — dcg deliberately treats the stash
as the safe harbour and already guards it with core.git:stash-drop and
core.git:stash-clear. Blocking it outright would fight a coherent design and leave no
sanctioned place to park work.
  BLOCK: git stash · git stash -u · git stash push · git stash push -u · git stash save
  ALLOW: git stash push -- <paths> · git stash push -u -- <paths> · list · show · pop · apply

WHY THIS EXACT LINE
Both incidents on 2026-07-31 were the unscoped form: one swept another agent's untracked
files into a global stack, one left work poppable by a stranger and one checkout from
unrecoverable. `stash push -- <paths>` touches only what the caller names.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN (re-run tools/dcg/stash-pack-probe.sh)
  baseline, no pack:            12 cases · 7 ok · 5 FAIL  <- the gap, precisely
  built-in strict_git enabled:  12 cases · 7 ok · 5 FAIL  <- no built-in path exists
  DCG_CONFIG is honoured:       proven via [policy] default_mode = "warn"
                                (BLOCKED -> WARNING), tools/dcg/dcg-config-honoured-probe.sh

WHAT IS BLOCKING
The custom-pack YAML schema. Five candidate shapes were tried (name+patterns,
pack+match, name+match+action, id+pattern, top-level list) against
[packs] custom_paths = ["<dir>/*.yaml"]. None registered in `dcg packs`.

*** AND THIS IS THE DANGEROUS PART ***
dcg gave NO error for any of them. An unloadable custom pack is silently ignored. So a
pack shipped with a typo reports nothing and protects nothing, while everyone believes
the guard is live. That is precisely the defect class this whole workstream exists to
remove (cf. bd-axeyx: consensus silently fell back to a smaller panel and dropped a
Critical). It is why this guard was NOT shipped unverified.

TO UNBLOCK — a lookup, not a guess
The dcg binary references `docs/custom-packs.md` ("See docs/custom-packs.md for pack
authoring guide"). Find that doc, or any working example custom pack, and the schema is
settled in minutes. dcg 0.6.7, installed at ~/.local/bin/dcg.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. tools/dcg/stash-pack-probe.sh reports 12 cases · 12 ok · 0 FAIL with the pack enabled.
   Both halves are load-bearing: 5 must flip to BLOCK, and the 7 ALLOW cases must STAY
   allowed. Over-blocking `git stash pop` or `list` would be worse than today.
2. The pack is proven to LOAD, not merely present — assert it appears in `dcg packs`
   output, since a silent no-op is indistinguishable from success.
3. Paste the real probe output in the close reason. A green claim without the
   denominator is not evidence.

INTERIM CONTROLS (already in place, keep until this lands)
- Primary: commit the instant a bead's ACs verify. Both incidents involved UNCOMMITTED
  work; under trunk-direct committing is free. This removes most of the need to stash.
- The delegation-prompt ban on git stash. Note it demonstrably fails at depth 2 — it
  reached conductors but not the agents THEY spawned, which is how both incidents
  happened. Do not treat it as sufficient.
close_reason: Schema found in the upstream repo (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard, docs/custom-packs.md): schema_version/id/name/version + destructive_patterns[] and safe_patterns[] with name/pattern/severity/description. safe_patterns made the design cleaner than planned — one broad destructive rule plus two explicit exemptions, no negative lookahead. Pack shipped and LIVE at ~/.config/dcg/packs/, committed to agent-compounds tools/dcg/. Proof on dcg's default config discovery (real hook path): before 12 cases/7 ok/5 FAIL, after 12/12/0. Two traps recorded: dcg silently ignores an unloadable pack (validate passing is not proof it is live), and a pack id that once failed stays poisoned — identical content under a fresh id loaded instantly.

title: dream check 14: self-arming skill-uptake decay cadence — emit demotion candidates from skill_reads
description:
Roadmap item 6: wire the skill-uptake demotion cadence — a scheduled step that reads
`skill_reads` telemetry and auto-files demotion-candidate beads, so registry shrink becomes
perpetual instead of episodic. Application stays human-gated.

discovered-from: unknown (roadmap item 6, banked by commit be40028 "roadmap items 5+6 banked
before session close" — no single originating bead)

## Premise state at HEAD (verified 2026-08-03)

- **Telemetry EXISTS but is FAR too sparse to act on.** `~/.claude/logs/activity.db` holds
  table `skill_reads(id, timestamp, session_id, skill, path)` with an index on `skill`.
  At 2026-08-03 05:30 it contained **7 rows across 3 distinct skills** (CORE 4,
  daily-brief 2, ac-pipeline 1), spanning 2026-08-02 06:39 -> 2026-08-03 05:30, against a
  **58-skill** registry (`ls skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l` = 58; `skills/_tools/` is a
  directory with no SKILL.md and is not a skill). One captured path is `/x/.claude/skills/ac-pipeline/references/run-id.md`
  — a non-absolute root, so path normalisation is not yet trustworthy either.
  A naive "N-week zero-read streak" rule run today would file demotion beads against
  roughly 55 of 58 skills. That is data sparsity, not evidence of disuse. **The self-arming
  gate below is the load-bearing part of this bead, not a nicety.**
- **The template already exists and must be mirrored, not reinvented.** dream check 12
  (`skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md:82-98`) is this exact shape for memory facts:
  script-driven (`~/Repos/infrastructure/dream-cycle/decay_lint.py`, present at HEAD),
  SELF-ARMING (does nothing until >=28 days of data exist AND the `memory_reads` table is
  live — docstring lines 15-28; `WINDOW_DAYS=28`, `MIN_ACTIVE_DAYS=5`), coverage-guarded,
  EMIT-ONLY, and always human-gated. Check 13 (provenance leak) occupies the next slot at
  `lint-checks.md:100-110` (the `## Ouroboros guard` heading follows at line 112), so this
  becomes **check 14**.
- Host cadence: dream's `[T2 weekly]` tier is where checks 12 and 13 live, and is the right
  home (ac-tidy's NIGHTLY tier at `skills/ac-tidy/SKILL.md:13,287` is T0/T3 daily work).
- `WORKER:` stamp grammar is real and greppable: `skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md:553`,
  `skills/beads-standards/SKILL.md:230-233`
  (`WORKER: model=<id> session=<name> skill@version=<SHA> duration=<wall-clock>`),
  queried via `grep 'WORKER:' .beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Work

**Two artifacts in TWO REPOS — both are required; the check text alone is not the bead.**
Check 12 is `[script-driven]` because it ships a real script; so is this. Deliver:

- **(a) the script** `infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py` — a sibling of
  `infrastructure/dream-cycle/decay_lint.py`, whose structure it should follow (arming
  logic, window constants, emit-only proposal output). **This file lives in the `~/Repos`
  root repo, NOT in agent-compounds** — `git -C ~/Repos/infrastructure rev-parse
  --show-toplevel` returns `/Users/craigvanheerden/Repos`. Per the repo-boundary rule,
  commit it separately; never in the same operation as the agent-compounds change.
- **(b) the check text** — numbered check 14 in `skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md`
  (agent-compounds), pointing at (a) exactly as check 12 points at `decay_lint.py`.

The script is what the two runnable ACs below execute; without it they are unsatisfiable.

Check 14 — skill-uptake decay `[T2 weekly, script-driven, data-gated]`, modelled directly
on check 12:

1. Reads `skill_reads` from `~/.claude/logs/activity.db`, aggregated **per skill**. Skill
   granularity ONLY — the `path` column is recorded but is not the unit of judgement in
   this bead (see Approach for why reference-file granularity is deferred, not forgotten).
2. **SELF-ARMS** — emits nothing until ALL hold: (a) >= 28 days elapsed since the earliest
   `skill_reads.timestamp`; (b) the `skill_reads` table is present and non-empty;
   (c) a coverage guard — at least 50% of registry skills (>= 29 of 58) have recorded at
   least one read within the window, so a zero for a given skill means "not read" rather
   than "not instrumented". Until armed, the check reports its own disarmed state and
   files nothing.
3. Once armed: a **skill** with **zero reads across the trailing 28-day window** is a
   demotion candidate. Emits ONE `unrefined`, `human-gate` demotion-candidate bead per
   candidate skill, evidence = the read count, the window bounds, and the coverage
   denominator that armed the run.
4. **EMIT-ONLY and human-gated** — never moves, demotes, or deletes anything itself.
5. Separately: a change of `model=` in the `WORKER:` stamps auto-files a re-ablation
   review bead (the prior uptake baseline no longer holds across a model generation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md` contains a numbered **check 14** for
      skill-uptake decay, tagged `[T2 weekly, script-driven, data-gated]`.
      Check: `grep -n '^14\.' skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md`.
- [ ] The check text states an explicit self-arming predicate with all three conditions and
      the numeric thresholds (28 days; table present + non-empty; >= 50% skill coverage, i.e. >= 29 of 58 at HEAD —
      compute the denominator at run time from `skills/*/SKILL.md`, never hard-code it).
      Check: read the section; every threshold is a number, not "N".
- [ ] **Run against the LIVE database, the check files ZERO beads** (it is disarmed at HEAD:
      7 rows / 3 skills / ~1 day of data). This is the bite-proof — an implementation that
      files anything today is wrong. Check: execute the check's own procedure/script against
      `~/.claude/logs/activity.db`: run
      `python3 ~/Repos/infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py` and confirm it
      reports "disarmed" and emits zero proposals.
- [ ] A RED proof that the check CAN fire: point it at a synthetic fixture DB satisfying all
      three arming conditions with one zero-read skill, and confirm exactly one
      demotion-candidate proposal is emitted. Check: build the fixture DB under `/tmp/`, run
      `python3 ~/Repos/infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py --db <fixture>`, and
      assert exactly one proposal. (Both legs required — disarmed-at-HEAD alone does not
      prove the check works; it is indistinguishable from a check that does nothing.)
- [ ] Emissions are gated: every proposal carries `human-gate` and `unrefined`, and nothing
      is auto-applied. Check: inspect the emit path; confirm the labels in the spec text.
- [ ] The `WORKER:` model-generation trigger is specified with its greppable source.
      Check: `grep -n 'WORKER:' skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md` returns the new text.
- [ ] `infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py` exists and runs. Check:
      `python3 ~/Repos/infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py --help` exits 0.
- [ ] The check-14 text names that script path, as check 12 names `decay_lint.py`.
      Check: `grep -n 'skill_uptake_lint' skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md`.
- [ ] The agent-compounds change and the infrastructure change are SEPARATE commits (repo
      boundary). Check: `git log --oneline -3` in each repo.
- [ ] `./lint.sh` exits 0 in agent-compounds. Check: `./lint.sh; echo "exit=$?"` gives
      `exit=0`.

## Test Scope

- `infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py` (NEW, in the `~/Repos` root repo — a
  DIFFERENT repo from agent-compounds; `infrastructure/dream-cycle/decay_lint.py` is the
  model to follow, verified present at HEAD)
- `skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md` — append check 14 after check 13. Check 12 is at
  lines 82-98 and check 13 at lines 100-110; both are the pattern to MIRROR, not to edit.
  The `## Ouroboros guard` heading at line 112 is the insertion boundary.
- `skills/dream/SKILL.md` only if the check list is enumerated there (verify before editing)
- Data under test: `~/.claude/logs/activity.db` table `skill_reads` (live, read-only) plus a
  synthetic fixture DB for the RED leg
- Verification: the two runs above (live -> zero emissions; fixture -> exactly one), plus
  `./lint.sh` exit 0
- Seam note: the seam is the telemetry WRITER (whatever logs `skill_reads`) <-> this READER.
  The live-DB run exercises the real writer's output shape (including the odd `/x/...` path
  root); the fixture run exercises the reader's logic. Neither alone covers the seam — run
  both, and if the live run cannot parse a real row, that is a finding, not a pass.

## Delivers

- `infrastructure/dream-cycle/skill_uptake_lint.py` (root repo) — the self-arming,
  emit-only skill-uptake decay script
- dream check 14 (skill-uptake decay) in `skills/dream/references/lint-checks.md`
  (agent-compounds), pointing at that script, with the self-arming predicate, emit-only
  human-gated proposals, and the WORKER model-generation re-ablation trigger

## Consumes

- none. `skill_reads` is live infrastructure, not a bead deliverable — there is no upstream
  bead to depend on, so the maturity precondition is enforced INSIDE the check (the
  self-arming predicate above) rather than as a dep edge. This bead is implementable now:
  what it ships is a check that correctly declines to fire until the data matures.

## Approach (advisory)

**Reference-file granularity is DEFERRED, deliberately.** `skill_reads.path` does record
which reference file was read, and ranking reference files for extraction is the natural
next step (it is what ac-znk.3's altitude sweep would consume). It is excluded from this
bead's binding scope because the arming predicate would need its own denominator — the
count of reference files across the registry, which is a different and larger corpus than
the 58 skills — and neither AC below tests it. Adding an untested second granularity is how
a check ships looking complete and firing wrong. File it as a follow-on once check 14 has
armed at skill level and produced one real batch.

title: ac-land teardown: uninstall_precommit_guard + tracked-hook integrity check (decision ac-4an)
description:
Implement decision `ac-4an` (Craig 2026-07-20; full memo + evidence on that bead) in
`skills/ac-land/SKILL.md` § `### Teardown (operational — part of landing)`.

Two additions:
1. **Step 2 addition** — if a mcp-agent-mail pre-commit guard was installed for this session's
   project, call `uninstall_precommit_guard(code_repo_path)` during teardown.
2. **Tracked-hook integrity check** — verify the agent-mail chain-runner left the repo's own
   TRACKED git hooks unmodified; restore if not. Pairs with step 3's tree-cleanliness rule.

**REFINED 2026-08-03 — the blocking "VERIFY LIVE FIRST" AC is DISCHARGED and the install
mechanism is traced. Read both sections below before editing.**

## Live verification (executed 2026-08-03) — AC #1 is ANSWERED

`uninstall_precommit_guard` was called twice against
`/Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/neometa/software/agent-compounds`:

- with a guard installed → `{"removed": true}`
- called again with no guard present → `{"removed": false}` — **a clean no-op: it returns a
  boolean, does not error, and needs no guard-present precondition.**

**What this licenses:** the skill text needs no defensive error handling and no "does a guard
exist?" probe before calling. Record `removed:false` as the benign "nothing was installed" result.

**What this does NOT license — read this before simplifying:** idempotence is not
concurrency-safety. `install_precommit_guard` is **repo-scoped, not session-scoped**
(`skills/ac-implement/SKILL.md` § Install Pre-Commit Guard: "Idempotent — safe to re-run every
session… blocks commits to files reserved by another agent"), and `ac-land/SKILL.md` itself
documents that **two `ac-loop` runs can overlap in time in the same checkout** (§ Concurrency-safe,
two-tier teardown). So an unconditional uninstall at ONE session's teardown strips the
cross-agent commit guard out from under every other session still working that repo. An earlier
draft of this bead proposed dropping the conditional on the strength of the idempotence probe;
that was wrong, and the reasoning error (idempotent ⇒ safe to call unconditionally) is worth
naming in the skill text so it is not repeated.

### The condition must be HARM-SCOPED, not session-scoped — this is the rule to write

`ac-4an`'s phrasing ("if a guard was installed for this session's project") cannot be
implemented as written: **neither tool carries any session or agent identity.** Both are pure
`(project_key, code_repo_path)` calls, `uninstall_precommit_guard` returns only `{"removed": …}`,
and `ac-implement` installs unconditionally at every session's Phase 1 — so "did THIS session
install it" is trivially true for essentially every land session and gates nothing. The
`AGENT_MAIL_ROSTER` teardown already holds only covers this run's own children, not a sibling
overlapping `ac-loop` run, which is precisely the case ac-land's concurrency doctrine warns about.

Write the condition against the HARM instead, which is checkable with two read-only git commands
and is exactly where `ac-4an`'s four collisions occurred:

> Uninstall the guard during teardown **only when the repo's hooks are TRACKED** — i.e. when
> `git config core.hooksPath` names a directory whose `pre-commit` appears in `git ls-files`.
> That is the only configuration in which the chain-runner dirties the working tree, which is the
> harm `ac-4an` was filed to stop. Everywhere else the guard lives in the untracked gitdir hooks
> directory, is invisible to the tree, and must be LEFT IN PLACE.

The asymmetry is what makes this the right default rather than a judgement call: leaving the
guard installed costs nothing (`ac-implement` re-installs it every session anyway, idempotently),
whereas removing one while a sibling session is still committing strips that session's protection.
Fail safe toward leaving it. Run the tracked-hook integrity restore **unconditionally** — it is
read-only unless something is actually modified.

Cost evidence that this is not theoretical: during RUN 20260803-113231-34132 a sub-agent called
`uninstall_precommit_guard` against this shared repo while sibling sessions were live; the guard
was removed and had to be reinstalled
(`install_precommit_guard(project_key="neometa/agent-compounds", code_repo_path=<repo root>)`),
after which the tree was verified clean.

**Do not re-run this probe against a shared working repo.** To re-verify, use a throwaway repo:
`cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q` and call the tool on that path.

## Mechanism the integrity check must handle (traced this run — it is repo-shape-dependent)

`install_precommit_guard` installs a chain-runner whose LOCATION depends on `core.hooksPath`:

- **`core.hooksPath` unset** (e.g. `agent-compounds`, which is a git SUBMODULE): the guard lands
  in the gitdir hooks directory — here
  `/Users/craigvanheerden/Repos/.git/modules/neometa/software/agent-compounds/hooks/pre-commit`.
  Nothing tracked is touched, so the working tree stays clean.
- **`core.hooksPath` points at a TRACKED directory** (e.g. `vitest-affected`, where
  `git config core.hooksPath` = `.githooks` and `git ls-files` lists `.githooks/pre-commit`): the
  guard chain-wraps the repo's OWN TRACKED hook, which **dirties the working tree**. This is the
  mechanism behind all four collisions `ac-4an` cites (two blocked `git pull --rebase` calls, one
  out-of-scope revert, one manual hand-restore).

Two consequences for the skill text:
- The integrity check must resolve the hooks directory with `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, or
  honour `core.hooksPath` — **never assume `.git/hooks/`**, which does not even resolve in a
  submodule (`.git` is a file there).
- The check only bites in repos whose hooks are tracked; say so, so agents in the common case do
  not hunt for a modification that cannot exist.
- **Say restore FROM WHAT.** `ac-4an` says "restore if not" without naming a source, and no
  snapshot step exists anywhere in the pipeline to restore from. Since the file in question is

per-skill headroom tables. NONE of them modelled limit (2). The epic's method — "every
precision/recall failure gets a description: edit", applied across 52 skills — is
structurally a registry-wide growth program, so the aggregate was always going to be the
binding constraint, not any single description.

B6 (+971 chars), B7 (+1391) and B8 (+1187 before correction) took the registry from roughly
27,484 to 31,033. Check 13 went RED on the aggregate while every individual description was
comfortably under 1024. B8 absorbed it inside its own family per the beads' net-neutral

every trigger token and every named destination preserved), family 7,268 -> 7,040 = net -228
while ADDING 8 exclusion clauses. Registry closed at 29,618/30,000.

ANY skill turns lint red, and the failure surfaces as a whole-registry Check 13 FAIL with no
pointer to the skill that caused it. The three plausible dispositions are all decisions, not
mechanics:

- pay for every future clause by tightening elsewhere (current de-facto policy, undocumented);
- raise `skillListingBudgetFraction` and `BUDGET_FAIL` together, deliberately (the script's

- flip low-inbound entry points to `disable-model-invocation: true`, which the script already

  (`skill-builder` — its SKILL.md already owns "optimizing description/token cost"), stating

The B2-B8 trigger passes moved the registry's model-invocable description total from 27163 to 29618 chars against `validate-skill.sh --registry`'s hard `BUDGET_FAIL=30000` — 86.5% of the pre-batch headroom consumed in one batch, and `lint.sh` already emits its WARNING. Note the coupling: bead 'audit description dropped its test-quality trigger' wants ~22 chars BACK, so recall repairs and budget compete. Resolve the budget policy first.

- `validate-skill.sh --registry` reports headroom consistent with that policy.

title: test-quality reviewer isolation: a probe worktree shares stash storage with the shared repo
description:
discovered-from: unknown

Recorded per ac-review Phase 3's reviewer-leakage rule. This run's test-quality reviewer followed its documented isolation discipline (git worktree add into a tmpdir, probe there, git worktree remove --force) but used a scoped 'git stash push' INSIDE the worktree to discard its sabotage edits. Worktrees share .git/refs with the parent, so the stashes landed in the SHARED repo: two inert entries 'WIP on (no branch): ef44c26' remain at stash@{0}/stash@{1} in agent-compounds. No tracked-file impact; the review did not drop them because dropping is a mutation the ceremony is not licensed to make.

The doctrine gap is real: review-dimensions.md section test-quality prescribes the worktree AND the environment contract prescribes scoped 'git stash push' as the discard shape, and the two combine into shared-repo pollution. A 'cp -R' copy avoids the stash issue but breaks git-dependent harnesses here (agent-compounds is a submodule, so a copied .git file points at an unreachable modules path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- review-dimensions.md section test-quality names the discard shape that IS safe from a probe worktree (scoped checkout inside the worktree, or worktree remove --force as the only discard) and forbids 'git stash' from a worktree.
- The same correction lands wherever the sabotage-in-a-worktree discipline is restated (grep 'git worktree add' across skills/ and fix every carrier).
- Craig drops stash@{0} and stash@{1} in agent-compounds, or confirms they may stay.

## Test Scope

- skills/ac-review/references/review-dimensions.md, the 'Isolation discipline' paragraph (grep-verified present).
- skills/ac-hygiene/references/reviewers.md — check for the same restatement before editing.
- No user-facing surface; no QA modality.

title: ac-bead-refine workflow.md Phase 0 mandates TaskCreate with no fallback — 5th+ child rediscovery after ac-qsz fixed the canon
description:
Loop-retro finding, RUN 20260803-221658-19787 (run 2). 5th+ independent rediscovery.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Spawn any ac-bead-refine child as a subagent (the normal pipeline shape).
2. Child reads skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md line 22: "MANDATORY FIRST STEP: declare the run ledger ... with TaskCreate BEFORE starting."
3. Child has no TaskCreate/TaskUpdate tool in its harness context.
4. Child burns turns discovering this, then improvises progress.md as the ledger.

## Context
ac-qsz already fixed the CANON: skills/ac-pipeline/references/run-ledger.md line 15 now
carries the file-ledger fallback ("No Task tools in your context? ... The ledger is then a
FILE: keep it as progress.md"). The fix did NOT reach the citing call site. workflow.md
line 22 states the mandate in imperative voice, names TaskCreate as the mechanism, and
cites run-ledger.md only as a parenthetical for the one-task-per-section contract, so a
child obeying the mandate never learns the fallback exists before it fails.

Four children hit it in THIS run alone (TopazHawkRefineA, B, C, and one more), each
reporting it as a fresh discovery; ac-qsz records 6 rediscoveries in the prior run.
Per-instance cost is small (minutes) but the recurrence is the defect: a canon fix that
does not propagate to its mandating call sites is not a fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. workflow.md Phase 0 names the file-ledger fallback inline (or makes the run-ledger.md
   citation unmistakably the authority for the MECHANISM, not just the contract) so a
   child with no Task tools resolves it without a failed attempt.
2. Every other ac-* skill that mandates TaskCreate in a CHILD-executed phase is swept for
   the same gap; grep the registry for TaskCreate and check each site's executor
   (conductor vs child). Sites executed only by a conductor need no change.
3. The fix is executed at draft: a probe confirms a reader arriving at the mandate reaches
   the fallback text without following an unmarked pointer.

## Test Scope
- skills/ac-bead-refine/references/workflow.md (Phase 0, line ~22)
- skills/ac-pipeline/references/run-ledger.md (The pattern section)
- grep sweep: TaskCreate across skills/

title: Bare tr still bites at reflex level despite in-brief warnings — silent empty-capture needs a mechanical guard, not prose (ac-e5a3 follow-on)
description:
Loop-retro finding, RUN 20260803-221658-19787 (run 2). 3rd+ occurrence in ONE run.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In this zsh environment, tr is aliased (tr to tmux) so a bare tr invocation does not run
   coreutils tr.
2. An agent writes a bare tr inside a command substitution, e.g. a pipeline that squeezes
   or deletes characters while counting bead IDs.
3. The substitution yields an EMPTY string. Downstream arithmetic reads it as 0.
4. No error is raised. The command exits 0. The wrong answer is silently accepted.

## Context
ac-e5a3 fixed this at the SNIPPET level: every bare tr in agent-pasted skill snippets was
converted to command tr (8 invocations / 7 lines / 4 files). That fix holds. The residual
defect is different and is what recurred here: agents write their OWN shell, and the trap
is reflex-level, not knowledge-level.

Evidence from this run: TopazHawkRefineE hit it with the route-around explicitly present in
its brief. TopazHawkRefineF hit it AGAIN, also with the explicit warning in its own brief,
and reported: "The warning does not inoculate; reflex-level." One of the two produced a
silent wrong result (an empty capture reading as zero hits) before it was caught.

Cost class: false-NEGATIVE generator. A zero-hit read is the most dangerous failure shape
in this pipeline because it looks like a clean pass and terminates a search early.

The claim being made here is that prose is the wrong instrument. The fix should be
MECHANICAL. Candidate shapes to evaluate (this bead does not pre-pick one):
- a shell function or PATH shim exported into agent shells so bare tr resolves to coreutils
- an unalias in the agent shell initialization
- a dcg-style guard that flags a bare tr in a command substitution before it runs
- a lint check over skill files plus a session-preamble line, if the mechanical routes are
  rejected for environment reasons

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A bare tr written by an agent in this environment either resolves to coreutils tr, or is
   blocked or flagged before it can return an empty capture. Prose-only is insufficient and
   does not close this bead.
2. RED demonstration: a probe reproduces the empty-capture-reads-as-zero failure under the
   pre-fix condition, in zsh (the shell that has the alias), not under bash.
3. GREEN demonstration: the same probe returns the correct count after the fix.
4. The chosen mechanism does not require every child prompt to carry a warning line; if the
   warning line is kept, it is belt-and-suspenders, not the mechanism.

## Test Scope
- shell environment: the tr alias resolution path used by agent Bash calls
- probe must run under zsh (a bash harness cannot demonstrate a zsh-only defect —
  independent lesson from TopazHawkImplA this run)
- prior art: ac-e5a3 (snippet-level fix, closed)

## Delivers
- config: a mechanical guarantee that bare tr does not silently no-op in agent shells

## Consumes
- none
