title: disposition.md Save-for-later dedupe command is broken — br list --json returns an object, snippet iterates it as a bare array
description:
Loop-retro finding, RUN 20260803-221658-19787 (run 2). Verified live at land time.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the Save-for-later dedupe check exactly as skills/ac-pipeline/references/disposition.md
line 48 prescribes it, from the agent-compounds repo root:

  br list --status=open --json | jq '[.[] | select(.labels | index("skill-improvement"))]'

Observed: jq error, "Cannot index array with string labels".

Root cause: br list --json returns an OBJECT with keys has_more, issues, limit, offset,
total. The snippet iterates it as a bare ARRAY. Correct form is .issues[].

## Context
The shape is genuinely inconsistent across the br surface, which is why this keeps biting:
  br list  --json  returns an object, keyed .issues
  br ready --json  returns a bare array (skills/ac-pipeline/references/board-scan.md line
                   43 documents this correctly)
So both jq shapes are right somewhere, and neither is right everywhere.

Impact is specific and current: this snippet IS the dedupe check that ac-land Phase 3 is
instructed to run before filing a T2 human-gate improvement bead. A silent jq error there
means the dedupe check returns nothing and every land re-files a duplicate. TopazHawkClose
independently reported the same bare-array assumption from the ac-batch-close side this
run (Act 0, ~1 turn).

Correct usages already exist and are the model:
  skills/ac-merge/references/feedback-writeback-hook.md:129 uses .issues[]
  skills/ac-pipeline/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh:329 uses jq .issues

## Acceptance Criteria
1. disposition.md line 48 is corrected to iterate .issues[] and the corrected command runs
   clean (exit 0, no jq error) against the live board.
2. A registry-wide sweep confirms no other skill file pipes br list --json into a bare-array
   jq program. Grep for "br list" with jq on the same line and check each hit.
3. Any hit found is either fixed or shown to be a br ready call (bare array is correct
   there).
4. Executed at draft: the amended command is actually run, not merely inspected.

title: lint.sh Check 14 prescribes only the HTML net-growth-ok stamp form — invalid inside a bash fence, and the substring grep passes it anyway
description:
Loop-retro finding, RUN 20260803-221658-19787 (run 2). Caught as a near-miss by
ac-bead-refine round 4 (TopazHawkRefineB), on 3 beads at once.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. A bead AC or skill edit needs a Check 14 net-growth exemption stamp.
2. The author follows lint.sh:791 verbatim, which prescribes the EXACT token
   as an HTML comment: an angle-bracket-bang-dashes wrapper around net-growth-ok.
3. The text being stamped lands INSIDE a fenced bash block (a shell snippet).
4. The HTML comment wrapper is not a shell comment. The snippet is now a syntax error.
5. lint.sh Check 14 still PASSES, because its detection is a substring grep for the
   literal "net-growth-ok:" and never inspects the surrounding syntax context.

## Context
The gate is deliberately substring-only, and lint.sh:787-789 already documents ONE
near-miss of exactly this family (bd-curate-...xu5tz asked for an "evidence:" comment that
the grep would not see). The mirror-image hazard is undocumented: a form the grep DOES see
but that is invalid in its landing context.

Cost this run: TopazHawkRefineB spent round 4 of 5 catching this as a Critical across three
beads' ACs. Had it shipped, three implement children would each have written a
self-breaking bash fence, and the gate would have reported clean.

Correct forms, by context:
  in prose            HTML comment wrapper (as lint.sh:791 says today)
  inside a bash fence a hash-prefixed shell comment carrying the same literal token
Both satisfy the grep; only one is valid in each context.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. lint.sh's Check 14 fail message (line ~791) and its header comment (lines ~654-668)
   state that the stamp form is CONTEXT-DEPENDENT and give both valid shapes, naming which
   belongs in prose and which inside a fenced code block.
2. The message keeps its existing warning that non-"net-growth-ok:" wordings do not count —
   this bead adds the second half, it does not replace the first.
3. Executed at draft: both stamp forms are actually run through Check 14 in a scratch
   probe and both are shown to PASS the grep; the bash-fence form is additionally shown to
   parse as valid shell while the HTML form is shown not to.

title: DECISION: centralize the child-prompt environment route-around block into a shared reference (pasted 8x this run, 5 new guard shapes never propagated)
description:
decision: should the environment route-around block that child prompts paste inline become
a single owner-hosted reference file that prompts cite, with the inline copies demoted?

options:
  a) adopt the reference file, prompts keep a 2-3 shape inline core plus a pointer — fixes
     drift and the 8x duplication, still gives a blocked child something to read without a
     file hop; costs one new reference and a demotion sweep across the paste sites
  b) adopt the reference file, prompts carry a pointer ONLY — maximal dedup and the
     smallest per-child token cost, but a child that is already blocked must spend a turn
     reading a file before it can unblock
  c) keep the inline prose as-is — zero change cost, but every newly-discovered guard shape
     keeps reaching only the prompts written after it, and this run discovered five that
     the pasted block does not contain

context:

**Target:** a new shared reference under skills/ac-pipeline/references/ (working name
environment-route-arounds.md), cited by the child-spawn preamble in
skills/ac-pipeline/references/delegation-contract.md and by every skill that pastes it.

**Evidence (RUN 20260803-221658-19787, run 2).** The conductor pasted the same block of
environment route-arounds into 8 separate child prompts this session (refine A-F, implement
lanes, review, close). The block is prose: dcg parses certain characters inside quoted
argument text as redirects; bare tr is aliased; git checkout with two dashes is blocked; use
tee rather than a redirect operator; and so on. Two costs, both measured this run.

1. DUPLICATION. 8 hand-maintained copies, no single source, so a newly-discovered
   route-around reaches only prompts written after it. This session discovered at least five
   NEW dcg shapes: the literal token "restore" inside a shell function name; a word-count
   redirect reading from a variable; an arrow sequence inside quoted argument text;
   angle-bracket placeholders inside a bead description; a stderr redirect inside a command
   substitution. None of them appear in the block that was pasted 8 times.

2. INEFFICACY. Route-arounds that WERE in the pasted block still did not take. Two children
   (TopazHawkRefineE, TopazHawkRefineF) hit the bare-tr trap with the warning present in
   their own briefs; F reported that the warning does not inoculate. Aggregate across the
   run: roughly 20-25 minutes of blocked turns and retries attributable to guard shapes,
   plus one silent wrong result.

**Explicit non-claim.** This fixes duplication and drift. It does NOT claim to fix
inefficacy — the bare-tr recurrence is evidence that prose does not inoculate at all, and
that half needs a mechanical guard. That is filed separately as ac-54t8.2 and is not
superseded by this decision.

**Supersession.** If adopted, the inline prose blocks in the citing skills are DEMOTED to
pointers, not left in place alongside the new file. Removal of the duplicated content is
part of the change, not an optional follow-up (promotion-ladder: removal ranks equally with
addition). Any line found in only one paste site moves to the reference first. Precedent
for the shape: the child-spawn preamble mirror already enforced by lint Check 16.

**Recommendation:** option (a).

## Delivers
- decision: adopt or reject a shared environment-route-arounds reference for child prompts
